speaker: A Greater Cause
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ratonhnhaké:ton's genetic memories stored in the Abstergo Cloud and relived by an Assassin hacker in 2023 through the Animus.

speaker: Warren
en: Animals! Stop!

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Take what you deserve, rebel.

speaker: Prudence
en: Please?! Stop!!

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Shut that whore up.

speaker: Soldier
en: You've been warned. You asked for it.

speaker: Connor
en: What happened?

speaker: Prudence
en: They demanded we give our entire yield to the crown. Warren refused. They killed our animals, salted our earth then dragged us out. You saw what followed. I'm afraid we have nothing to give you in thanks, stranger- we have nothing left.

speaker: Connor
en: Perhaps there is something you could DO instead.

speaker: Warren
en: Anything.

speaker: Connor
en: I live in a small community not far from here. The soil is rich. The people I live with would have need of fresh vegetables, wheat or corn. If you were to rebuild your farm, you may prosper.

speaker: Prudence
en: What kindness is this? We'll certainly come see. Thank you.

speaker: Hunter
en: There's a valley nearby that's used in Kanien'kehá:ka rite of passage ceremonies. I been told there's a cougar that's staked his claim on the area and been the cause of a few too many accidents for the young'uns. Might do some good to put an end to it. Probably get a damn nice pelt out of it while you're at it.

speaker: Connor
en: I have been reunited with my father, but do not yet know if this bodes well or ill. Our goals are aligned, at least so far as independence is concerned. But he continues to defend Charles Lee—the man who murdered my mother and burned my village... Still, he makes a point about Washington and those who back him. I hear much talk of freedom and equality, but it seems one must be a landed white man to benefit. What of someone like me? Or Surry? What role for us in this new world? Is my father right, then? There is so much I must consider and so little time in which to do it.

speaker: Achilles
en: Welcome back. And how was Martinique?

speaker: Connor
en: Achilles... I... I owe you an apology... It was wrong of me to say the things I did...

speaker: Achilles
en: Your words were harsh, Connor, but there was also truth there. I failed the Order. Allowed the Templars to take control...

speaker: Connor
en: But now their hold is weakened, which makes me believe there's a chance for peace. Imagine what might be accomplished if we were to unite.

speaker: Achilles
en: Why the change of heart? Where is this coming from? You've met your father, haven't you?

speaker: Connor
en: I do not claim to trust the man—or even like him. But I would be remiss to ignore this opportunity.

speaker: Achilles
en: Haytham may listen. But will he understand? And even if he does, will he agree?

speaker: Connor
en: Even he must admit that we achieve more together than we do alone.

speaker: Achilles
en: I assume you're off to find him?

speaker: Connor
en: Yes. I ride for New York to see what might be done.

speaker: Haytham
en: We need to know what the Loyalists are planning if we're to put and end to this.

speaker: Twitch
en: I've tried! But the soldiers themselves are told nothing now—only to await orders from above.

speaker: Haytham
en: Then keep digging. Come find me when you have something worth sharing.

speaker: Haytham
en: We're so close to victory. A few more well-placed attacks and we'll be able to put an end to this civil war and be rid of the Crown.

speaker: Connor
en: What do you intend?

speaker: Haytham
en: Well nothing at the moment—since we're completely in the dark.

speaker: Connor
en: I thought the Templars had eyes and ears everywhere.

speaker: Haytham
en: Oh, we did. Until you started cutting them off.

speaker: Connor
en: Your contact said orders from above. It tells us exactly what we need to do: track down the Loyalist commanders.

speaker: Officer
en: Have you considered the proposal?

speaker: Officer
en: I'm unconvinced. To reinforce them would leave New York exposed. It's hard enough maintaining order with our current numbers. Cut in half...

speaker: Officer
en: Yet if we do not join with them, they risk defeat. And then what?

speaker: Officer
en: Well they should have come by sea...

speaker: Haytham
en: They're talking in circles. We'll learn nothing, watching as we are.

speaker: Connor
en: Then what do you propose we do? March in there and demand answers?

speaker: Haytham
en: Well, yes.

speaker: Officer
en: Ambush!

speaker: Haytham
en: Connor! A little help, here?

speaker: Haytham
en: We'll bring them to my quarters at Fort George and see what secrets they might share.

speaker: Haytham
en: Really? Well you'd best get after him, then.

speaker: Connor
en: You go. I will watch the prisoners.

speaker: Haytham
en: No, you do it.

speaker: Connor
en: Why me?

speaker: Haytham
en: Because I said so! Now go!

speaker: Officer
en: Help! I need help! Come no closer! Stop him! To arms, men! To arms! Save me! Keep him away from me!

speaker: Connor
en: Move.

speaker: Officer
en: Go to hell.

speaker: Connor
en: I said MOVE.

speaker: Officer
en: Wait, wait! I'll tell you anything you want. Anything! Only don't make me go in there!

speaker: Connor
en: We just have some questions for you.

speaker: Officer
en: Cross that threshold and I'm a dead man!

speaker: Haytham
en: There you are, Connor! I was worried you might have gotten lost... Come along, then!

speaker: Haytham
en: What are the British planning?

speaker: Officer
en: To march from Philadelphia. That city's finished. New York's the key. They'll double our numbers—push back the rebels.

speaker: Haytham
en: When do they begin?

speaker: Officer
en: Two days from now.

speaker: Connor
en: June 18th... I must warn Washington.

speaker: Haytham
en: You see? That wasn't so very difficult, now was it?

speaker: Officer
en: I've t-told you everything! Now l-let me go!

speaker: Haytham
en: Of course.

speaker: Haytham
en: The other two said the same. It must be true.

speaker: Connor
en: You killed him... You killed ALL of them. Why?

speaker: Haytham
en: They'd have warned the Loyalists.

speaker: Connor
en: You could have held them until the fight was done.

speaker: Haytham
en: What? ... And waste precious time and money on their care? What would be the point? They'd given up everything they knew. I'll meet you at Valley Forge.

speaker: Connor
en: Stephane, what is wrong? Where is Sam Adams?

speaker: Stephane
en: Who cares! I've been robbed! Ils vont me le payer ces scélérats de merde... (Those pieces of shit are going to pay for this...)

speaker: Connor
en: Where are you going?!

speaker: Stephane
en: To get back what's rightfully mine! Oh! Regardez! (Look!) Some pathetic Redcoats waiting for a beating! I will match your face to your jacket, crapule! (Bastard!)

speaker: Stephane
en: Ces Coquins me prennent mon père au Canada et voilà qu'ils me ravissent ma propriete ici. Il suffit! (The dirty bastards take my father from me in Canada and now they take my property in Boston. I've had enough!) We are not English! We are not the King's men! We are free! But the King sends these REDCOATS to push us around! They are not our masters! This is our city! Let's show them who owns it! It's time to fight!

speaker: Connor
en: Stephane. Please. Stop and listen to me.

speaker: Stephane
en: I've listened for long enough! They come into MY home and take MY things? I will get my revenge. The man responsible for this will pay. His friends will pay! Voilà trop longtemps que je subis ces affronts! Ils vont goûter de mon courroux! (For too long I've suffered these indignities! They will taste my wrath!) You looking for a fight, Englishmen!? I'll give you what you want!

speaker: Stephane
en: Où que j'aille, l'Anglais croise mon chemin. Ils me volent ma maison, ils m'obligent à fuir mon pays. Et les voici qui veulent s'approprier ma NOUVELLE demeure! (I cannot escape the English, no matter where I go. They kick me out of my home, I come here. Now they want to take my NEW home!)

speaker: Connor
en: There is a way to fight injustice! But THIS is not it!

speaker: Taxman
en: Destroyed!? You stupid mongrel. And I suppose you want me to tell Johnson his tea just spontaneously combusted! Nonsense! Someone's responsible for this and you will find out who. And if you can't, I'll gut you and find a smarter mongrel who can.

speaker: Stephane
en: What do we do?

speaker: Connor
en: Create a window.

speaker: Taxman
en: Who the bloody hell are you?!

speaker: Taxman
en: W-why?

speaker: Stephane
en: You have no right to rob people blind. By decree of the British Parliament or not.

speaker: Taxman
en: British Parliament? I work for William Johnson.

speaker: Stephane
en: Johnson?

speaker: Connor
en: End his suffering cleanly.

speaker: Taxman
en: Please...

speaker: Connor
en: The people seem to have an ear for you. What of the things you lost?

speaker: Stephane
en: The people listened to me only because I spoke the truth loud enough, which is worth one thousand times the contents of my footlocker. The English, they can keep my THINGS.

speaker: Connor
en: You did well tonight.

speaker: Stephane
en: I said I'd buy you an ale when you first helped me. In place of drink I offer you my allegiance, for what it's worth.

speaker: Connor
en: Your aid is welcome and I am grateful. Now, I need to find Sam Adams.

speaker: Franklin
en: This should get us close to Washington. By heavens, what happened?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Boston Neck was a trap set by Putnam.

speaker: Franklin
en: And Adams? ... Kanen'tó:kon?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Everyone killed.

speaker: Franklin
en: Killed? We'll be next! We've got to get out of here!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: The land routes are cut off. We must escape by sea.

speaker: Franklin
en: Yes! By sea! I know of an excellent ship, but I'm too well known to move about freely.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I will find you a disguise.

speaker: Franklin
en: Excellent idea. In the meanwhile, give me the diagram. I'll file this metal to precision.

speaker: Franklin
en: Hm. Bit of a tight fit, you know. How do I look?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Ridiculous.

speaker: Franklin
en: You don't have to be so honest.

speaker: Franklin
en: Oh, dear. Trouble ahead.

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: Look! Here is one of us!

speaker: Bluecoat 2
en: Come along, we're headed to the tavern. You can buy us a mug of flip!

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: They tossed us out of the last one. Not a very friendly bunch.

speaker: Bluecoat 2
en: Wassa matter? We're not good enough for ya!?

speaker: Bluecoat 3
en: Hold on there, corporal!

speaker: Franklin
en: Yes, sir.

speaker: Bluecoat 3
en: That uniform doesn't really fit you, does it?

speaker: Franklin
en: I've uh, I've gained a few pounds is all.

speaker: Bluecoat 3
en: Have you, now?

speaker: Franklin
en: Too many popovers, you see? With butter. And ale.

speaker: Bluecoat 3
en: That's not your uniform at all, is it?

speaker: Franklin
en: I'm going to need some help here.

speaker: Franklin
en: Whew! That was close!

speaker: Bluecoat 4
en: You there! Soldier! Stop!

speaker: Bluecoat 5
en: What business have you in this district?

speaker: Franklin
en: Why, I, um.

speaker: Bluecoat 5
en: What corps are you with?

speaker: Franklin
en: I'm, uh ... I'm assigned directly to General Putnam! Personal detail.

speaker: Bluecoat 4
en: Likely story. Let's see your papers, Corporal Personal Detail.

speaker: Franklin
en: I've just been assigned. My papers are still in process.

speaker: Bluecoat 5
en: All right, that's it! Come on! To the hoosegow!

speaker: Franklin
en: I'm going to need some help here.

speaker: Franklin
en: Thanks for taking care of that.

speaker: Franklin
en: Mister Faulkner! Sir!

speaker: Faulkner
en: Who's that? Do I ...? Franklin!?

speaker: Franklin
en: Don't let the disguise fool you.

speaker: Faulkner
en: You goddamn ...! Your men stole my ship, you shite!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Easy, Mr. Faulkner. Mr. Franklin is on the side of the rebels, now.

speaker: Franklin
en: We need your help.

speaker: Faulkner
en: And why should I?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: You'll get your ship back.

speaker: Faulkner
en: Ah! ... The goddamn wharf's too heavily guarded.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I can change that, if you'll tell me what needs to be done.

speaker: Faulkner
en: Well, let's see. I'll need you to untie the Aquila so it's all set to go. Meantime, I can scare you up a small crew.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Then we'll rush the guards and set sail.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Ratonhnhaké:ton. Ratonhnhaké:ton, wake up.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Ratonhnhaké:ton. Rise. We must go.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Mother! What are you doing here?

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Are you still dreaming? We came here together. Now we must go.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I thought... I thought I lost you. But you're here.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: I am here. I have always been here. Are you alright?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Better than alright.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Good. Now come, I have heard screaming in close by. We must learn what's going on.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: This could be all my fault!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What is your fault? What have you done?

speaker: Bluecoat
en: Are you the one?! Thief! You tried to steal the source of his power! The King said to find a Mohawk girl with braids. You're a Mohawk. And you have braids.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: On the right! I'll get the one on the left. She's not the one you want!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Why has Washington sent his men to raid the Frontier?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Washington?

speaker: Bluecoat
en: To find somebody—a native woman who tried to take it from him.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: He will not find me by you.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What could Washington have to do with this? He is no longer Commander-In-Chief, he retired to Mount Vernon.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: A lovely fantasy, Ratonhnhaké:ton, you know Washington went mad with power long ago. I tried to stop him but failed. And now I've brought down his wrath upon my own people.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I don't understand. None of it fits. Are we

speaker: Tribeswoman
en: King Washington's men are raiding Concord right now, murdering everyone. They're looking for you Kaniehtí:io!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: KING Washington?

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Come.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: I never imagined he would strike out so recklessly.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Are you talking about Commander Washington? Why did that woman call him King?

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Many innocent people are suffering because of me. Not only the villagers. We must protect as many as we can.

speaker: Bluecoat
en: Only tell us where she is and these people live. Refuse and they burn. It's really quite simple.

speaker: Townsman
en: We don't know who you want!

speaker: Bluecoat
en: Very well.

speaker: Townsman
en: Please! Please! There are women and children in there! Are you a monster?! Do not do this!

speaker: Bluecoat
en: You had your chance.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Do it quietly! Don't let them see you. Take them by surprise!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Free them! This is all because of me.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Get as far away from town as possible! Find shelter in the forest!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Ratonhnhaké:ton!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: There!

speaker: Bluecoat
en: Fire!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Ratonhnhaké:ton! We must move swiftly! Make haste! What are you doing?! Hurry! I won't forgive myself if we don't stop them!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: This is madness! I cannot understand what is going on!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: You! I need your help! Help me load the cannon!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: The King's army is advancing! Use this gun to stop them!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: They are retreating! We have done it!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Washington's troops do not retreat—they advance or die. To Lexington, we will have a better vantage point from there. If I had only succeeded in taking the scepter. Now I must make amends.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Scepter? Mother, this all becomes more and more difficult to understand.

speaker: Washington
en: There she is! The savage that tried to steal this, the source and symbol of my power! Gaze upon it! For it will be the last object you will ever see!

speaker: Washington
en: I come here to destroy both you and your sad village, for none like you will be allowed to live.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Commander Washington! Why are you doing this? After all we accomplished! Take hold of your senses!

speaker: Washington
en: Another delusional savage. I have never had such a firm grasp on my senses. Now bend your knee to your monarch, and make penitence in the last moments before you are blasted to your dread reward. Corporal! Take care of them.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Ratonhnhaké:ton! A Bluecoat over there! Stop them from setting off the powder kegs! Kill anyone trying to light the fuses! Here comes another one! There! We must stop them! Stop him! He's almost there!

speaker: Putnam
en: The enemy advances and you tremble. They've better numbers, you say. Better weapons. Better training. But I do not fear, and neither should you. For what they have in material, they lack in conviction and care. But not us. We have discipline. We have order. And most importantly, we have passion. We believe! So maintain vigilance. Conserve your ammo. Ensure a proper line of sight. And above all else, men, do not fire until you see the whites of their eyes.

speaker: Putnam
en: Well I'll be damned. You did it.

speaker: Connor
en: That was quite a speech.

speaker: Putnam
en: Lies, all of it, I'm afraid. Still, such words have carried us thus far...

speaker: Connor
en: And what of Pitcairn?

speaker: Putnam
en: He's left Boston as I said he would, and set up camp on Moulton Hill. There's no good way to get at him – not with that maelstrom brewing down below. I suppose you could circle around a bit, or wait for us to thin their ranks.

speaker: Connor
en: There is no time. I will have to chance direct approach.

speaker: Putnam
en: That's twice today you've proposed the impossible!

speaker: Connor
en: I see no other choice.

speaker: Putnam
en: That's cos you're mad as a march hare, son.

speaker: Connor
en: I expect an apology on my return.

speaker: Pitcairn
en: It seems we are well and truly at war... A pity, that. For it's a war we did not ask for. A war we did not wish... And why would we? We're killing our brothers down there – and for what? Duty? Honor? Liberty and justice as the Yanks claim? No. Clinton, . To me. We must ready the next offensive.

speaker: Pitcairn
en: Why... Why did you do this?

speaker: Connor
en: To protect Adams and Hancock – and those they serve. You meant to kill them–

speaker: Pitcairn
en: Kill them? Are you mad? I wanted only to parley. There was so much to discuss. To explain... But you've put an end to that now.

speaker: Connor
en: If you speak true then I will carry your last words to them.

speaker: Pitcairn
en: They must lay down their arms. They must stop this war!

speaker: Connor
en: Why them and not the Redcoats?

speaker: Pitcairn
en: Do you not think we asked the same question of the British? These things take time. And it would have succeeded, had you let me play my part.

speaker: Connor
en: The part of the puppeteer.

speaker: Pitcairn
en: Better we hold the strings than another.

speaker: Connor
en: No. The strings should be severed. All should be free.

speaker: Pitcairn
en: And we should live forever on castles in the sky. You wield your blade like a man, but your mouth like a child. And more will die now because of that...

speaker: Connor
en: It is better to have faith in something, than none at all...

speaker: Putnam
en: How dare you sneak up on me like that! Why don't you just go off there and just help this camp retreat! Don't ever do that again you hear me! God Damnit.

speaker: Connor
en: General Putnam.

speaker: Putnam
en: You live!

speaker: Connor
en: The same cannot be said for Pitcairn.

speaker: Putnam
en: Well done, I suppose. But it matters little now. I'm ordering a full retreat. We have lost too many in exchange for too little. If the Tories want this hill so badly, let them have it. Boston is the true prize.

speaker: Connor
en: We have a bigger problem.

speaker: Putnam
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Putnam
en: This can't be right. It says they plan to murder Washington!

speaker: Lafayette
en: We must hold this position for as long as it takes! If the enemy is allowed to push through, we will lose what precious little ground we've gained. The sacrifices your brothers have made today must not have been in vain! Now go! Bring the fight to our enemy! Make them rue the day they marched upon us!

speaker: Lafayette
en: Connor, my friend! You have arrived just in time to bear witness to our glorious victory!

speaker: Connor
en: Where is Charles Lee?

speaker: Lafayette
en: That batard (bastard). He shows up in the middle of our preparations and just takes charge. Screams at everyone to advance and then rides away. I am left to pick up the pieces. Where did THEY come from? Send word that we are falling back. Everyone to me! Now! Now!

speaker: Connor
en: I will hold the area while you bring them to safety.

speaker: Lafayette
en: I grant you my finest soldiers to serve as your personal guard. There is nothing they will not do to ensure you are victorious. Bonne chance, mon ami. (Good luck, my friend.)

speaker: Soldier
en: We are low on ammunition, sir - and the enemy advances.

speaker: Connor
en: Then we need to pull back, rejoin the others, and cover their escape.

speaker: Soldier
en: If we tarry - we'll die. Best we go!

speaker: Soldier
en: We've done all we can. We must retreat!

speaker: Soldier
en: Come on men, we must fall back!

speaker: Lafayette
en: Well done, my friend! You have saved many lives today.

speaker: George
en: Connor?

speaker: Connor
en: Charles Lee has betrayed you. He forced retreat in the midst of battle - hoping the loss would take the lives of your men and see you relieved of your command.

speaker: George
en: What?!

speaker: Connor
en: I am sure he will come and spin a tale - saying he was outnumbered - or I was somehow to blame. All lies. I will say it one last time - that man is your enemy and he will not stop until you are dead or dishonored.

speaker: Lafayette
en: Connor's tale rings true. Lee was acting most odd upon the battlefield.

speaker: George
en: I will investigate these allegations at once.

speaker: Connor
en: The time for that is long past.

speaker: George
en: This must be done properly, else we're no better than those we oppose. Never mind the political ramifications of such an act.

speaker: Connor
en: Should you choose to spare Lee's life then I will take it myself. Enjoy your victory, Commander. It will be the last I deliver you.

speaker: Connor
en: The tides of war are turning. The Loyalists fall back beneath the advancing Patriot army, their hold on this land weakening by the day. But the Templars only seem to grow stronger. Though fewer in number, the threat they pose appears undiminished. Making matters worse, Washington chose to spare the life of Charles Lee. I am told he has taken refuge inside Fort George, and so my days are spent searching for a way to breach its walls. Of my father, there is no trace. And I am glad of it. If I can be rid of Lee, there may still be a chance for reconciliation - and through it, peace.

speaker: Diana
en: Connor? He's asking for you.

speaker: Achilles
en: Hello, Connor. Come now. Your sadness won't sustain me any more than that fool woman's soups and potions... Tell me of your latest exploits.

speaker: Connor
en: Charles Lee has been exposed and the Patriots finally rid of him. They march now to secure the remaining cities that this country might finally be free.

speaker: Achilles
en: Then you have won. The land and your people are safe. Yet you seem troubled...

speaker: Connor
en: Washington spared Lee's life.

speaker: Achilles
en: So long as he lives, all are in danger. The same is true for your father. When you first came to me, you understood what had to be done. Swore you'd see it through. If not for the Brotherhood, for your people - and all those threatened by the Templars.

speaker: Connor
en: But with Lee gone, my father might...

speaker: Achilles
en: Listen to me. You have not come this far to throw it all away over misplaced sentiment. Both men must die.

speaker: Connor
en: Ach... Achilles.

speaker: Achilles
en: There is nothing more to discuss.

speaker: Lafayette
en: Connor! I came as soon as I could.

speaker: Connor
en: Tell me you bring good news?

speaker: Lafayette
en: The Comte de Grasse said yes. You need only join his fleet in Chesapeake Bay and they will serve as required. But what exactly is it you intend?

speaker: Connor
en: It's better that I show you. Charles Lee may have been dismissed, but it does not mean we are safe.

speaker: Lafayette
en: But the Commander

speaker: Connor
en: The Commander underestimates the threat and no more time can be wasted trying to convince him otherwise. I must do this on my own.

speaker: Lafayette
en: Do what, exactly?

speaker: Connor
en: Kill Charles Lee. He hides within Fort George, which is itself, surrounded by a militarized district. I cannot hope to infiltrate it directly - so I will go under instead.

speaker: Lafayette
en: Incroyable. (Incredible.)

speaker: Connor
en: The tunnels leading to the fort have been filled in. While I secure the Admiral's ships, I need you to clear them for me.

speaker: Lafayette
en: And the ships?

speaker: Connor
en: When signaled, they will bombard the fort.

speaker: Lafayette
en: Breaching its walls and creating a distraction. I see!

speaker: Connor
en: In the chaos, I will slip inside, find Charles Lee - and silence him forever.

speaker: Connor
en: Ready the crew, Mister Faulkner. We sail for Chesapeake Bay.

speaker: De Grasse
en: Lafayette promised me a fleet beyond compare, and a captain without peer! Instead I find myself greeted by one old ship and a boy in costume!

speaker: Connor
en: I promise we are all you need, Admiral.

speaker: De Grasse
en: I doubt this very much. But beggars do not choose, hmm?

speaker: Connor
en: And the ships I require?

speaker: De Grasse
en: They are yours... provided we survive this.

speaker: Connor
en: And what would you have me do?

speaker: De Grasse
en: Hold the bay while I engage the main fleet. Should any British ships dare approach, destroy them! They must be kept from Yorktown.

speaker: Faulkner
en: Herod all handsaws! Hell has manifest upon the sea. How many do you reckon?

speaker: Connor
en: Too many.

speaker: Faulkner
en: If anyone can hold the line, 'tis us. I only hope the Admiral's quick to return.

speaker: Faulkner
en: She's breaking up! We're down a ship. Take care...

speaker: Faulkner
en: Ship lost! Escorts all sunk. We're on our own now, sir... My God... Where are our blasted reinforcements?

speaker: Connor
en: They will come. We must hold the bay until they do.

speaker: Faulkner
en: This is madness! You're alone and we're without reinforcements!

speaker: Crew
en: We're under attack! Man-of-war's firing!

speaker: Faulkner
en: All our guns are down. We've no way to defend ourselves now! That beast is sure to sink us if we're not careful. He's not really planning to board them is he? Has he lost his mind? He's going to get us all killed...

speaker: Connor
en: The ship is yours, Mister Faulkner.

speaker: Faulkner
en: You mad bastard.

speaker: De Grasse
en: They say you took down the man-of-war all alone. Perhaps Lafayette did not exaggerate when he spoke of your abilities. As promised, my ships are yours to command. What do you require?

speaker: Connor
en: Five of them must enter New York's harbor, flying British flags.

speaker: De Grasse
en: Wait, wait. I thought you might need some pirates killed or goods transported... And instead you ask for us to, what, shell New York?

speaker: Connor
en: No. Of course not.

speaker: De Grasse
en: Ah...

speaker: Connor
en: Only part of it.

speaker: De Grasse
en: Explain yourself.

speaker: Connor
en: I mean to infiltrate Fort George. But it is too well-guarded. Cannon fire will breach its walls and scatter its guards.

speaker: De Grasse
en: And a ship that flies the French flag could never get near it...

speaker: Connor
en: You understand, then?

speaker: De Grasse
en: Not at all. But a promise is a promise - even when made to a lunatique (lunatic).

speaker: Connor
en: I will light a signal fire when it is time for you to attack.

speaker: De Grasse
en: Vous l ávez entendu! Récupérez leurs drapeaux qu'on les accrocher. Allez! Vite! (You heard the man! Scavenge their flags that we might fly them. Quickly now!)

speaker: Benedict
en: Connor, finished already. I have some more

speaker: Connor
en: Explain this.

speaker: Benedict
en: I don't know what 'this' is.

speaker: Connor
en: A letter, in your hand addressed to General Clinton of the British Army, confirming the surrender of West Point for the sum of twenty thousand pounds.

speaker: Benedict
en: This must be some sort of plot to expose the fort! I am a Patriot through and through, Connor! My actions at Saratoga speak to that, I'm sure.

speaker: Connor
en: For your sake I hope General Washington agrees. He will be arriving here today.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Regulars! Regulars! We're under attack! The main gate! The main! Push them back!

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Arnold betrayed us! That turncoat bastard!

speaker: Connor
en: We secure the fort! Then we deal with Arnold!

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Aye!

speaker: Soldier
en: Keep running, ya lechers! Ha! We did it! Well done!

speaker: Washington
en: Connor.

speaker: Connor
en: Arnold was behind this but he escaped.

speaker: Washington
en: If you did not catch him, nobody could have. Westpoint is secure and Major André will hang for his crimes.

speaker: Connor
en: And Arnold?

speaker: Washington
en: We'll try to find him, though I have my doubts. Whom can we trust now, if Patriot heroes are betraying us...?

speaker: Connor
en: You reap what you sow.

speaker: Connor
en: Where is Benjamin Church?

speaker: Haytham
en: So you want to see the man dead. Good. That makes two of us.

speaker: Connor
en: I don't need him to die. I just want back what he stole from the Continental Army.

speaker: Haytham
en: Oh, you Assassins ... always pretending to loathe act of taking a life. Just accept that it is not exactly the worst part of the job. Either that or consider changing your name...

speaker: Connor
en: Why do you want Church dead?

speaker: Haytham
en: The good doctor has gone and ran back to the British, I'm afraid. Abandoning his compatriots and the role he was to play here. Foolish man.

speaker: Connor
en: A role in your new world order?

speaker: Haytham
en: We can discuss politics later, if you manage to live long enough. Now, would you mind giving me a hand? This will go much quicker with both of us.

speaker: Connor
en: Why should I help you?

speaker: Haytham
en: You clearly want the supplies he's stolen. I want him punished. Our interests are aligned.

speaker: Connor
en: What about after we deal with Church? Will I just be waiting for your knife in my back?

speaker: Haytham
en: Who can say? Perhaps I'll have talked some sense into you by then. Come along.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Not this time, I'm afraid.

speaker: Connor
en: Just give me the supplies you stole, and I won't kill you!

speaker: Benjamin
en: Why I should I be afraid of you after this failure?

speaker: Connor
en: Next time will be different.

speaker: Benjamin
en: They all say that.

speaker: Connor
en: Where are the supplies you stole?

speaker: Benjamin
en: Why do you care? You have no claim to them.

speaker: Connor
en: I do not want them for myself. They were stolen from the Continental Army.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Where they, now? These muskets and medical supplies are of British manufactures. I doubt they were intended to be used against the British.

speaker: Connor
en: If that is true, then the British have no greater claim to the Colonies than the Iroquois.

speaker: Benjamin
en: And neither do your so-called Patriots.

speaker: Connor
en: I believe the Colonists and the Iroquois can live together in peace.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Then you are a naive fool. One I'll not waste any more breath on.

speaker: Crew
en: You see the catchfart, cap'n?

speaker: Robert
en: Anything, captain?

speaker: Connor
en: Due North of here.

speaker: Crew
en: The Randolph!

speaker: Robert
en: What's that weasel up to? Sheet anchor to windward, captain. You can be sure he's got something up his sleeve.

speaker: Robert
en: It's a bloody armada! I knew he was up to something! And he's turned to fight us - we're in it now, captain!

speaker: Connor
en: So we FIGHT, Mister Faulkner! Board the Randolph. Sink the rest!

speaker: Crew
en: Mast is down! We got the cockrobin!

speaker: Connor
en: She's ours men! Prepare to board! Biddle is mine!

speaker: Robert
en: Hook us in! Bring her close! To arms! To arms!

speaker: Clutterbuck
en: Man the swivels! Cover from the quarter deck!

speaker: Robert
en: Secure the aft lines! Tie off the bow! Board the Randolph!

speaker: Nicholas
en: Tenacious! Smart! Pity I have to kill you! Mr. Kenway will reward me greatly for ridding him of you. I will make you suffer for the damage you've done to the Randolph!

speaker: Connor
en: Your reign over the Colonial coast has come to an end.

speaker: Nicholas
en: Is that why you hunted me? Because you thought me an enemy to the cause? You're every bit the fool I was told.

speaker: Connor
en: You brought pain and suffering upon innocent people for nothing but personal gain.

speaker: Nicholas
en: Pain. Suffering. I set them free. Weeded out the dissenters and empowered the Patriots. So what if I was named Admiral. The Revolution needs one and I was the best man for the job. The only man. If not for me, the Continental Navy would remain but a handful of rafts. For all your vision, you Assassins are blind to the truth.

speaker: Connor
en: Enough.

speaker: Nicholas
en: Wait. Let the Randolph die with me. Don't take her as a prize. Please. Please. I want no quarter, just to sink with my ship.

speaker: Robert
en: I can't believe you mean to leave the Randolph! She's a mighty vessel captain - and what of Biddle?! You show him mercy in the face of

speaker: Robert
en: I guess that's that then. A tad over-dramatic, if you ask me. Still, a waste of a formidable ship. How's about a cheer for the boys then, eh?

speaker: Connor
en: Victory for the Aquila! For her glory! Hip hip!

speaker: Crew
en: Hurrah!

speaker: Connor
en: Hip hip!

speaker: Crew
en: Hurrah!

speaker: Robert
en: I've been a wild rover for many a year, and I spent all me money on whiskey and beer. And now I'm returning...

speaker: Haytham
en: Shall we?

speaker: Haytham
en: I told you this was a poor heading. Church is surely days ahead of us now...

speaker: Robert
en: Have some faith in the boy! He's yet to disappoint!

speaker: Haytham
en: Well the bar's not been set very high now, has it?

speaker: Connor
en: We are closer than you think, father.

speaker: Connor
en: Is it the Welcome?

speaker: Robert
en: Aye! And she's dropped anchor.

speaker: Haytham
en: Bring us in for a closer look, son.

speaker: Connor
en: It seems the ship has been abandoned.

speaker: Haytham
en: Church always was a slippery little bastard...

speaker: Crew
en: Enemy ahead! They're making to flee!

speaker: Connor
en: After them!

speaker: Haytham
en: How is it you came to captain a ship, given the way you sail? Perhaps someone with more experience should take the wheel? Speed, Connor! We need more speed! It's almost as though you WANT him to escape... Can the ship go no faster?! Hurry son! We won't get a second chance at this!

speaker: Robert
en: She's passing between the cliffs, boy, and the Aquila's too big to follow. We need to go around!

speaker: Haytham
en: Goddammit! We're going to lose him!

speaker: Robert
en: What other choice have we?! Those rocks would crush us!

speaker: Connor
en: The current here is swift. We still have a chance.

speaker: Haytham
en: Church is using the ambush as cover. Sink him before he escapes! Send that bastard to the seafloor!

speaker: Connor
en: No. I need his ship afloat. The cargo must be saved.

speaker: Haytham
en: Stop him, Connor! You should have listened to me! He's nearly away!

speaker: Connor
en: Men, prepare to board–

speaker: Connor
en: What are you doing?!

speaker: Haytham
en: Ending this!

speaker: Connor
en: Secure the ships!

speaker: Robert
en: Hook us in! Bring her close! To arms! To arms!

speaker: Connor
en: I need to get below deck. Who knows what madness my father intends...

speaker: Connor
en: Empty... What has Church done with the cargo?

speaker: Haytham
en: So here we are, face to face at last, my friend. It's been quite an adventure – let me tell you – working my way through your nasty little tricks and traps. Clever. Some of them, anyway. I'll give you credit for that. And for the quietude with which you pulled it off. We had a DREAM, Benjamin! A dream you sought to DESTROY! And for that, my fallen friend, you will be made to pay.

speaker: Connor
en: Enough! We came here for a reason.

speaker: Haytham
en: Different reasons, it seems.

speaker: Connor
en: Where are the supplies you stole?

speaker: Benjamin
en: Go to hell.

speaker: Connor
en: I ask again: where are the supplies?

speaker: Benjamin
en: On the island yonder, awaiting pickup. But you've no right to it. It isn't yours.

speaker: Connor
en: No, not mine. Those supplies are meant for men and women who believe in something bigger than themselves. Who fight and die that one day they might be free from tyranny such as you.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Are these the same men and women who fight with muskets forged from British steel? Who bind their wounds with bandages sewn by British hands. How convenient for them. We do the work. They reap the rewards.

speaker: Connor
en: You spin a story to excuse your crimes. As though you're the innocent one and they the thieves.

speaker: Benjamin
en: It's all a matter of perspective. There is no single path through life that's right and fair and does no harm. Do you truly think the Crown has no cause? No right to feel betrayed? You should know better than this, dedicated as you are to fighting Templars – who themselves see their work as just. Think on that the next time you insist your work alone befits the greater good. Your enemy would beg to differ – and would not be without cause.

speaker: Connor
en: Your words may have been sincere, but that does not make them true.

speaker: Haytham
en: You did well. His passing was a boon for us both. Come on. I expect you'll want my help retrieving everything from the island?

speaker: Blistering Dawn
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ratonhnhaké:ton's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Leaving home was harder than I thought. I expected the journey would fill me with a sort of pride. A sense of accomplishment. But whatever it was that carried me away from home soon fled, replaced by questions - and no small amount of doubt. Had I been too hasty? Had I made a mistake? The others in the village - they thought this was something I wanted. Something I chose to do. But it never felt that way to me. No, it was not a choice. It was an obligation. Because if not me, then who?

speaker: Achilles
en: GET OUT OF THE WAY!

speaker: Robber 1
en: After 'im!

speaker: Man
en: Hey! What are you doing?! That's mine! I'll have your head, scapegrace! Get back here, you addle-plot! Stop, thief!

speaker: Terry
en: Hello!

speaker: Godfrey
en: Hello!

speaker: Terry
en: You must be one of them native fellas. From the uh... what's it called... Iroquois tribe? Aye. You from that?

speaker: Godfrey
en: Course not, Terry. Iroquois ain't a tribe.

speaker: Terry
en: Is so.

speaker: Godfrey
en: Is not! The Iroquois is a confederation.

speaker: Terry
en: Confeda-what-now?

speaker: Godfrey
en: Confederation, ya tony. It's a group. An alliance. Lotsa different kinds of people all united.

speaker: Terry
en: Right. Like I said. A tribe.

speaker: Godfrey
en: Listen you totty-headed twiddle poop - there's difference between a tribe and a confederation and it's not my fault your skull's too thick to make sense of it.

speaker: Terry
en: Who you calling a twiddle poop, you crump-backed scab!

speaker: Terry
en: Hey now! This is between me and him!

speaker: Godfrey
en: Yeah! Mind your business!

speaker: Robber 1
en: Just give it a few days. We'll tend to the wounded, resupply, and come up wit a plan... I've sent Enoch to scout the place, figure out the best way in...

speaker: Robber 2
en: You hear 'im before? Sayin' 'e 'as no master but 'imself. What a load of fee faw fum. If he ain't no master, guess he's ours to do wit as we please.

speaker: Robber 1
en: Indeed. All in good time.

speaker: Robber 1
en: Private matters being discussed here. Best you move along.

speaker: Robber 2
en: Won't warn you again...

speaker: Achilles
en: What?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Um... I... I was told you could train me.

speaker: Achilles
en: No.

speaker: Achilles
en: Go away!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I'm not leaving! ... I need a place to camp. This should do.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: There must be another way in.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Please, all I ask is a moment of your time...

speaker: Achilles
en: I apologize if I've been unclear - or otherwise confused you with my words, it was never my intention to mislead. So let me try to clarify: GET THE HELL OFF MY LAND!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I'm coming up! Just hear me out! What are you so afraid of?!

speaker: Achilles
en: Afraid? You think I'm afraid of ANYTHING, least of all, a self-important little scab like you?! Oh, you might dream of being a hero. Of riding to rescues, of saving the world - but stay this course, and the only thing you're gonna be is DEAD. The world's moved on, boy. Best you do too.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I will not leave! Do you hear me? I am NEVER leaving! Just wait, old man. I won't be defeated so easily. You WILL train me, you HAVE to.

speaker: Robber 1
en: He's a square toes - this'll be easy.

speaker: Robber 2
en: That's what you said last time and I wound up with a dead 'orse an a dark eye.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Who are you?

speaker: Robber 1
en: No one you need concern yourself with, little breeches.

speaker: Robber 2
en: Best cut 'fore something bad 'appens.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: No.

speaker: Robber 2
en: Can't say we didn't warn ya.

speaker: Robbers
en: Oi! Brothers! Yield, boy, and we'll do ya quickly Songs and spirits can't save ya now! Hah! Look at the savage dance! Shoulda run when ya had the chance...

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Why are you here? What do you want?

speaker: Robber
en: Best ask the bossman.

speaker: Leader
en: You workin' for the old man, then? That it? Maybe this'll get ya talkin'. Oh.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Thank you.

speaker: Achilles
en: Clean this up. Then, I suppose we should talk...

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Sorry.

speaker: Achilles
en: Not your fault. This whole place is ready to come down. Goddamn miracle it hasn't already. Anyway, who are you?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: My name is Ratonhnhaké:ton.

speaker: Achilles
en: Right. Well, I'm not even going to try and pronounce that. Now tell me why you're here.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I was told to seek this symbol.

speaker: Achilles
en: Do you even know what that symbol represents? Or what it is you're asking for?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: No.

speaker: Achilles
en: And yet here you are.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: The spirit said that - That I've

speaker: Achilles
en: These "spirits" of yours have been harassing the Assassins for centuries. Ever since Ezio uncorked the bottle... Ah - but you don't even know what an Assassin is, do you? Well best settle in, then. I've got a story to tell and it's gonna take a while to get it all out...

speaker: Achilles
en: ... and so this is why the Assassins have dedicated themselves to the pursuit of the Templars. Because if they succeed - your spirit's visions will become reality.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Then I will stop them.

speaker: Achilles
en: Oh I have no doubt you'll try. Come on. I've something to show you. Careful. Wasn't a joke when I said this place was coming apart.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Why don't you repair it?

speaker: Achilles
en: What's the point? Besides I don't have materials for the job.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: So buy them.

speaker: Achilles
en: Look at me! You think I can just march into some store, purse full of pounds, and go shopping?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Yes. Why not?

speaker: Achilles
en: So naive...

speaker: Achilles
en: This way.

speaker: Achilles
en: Don't think you can just come in here, throw those on and call yourself an Assassin.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I... did not... I would never presume...

speaker: Achilles
en: That's alright. I know they've a certain allure. Very well. I'll train you. Then we'll know if you've the right to wear those robes...

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Thank you... uh...

speaker: Achilles
en: Name's Achilles. Come on, then. We've work to do.

speaker: Echo
en: You are a speck of dust. A nothing. You - and all your kind. Living in the dirt like animals. Oblivious to the true ways of the world...

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What do the Templars want?

speaker: Achilles
en: What they've always wanted: Control. They see an opportunity in the colonies. A chance for new beginnings, unfettered by the chaos of the past. This is why they back the British. Here they have a chance to illustrate the merits of their beliefs: A people in service to the principles of order and structure.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I have seen what is to come if they succeed. They have to die, don't they? All of them. Even my father.

speaker: Achilles
en: Especially your father. He's the one holding the whole thing together.

speaker: Ring
en: Think you're meaner than goose grease, do you? I'm organizing a tourney for lads like you. But it's not open to just anyone. Gotta prove yourself first. Here's a list of names. Beat each of these brutes and you'll get your spot. Then we'll see how tough you really are.

speaker: Duncan
en: So you're the lad. Neighborhood could use more men of action like yourself.

speaker: Connor
en: My name is Connor.

speaker: Duncan
en: That's a lovely name for a man from Wales. What's your name?

speaker: Connor
en: Ratonhnhaké:ton...

speaker: Duncan
en: A strong name—you should use it. Mine's Duncan, plain as they come. If you've the time to spare, I'd urge you to keep on doing what you're doing. This infernal gang needs to be stopped.

speaker: Duncan
en: How's it going, lad? I imagine you're busy these days, not much has changed with regards to our local thugs. I'll leave you to it.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Empty that purse.

speaker: Civilian
en: God forsaken thugs!

speaker: Mercenary
en: If you want to catch a beating, get closer.

speaker: Mercenary
en: You won't catch him!

speaker: Mercenary
en: Come on! Hit! I'll give you a real shot. You hit like a dandy. Keep talkin' and see where it gets ya.

speaker: Duncan
en: Your work is bearing fruit, my boy, and I'm close to figuring out who's orchestrating this ugly symphony. But something's got people spooked beyond the usual gang stuff. Odd. Anyway, keep on it.

speaker: Clipper
en: Don't mean to bother you, but I couldn't help but notice what you done. Real good of you.

speaker: Connor
en: What is happening here?

speaker: Clipper
en: Regulars have taken to conscribing the young ones 'round here. It's not right. I was thinking that maybe we could do some good together—if you had the time.

speaker: Connor
en: What would you have me do?

speaker: Clipper
en: More of the same, actually. I got a plan cooking, but the folks need to know they've got someone to turn to. Find me when you're done.

speaker: Clipper
en: They're still conscribing kids all over, but I wager you've been off fryin' bigger fish.

speaker: British soldier
en: Halt! In the name of the King!

speaker: Civilian
en: Leave me be! I never agreed to be a soldier!

speaker: Civilian
en: They're off my back for now.

speaker: British soldier
en: Piss off. This is military business.

speaker: Connor
en: You did not consent to this. Go home.

speaker: Civilian
en: You're a great man!

speaker: Clipper
en: You're doing it. The recruiters are scared to go out collecting. We're almost ready to make our move.

speaker: Adams
en: Over here! You're Achilles' boy. Connor, was it? I saw what happened at the Town House. A fine mess, that.

speaker: Connor
en: Who are you?

speaker: Adams
en: Samuel Adams, at your service. Achilles asked me to get you out of Boston.

speaker: Connor
en: Explain.

speaker: Adams
en: The whole city's looking for you...

speaker: Town crier
en: Oye! Oye! A criminal stalks the streets — wanted in connection with the massacre at the Town House! Citizens are advised to call the guards if they see him! Ten pounds to whoever brings this madman to justice!

speaker: Connor
en: What am I supposed to do?

speaker: Adams
en: You can take down these posters for a start. Return to me once you've removed the others.

speaker: Adams
en: Take down those posters, and then we'll talk... We can't be seen together until these posters are gone... I've nothing more to say so long as those posters remain...

speaker: Cyrus
en: None can say for certain who fired the first shot, but we now suspect a man of native origin. Many speculate as to why he acted. A show of solidarity with the protesters or was it vengeance for an attack on his people?

speaker: Redcoat 1
en: If it gets any colder, my nutmegs are apt to freeze.

speaker: Redcoat 2
en: What a beautiful picture you've painted for me. Thank you kindly that.

speaker: Redcoat 1
en: If they haven't caught the man who took the first shot by now, I can't imagine they ever will...

speaker: Redcoat 2
en: Aye. It's unlikely... But for a purse of fifty pounds no harm in keeping an eye out.

speaker: Redcoat 3
en: Was a mistake to let any of those troublemakers go. Should've silenced them all and been done with it.

speaker: Redcoat 4
en: What? And have more martyrs for their cause? No. It was a mistake for them to fire at all.

speaker: Redcoat 3
en: Are you mad? They'll see they can get away with it now. To stand down is to concede. We've empowered them!

speaker: Redcoat 4
en: We empowered them when the men opened fire.

speaker: Redcoat 3
en: The protesters shot first!

speaker: Redcoat 4
en: See how much that matters in the days to come. As they parade their dead and curse our names.

speaker: Adams
en: Ah, Connor, there you are. I'd like you to meet Cyrus.

speaker: Cyrus
en: Is he the killer?

speaker: Adams
en: Peace. Cyrus is on our side. Or rather... for the right price, he will be.

speaker: Jäger
en: Have you seen this man?

speaker: Adams
en: Watch and learn.

speaker: Cyrus
en: Oye! Oye! Word has reached us that the man responsible for today's shooting may have been in disguise! A hat and makeup tin were found near the scene of the crime. Witnesses describe a middle-aged gentleman of pale complexion fleeing towards the wharves, rifle in arm.

speaker: Adams
en: Thank you kindly, Cyrus.

speaker: Cyrus
en: Pleasure.

speaker: Adams
en: Come on, then. There's still one last bit of work to do.

speaker: Adams
en: Dammit! We're too late. They've set up a checkpoint. Come on. This way.

speaker: Connor
en: I can go by rooftop and meet you there?

speaker: Adams
en: No. Better you learn about the tunnels now.

speaker: Connor
en: Tunnels?

speaker: Adams
en: The Masons have a whole network of them under the city. They're quite useful when speed and secrecy are required.

speaker: Adams
en: You've no right to treat him that way! He's done no wrong! Let him alone! Leave him be! He's just a child! Unhand that boy or I'll see to it the whole city knows of your crimes!

speaker: Adams
en: Here we are, then. I'll see you inside.

speaker: Terry
en: Hey! Connor! How about a quick game of bowls? You ever played bowls?

speaker: Connor
en: I see you are getting along again.

speaker: Terry
en: Oh yeah. We're always at each other for one thing or another but more oft than not we work it out in the end. Was just the thought of my family threatened got me hot under the collar.

speaker: Godfrey
en: And Terry knows he couldn't beat me in a fight.

speaker: Terry
en: You rat!

speaker: Godfrey
en: That's why he build this bowls pitch- so he could beat me at something. Still can't though, can ya Terry?

speaker: Terry
en: I was winning 'til Connor came along!

speaker: Godfrey
en: Suuure you were.

speaker: Boone
en: There we was, eight months in the frontier trappin' and skinnin' elk - well along my third bale - when they came upon us. No less than a dozen Shawnee hunters had us surrounded at the point of musket and arrow. My bush partner froze up stiff. The fear chilled me the same but I managed to muster what little Shawnee I was knowin'. The leader spoke too quick but I gathered we was poachin', havin' crossed into their territory a month or so hence. Their musket barrels stared us down - the heads of their arrows smilin' sharp at our backs. I bumbled a proposition in busted Shawnee: our full piece - my three bales and my partner's two less a half - in exchange for us quittin' the Shawnee bush on our own legs. Leader nods to his boys. They load up our take and start back into the trees. The honcho stays a spell longer just starin'. Starin' right through us with his two black eyes. And then he was gone. We picked up and set back east the way we came - months of profit lost but our own hides intact. Never saw the Shawnee again but I know they was followin' us. I could feel their eyes on our backs clear to North Carolina...

speaker: Norris
en: Get off me, baptesme! (baptism!)

speaker: Redcoat 1
en: Have a taste of my boot, Frenchie.

speaker: Norris
en: A little help?! S'il vous plait?! (Please?!)

speaker: Redcoat 1
en: Ah! Go back to where you came from!

speaker: Norris
en: You just watch me take a beating?!

speaker: Redcoat 2
en: That feel nice, soap dodger?

speaker: Norris
en: Thank you, my friend. They had a little too much biére (beer) and didn't like the sound of my voice. I was only talking to that girl.

speaker: Connor
en: Your accent is unfamiliar. Where are you from?

speaker: Norris
en: North of here. Province de (of) Quebec.

speaker: Connor
en: And what brings you to Boston?

speaker: Norris
en: I am a miner by trade but it's hard to find work. People don't listen to me because of my accent.

speaker: Connor
en: It might be our meeting was fate. I hail from a village just a few miles north of here. There are beginnings of a mine. I do not know what is in there but perhaps you might find what you are looking for within.

speaker: Norris
en: I'll come have a look. If there's something good, maybe we'll talk.

speaker: Connor
en: You.

speaker: Thomas
en: You miss me, swee'art? Wot? Nothin' to say?

speaker: Connor
en: If you are here, then Washington is safe.

speaker: Thomas
en: True, true. Thing is... I believe I've just been pardoned.

speaker: Thomas
en: Thank you kindly for the rescue, gents.

speaker: Haytham
en: There can be no further mistakes, Thomas. Am I understood?

speaker: Thomas
en: Wot about the Assassin? E's here. They put 'im in the cell next to mine. Guess we didn't quite get 'em all, eh?

speaker: Haytham
en: Deal with this, Charles.

speaker: Charles
en: At once, sir.

speaker: Thomas
en: Wot are we gonna do?

speaker: Charles
en: You're that boy from the Continental Congress. Adams' little lap dog. Hmmm, I think I have an idea... Yes. Two birds with one stone.

speaker: Thomas
en: Do tell.

speaker: Charles
en: All in good time. It's not like the Assassin's going anywhere. For now we should see about getting you better accommodations here.

speaker: Thomas
en: What are you on about? I thought I was gettin' out.

speaker: Charles
en: I'm afraid you won't be leaving for a while, thanks to Benjamin Tallmadge. He's been running his mouth, saying all sorts of things. You're being investigated for plotting to assassinate George Washington.

speaker: Thomas
en: What a bunch of bollocks! I thought you was gonna handle that.

speaker: Charles
en: We'll discuss this ELSEWHERE.

speaker: Connor
en: They clearly spared no expense here... That is quite the view...

speaker: Connor
en: Smells even worse than it looks... Hmmm. I think I would rather hold it in. I hope that is not meant to be my meal...

speaker: Guard
en: Quiet in there! I said knock it off! I said quiet! Keep that up and I'll have you tossed in the pit!

speaker: Finch
en: ...I'm tellin' ya, he's plannin' to escape. We should get in on it!

speaker: Prisoner
en: Yeah? And what makes ya think that?

speaker: Finch
en: Caught 'im carvin' something in the yard. Slipped it in his pocket real quick when 'e saw me. Looked like a key.

speaker: Prisoner
en: Probably just a shiv.

speaker: Finch
en: Nah. Mason ain't a fighter. Always talkin' and trickin' his way outta trouble. Weasel Weems, they call 'im. Sneaky bastard.

speaker: Prisoner
en: Come on, Finch. He's not so bad. Even taught me some letters once. Gonna write a note to my lady.

speaker: Finch
en: What for? You think that whore's out there pinin' for ya? Savin herself for when you get out? Hah! No doubt she's already moved onto the next fella. And the fella after 'im.

speaker: Prisoner
en: You shut your mouth, 'fore I shut it for you.

speaker: Finch
en: Easy now – was just a joke.

speaker: Prisoner
en: Yeah? Well it wasn't very funny...

speaker: Guard 1
en: Get up.

speaker: Connor
en: Where are we going?

speaker: Guard 1
en: Stay out of trouble or you'll wind up in the pit.

speaker: Guard 2
en: What are you looking at, half-breed? You not understand English? That it? Do I need to knock some sense into that thick head of yours?

speaker: Connor
en: I should try and find this Weems fellow. If he intends to escape, perhaps he can help me.

speaker: Thomas
en: How's Bridewell treating ya, lad? Not too rough, I hope. I asked a few friends to pay you a visit. They been by yet? Thought you might like the company... Wait til you see what we have planned for you... Your sweetheart Tallmadge is tryin' to get you out. He ain't have much luck, I'm afraid. Master Lee made sure of that. Just a few more days and this'll all be over - for you n' Georgie bof. It's a nice pair of blades you got. Think I'll take 'em for myself when I get out. I might not be able to leave here, but don't mean I can't find ways to trouble you... Remember that.

speaker: Man
en: Please don't hurt me. Just... go away. Leave me alone or I'll call the guard! Help! Guards!

speaker: Guard 3
en: Get outta here. You not hear me the first time? Last warning, little man.

speaker: Connor
en: Mason Weems?

speaker: Weems
en: Could be.

speaker: Connor
en: I need your help.

speaker: Weems
en: Oh?

speaker: Connor
en: They say you know a way out of here.

speaker: Weems
en: THEY say a lot of things...

speaker: Connor
en: I do not have time for games.

speaker: Weems
en: A shame, as I was hoping you might play one with me.

speaker: Connor
en: Fine.

speaker: Weems
en: Are you familiar with the rules?

speaker: Weems
en: Seeing as you already know mine – what's your name?

speaker: Connor
en: Connor.

speaker: Weems
en: Pleased to meet you, Connor. Well played! So, what brings you to Bridewell?

speaker: Connor
en: Treachery. I have been falsely accused.

speaker: Weems
en: Of course you have...

speaker: Connor
en: You do not believe me?

speaker: Weems
en: Why should I? You've the look of a brute.

speaker: Connor
en: You misjudge. I am an honest man.

speaker: Weems
en: And yet also a man imprisoned. Tell me how you found yourself in this place.

speaker: Connor
en: It is a private matter.

speaker: Weems
en: As is what you ask of me...

speaker: Connor
en: I was trying to prevent a murder.

speaker: Weems
en: Oh? Anyone I know?

speaker: Connor
en: George Washington.

speaker: Weems
en: The others put you up to this, didn't they? Thought it might be fun to have another laugh at Mason's expense? Fools, the lot of them, to make light of something like this. George Washington is brave beyond measure, loyal like a brother, peerless in character, and unshakable in his convictions! That man is our Jupiter Conservator, destined to lead us not just to freedom, but greatness. Anyone who says otherwise is either a simpleton or a traitor.

speaker: Connor
en: Then you understand why I need to get out of here. If I don't help him, he is going to die.

speaker: Weems
en: You're serious, aren't you? Very well. But it's going to take some doing. See—everything hinges on the key I forged. But that lout Finch stole it! Took me three months to make the thing, too. You need to get it back or we're not going anywhere.

speaker: Connor
en: Consider it done.

speaker: Guard
en: Alright scoundrels, back in your cells!

speaker: Connor
en: This key is useless!

speaker: Guard
en: What are you looking at? You in the market for a husband?

speaker: Connor
en: Your key is useless.

speaker: Weems
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Connor
en: It did not fit the lock.

speaker: Weens
en: It's not meant to.

speaker: Connor
en: You forged a key that does not work?

speaker: Weems
en: Well that all depends on what you mean by work. It'll get us out of here, just not the way you expected.

speaker: Connor
en: Then how?

speaker: Weems
en: You're going to use it to get the real key off the warden. You have to swap yours for his.

speaker: Connor
en: Why not just have me take the real key? Why all this extra work?

speaker: Weems
en: He might notice if it went missing. This way, he'll be none the wiser.

speaker: Connor
en: And when HE tries to use it?

speaker: Weems
en: He won't. That's why we're targeting him.

speaker: Connor
en: How do I reach the warden?

speaker: Weems
en: Yes... This next part you may not like.

speaker: Connor
en: As if I've liked the others? Out with it.

speaker: Weems
en: You need to pick a fight.

speaker: Connor
en: What?

speaker: Weems
en: Pick a fight and they'll throw you in the pit.

speaker: Connor
en: How in the world does this help us?

speaker: Weems
en: The warden oversees the pit. Getting sent there is the only way to reach him.

speaker: Connor
en: I'll give you credit... You've given this plan to risk my life a great deal of thought.

speaker: Weems
en: Take down as many as you can. One or two will only serve to entertain the guards. You need to make them angry. We all have our part to play. Try not to die.

speaker: Guard
en: Fancy yourself a trouble-maker, eh? Some time in the pit should cool your blood.

speaker: Warden
en: Look at all of you. Pathetic, dirty wretches. You're naught but swine suckling at the teats of civilization. Thieves and scoundrels, all. And do you acknowledge this? Do you repent and beg forgiveness? No. You elect, instead, to commit new and more terrible crimes inside what should be a place of rehabilitation. You bide your time, awaiting the day of your release, that you might corrupt anew. The worst part is that the good people of New York are forced, quite literally, to pay for your crimes. Where do you think the money for this prison came from, hm? For your outfits? Our wages? Resources wasted because you refuse to contribute to society. You would rather dwell in its margins, living off the hard work of others. We'd be doing everyone a favor if we simply put you all down! Then our money might be spent on more productive things... ah, but it seems our current leaders lack the courage to accept this truth. So you are spared, that you might leech a while longer. And if a few of you might die or go missing, who would notice? Who will care, and why should they? You are wasted on the world. Mark my words, the time fast approaches when such weakness will no longer be tolerated. And what a joyous day that will be...

speaker: Connor
en: I need to take care not to raise the alarm.

speaker: Weems
en: You'll find Hickey through that door. It's where they keep the "important" prisoners. Nicer rooms, more space—those sorts of things. It seems even in a prison, who you know makes all the difference.

speaker: Connor
en: Thank you, Mason. For everything. I will find a way to repay the favor when my work here is finished.

speaker: Thomas
en: Not who you was expectin', am I right?

speaker: Charles
en: What have we here? I thought we'd finished off your kind.

speaker: Connor
en: You would like that, wouldn't you? To rid the world of all who do not share your views.

speaker: Charles
en: Guilty as charged. Your meddling in the revolution has caused us no small measure of grief. It cannot continue. Our work is too important. But what would you know, beyond all the lies Achilles feeds you and the tales you tell yourself.

speaker: Connor
en: I know that the people wish to be free—and that men like Washington fight to make it so.

speaker: Charles
en: Please. The man is weak. He stumbles and stammers through each engagement, making it all up as he goes along. His pedigree is pathetic – his military record even more so. I could go on and on but we'd be here for days, so manifold are his faults, so deficient are his merits. He must be dealt with. You as well. I will abide no more flies in the ointment.

speaker: Thomas
en: Ere is 'ow it's gonna work. First we bind ya and bring ya to your cell. Then, tomorrow, you go before the court, accused of plottin' to kill good ol' Georgie. Maybe we could pin the murder of the Warden on you too. You did kill 'im, after all. And who wouldn't take the word of Charlie over here? Once that's all squared away, well then...

speaker: Charles
en: All those years ago. The child in the forest was YOU.

speaker: Connor
en: I said I would find you.

speaker: Charles
en: And so you have. But not quite as you had expected, am I right? You know – all of this might have been avoided, had you only done what I asked. Ah, but what's done is done.

speaker: Achilles
en: Congratulations, Connor. You are now an Assassin.

speaker: Connor
en: Thank you.

speaker: Achilles
en: Now, what is most befitting of a new Assassin?

speaker: Connor
en: A target.

speaker: Achilles
en: Precisely! Times of war might be lamentable, but they offer an abundance of potential victims. Can you think of any?

speaker: Connor
en: Given the chance, the British would grind this land under their heel.

speaker: Achilles
en: Then might I suggest you don't give them that chance?

speaker: Connor
en: Am I to take the entire British army?

speaker: Achilles
en: No, my boy. Only the ones with power and authority.

speaker: Achilles
en: Well, what news do you bring?

speaker: Connor
en: The British Officer escaped.

speaker: Achilles
en: That is unfortunate, but hardly the end of the world.

speaker: Connor
en: When their patrol comes around again, I will make another attempt.

speaker: Achilles
en: Very good.

speaker: Connor
en: It is done.

speaker: Achilles
en: Very good. You have served the Assassins well.

speaker: Connor
en: But there is still much to be done.

speaker: Achilles
en: Yes, of course. A single officer will make little difference on the course of the war.

speaker: Connor
en: What would you suggest next?

speaker: Achilles
en: Let me think on it for a while. Speak to me after you've rested.

speaker: Haytham
en: We should be sharing what we know with Lee, not Washington...

speaker: Connor
en: You seem to think I favor him. But my enemy is a notion, not a nation. It is wrong to compel obedience—whether to the British Crown or the Templar Cross. And I hope in time the Loyalists will see this too, for they are also victims.

speaker: Haytham
en: You oppose tyranny. Injustice. These are just symptoms. Their true cause is human weakness. Why do you think I keep on trying to show you the error of your way?

speaker: Connor
en: You have SAID much, yes. But you have SHOWN me nothing.

speaker: Haytham
en: Then we'll have to remedy that then, won't we...

speaker: Connor
en: Sir.

speaker: George
en: Hello, Connor. What brings you here?

speaker: Connor
en: The British have recalled their men in Philadelphia. They march for New York.

speaker: George
en: Very well. I'll move our forces to Monmouth. If we can rout them, we'll have finally turned the tide.

speaker: Haytham
en: And what's this?

speaker: George
en: Private correspondence!

speaker: Haytham
en: Of course it is. Would you like to know what it says, Connor? It seems your good friend here has just ordered an attack on your village. Although attack might be putting it mildly. Tell him, Commander.

speaker: George
en: We've been receiving reports of allied natives working with the British. I've asked my men to put a stop to it.

speaker: Haytham
en: By burning their villages, and salting the land. By calling for their extermination, according to this letter. Not the either. Tell him what you did fourteen years ago.

speaker: George
en: That was another time. The Seven Years' War.

speaker: Haytham
en: And so now you see what happens to this "great man" when under duress. He makes excuses, displaces blame. Does a great many things, in fact—except take responsibility.

speaker: Connor
en: Enough! Who did what and why must wait. My people come first.

speaker: Haytham
en: Then let's be off.

speaker: Connor
en: No. You and I are finished.

speaker: Haytham
en: Son...

speaker: Connor
en: Do you think me so soft that by calling me son I might change my mind? How long did you sit on this information? Or am I to believe you discovered it now? My mother's blood may stain another's hands, but Charles Lee is no less a monster, and all he does, he does by your command. A warning to you both—choose to follow me or oppose me and I will kill you.

speaker: Connor
en: I should make sure the village is safe.

speaker: Clan Mother
en: Ratonhnhaké:ton! You have returned! But why? I thought you would be with that other man.

speaker: Connor
en: What other man?

speaker: Clan Mother
en: Boiling Water. The one called Charles Lee. He took Kanen'tó:kon and a few others with him.

speaker: Connor
en: What? Where have they gone?

speaker: Clan Mother
en: To push back those who would take our land.

speaker: Connor
en: No. This is wrong...

speaker: Clan mother
en: Why are you troubled? Is this not what you wanted? For us to take a stand?

speaker: Connor
en: I... I have to go. I need to stop them.

speaker: Connor
en: Peace, Kanen'tó:kon!

speaker: Connor
en: What?!

speaker: Connor
en: That man is a liar!

speaker: Connor
en: It is a mistake!

speaker: Connor
en: Stop!

speaker: Connor
en: It seems our people will never be safe. You are resting now, my friend.

speaker: Catherine
en: Connor! Connor! Some lout's trying to break into our house! He's armed! I'm getting the boys.

speaker: Connor
en: Find them, I will handle it.

speaker: Connor
en: Stop!

speaker: Terry
en: You can go home, if you want. I don't need you for this one.

speaker: Godfrey
en: Something's amiss!

speaker: Burglar
en: Please, mister. Don't hurt me. Beggin' yer mercy, sir. I din' mean it. Won' 'appen again, I swear. I won' come back 'ere. I promise. Just leave me be, mister.

speaker: Terry
en: What's the trouble Connor? Saw you tear past chasing a man.

speaker: Connor
en: He was trying to rob your home. It has been dealt with.

speaker: Godfrey
en: What? The women! Is everyone alright?!

speaker: Terry
en: You should have been there!

speaker: Godfrey
en: What?!

speaker: Terry
en: I TOLD you to head back. I didn't need you!

speaker: Godfrey
en: Since when is a skinny runt like you safe out in the bush alone?

speaker: Terry
en: If Diana's hurt, I swear you'll be the one payin' for it.

speaker: A Call for Help
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ratonhnhaké:ton's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Connor
en: I have come for you, Charles Lee!

speaker: Charles
en: You again? Don't you ever give up?

speaker: Connor
en: Not until your life has been ended.

speaker: Charles
en: Have you not noticed that all your attempts have failed? That all of your schemes on my life have come to nothing?

speaker: Connor
en: Eventually one of my schemes will succeed.

speaker: Charles
en: Yes, it is only a matter of time. Old age, or perhaps a fever, will claim me, and you can finally celebrate your hard fought victory.

speaker: Connor
en: I will not let that happen. Let's end this now!

speaker: Charles
en: You are a fool. A mad fool. And I'll no longer waste my time with you.

speaker: Connor
en: You can't escape that easily, Lee!

speaker: Connor
en: Get back here, Lee!

speaker: Charles
en: Another attempt, another failure. You are pathetic.

speaker: Connor
en: I will succeed, even if it takes my whole life to do so.

speaker: Charles
en: Such a persistent sod you are. It's almost depressing. Give up!

speaker: Connor
en: Never.

speaker: Charles
en: Why do you persist? You put us down, we rise again. You end one plot, we forge another. It always ends the same.

speaker: Connor
en: Because no one else will.

speaker: Charles
en: An absurd reason. We are not the demons you see us as.

speaker: Connor
en: What are you, then?

speaker: Charles
en: We merely offer guidance. With our direction, this new world would be a place where all are freed and equal.

speaker: Connor
en: The cost is too great.

speaker: Charles
en: You know nothing of cost! You have always acted without thinking of the cost. That is why there is no one left who stands with you.

speaker: Connor
en: That is a sacrifice I will gladly accept in order to rid the Colonies of you and your influence.

speaker: Charles
en: Foolish boy.

speaker: Faulkner
en: Ah, it's good to be at sea again! But I don't much like that sky.

speaker: Connor
en: Even a pretty sunrise is a bad omen to you, Mister Faulkner. Where are these raiders?

speaker: Faulkner
en: By guess and by God an Easterly course—t'wards the coast. Miss Mandy reports of some British boats gathering somewhere in these rocks, threatenin' the Vineyard.

speaker: Crew member
en: Sails ahoy!

speaker: Faulkner
en: British gunboats after one of the Vineyard's ship's captain! We must protect her!

speaker: Faulkner
en: Draw their fire, captain! We need to keep the gunboats off 'er till she reaches the Vineyard pier! We need to protect the civilian ship! She can't take much more of that! What are you doing, captain? That ship needs our help!

speaker: Crew member
en: Mines, captain!

speaker: Faulkner
en: Mines, captain! Destroy 'em or use 'em to our advantage. Either way, avoid the blasted things!

speaker: Connor
en: To our advantage? How?

speaker: Faulkner
en: Shoot the bloomin' things with the swivels when our targets get too close.

speaker: Faulkner
en: She should be safe now but it's a hot chase. Get after them and end the threat on the Vineyard.

speaker: Faulkner
en: They've veered north. Naught there but an abandoned fort.

speaker: Crew member
en: FORT! FORT!

speaker: Faulkner
en: That lobcock shouldn't be there!

speaker: Connor
en: Well it IS there, Mister Faulkner!

speaker: Faulkner
en: And it's too close to the Vineyard! Time and tide waits for no man! Take out her towers!

speaker: Crew members
en: Won't hit us with you at the helm, sir! Nice drivin' cap'n. Gotta avoid the mortars, sir! We need to dodge those mortars! Head clear of their splash down! We can't take another hit like that, captain! Steer away from them! Now, cap'n! While they reload!

speaker: Faulkner
en: That fort won't be troubling anybody no more. Bloody English have gone too far this time.

speaker: Connor
en: That is the problem. What reason would the English have to threaten Martha's Vineyard? It has no strategic value and its people remain peaceful. I fear an influence of a different kind saw to this.

speaker: Faulkner
en: Templars.

speaker: Connor
en: But what they intend, I do not know.

speaker: Faulkner
en: Your orders?

speaker: Connor
en: I need time to piece things together. We set a course for home.

speaker: Faulkner
en: Aye aye.

speaker: Catherine
en: Need something, darling?

speaker: Connor
en: No.

speaker: Catherine
en: Rude.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Can I help you?

speaker: Connor
en: You know you can.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Pardon?

speaker: Mercenary
en: Ow! Geez...

speaker: Connor
en: I do not like having my time wasted.

speaker: Mercenary
en: S-stop that. D-don't make me call the guards.

speaker: Connor
en: Make a sound and you die.

speaker: Mercenary
en: What do you want? He's in the harbor. At the long pier, most likely. We heard what happened at the parade. Charles got all nervous—said he was leaving the country. I thought he was overreacting. Guess not.

speaker: Connor
en: Thank you.

speaker: Charles
en: Why do you persist...? You put us down. We rise again. You end one plot – we forge another. You try so hard... But it always ends the same. Those who know you think you mad and this is why... Even those men you sought to save have turned their backs on you. Yet you fight. You resist. Why?

speaker: Connor
en: Because no one else will!

speaker: Harbormaster
en: Rough night, was it? He headed inland. Took a ferry up the Charles River.

speaker: Connor
en: I will need passage as well.

speaker: Harbormaster
en: Of course. Only say the word.

speaker: Connor
en: Why would they leave this behind?

speaker: Juno
en: Ah... long have we waited for you to return. You have done as we asked. You have succeeded.

speaker: Connor
en: No. I have failed. My people are gone—chased out by those who I thought would protect them...

speaker: Juno
en: It is a trade. A sacrifice. And not in vain.

speaker: Juno
en: For you have found it.

speaker: Connor
en: This?

speaker: Juno
en: Now you must hide it. Where none shall think to look.

speaker: Juno
en: And then in time... In time... What once was... shall be... again.

speaker: Connor
en: I do not understand.

speaker: Juno
en: Nor need you.

speaker: Juno
en: Only do as we ask. Then you may do as you wish.

speaker: Connor
en: But what of my people?

speaker: Juno
en: You have saved this place—as was your people's purpose. And that matters most.

speaker: Connor
en: It is not enough!

speaker: Juno
en: It will never be enough. You strive for that which does not exist. Still you have made a difference. And you will do so again. Remember... you must hide the amulet where none might find it.

speaker: Godfrey
en: They'll have to get through us first.

speaker: Terry
en: We're with ya, big guy. No matter what who's coming.

speaker: David
en: Connor! Connor! Connor. There you are.

speaker: Terry
en: ...they're coming, David. We need to be ready.

speaker: Connor
en: Who is coming?

speaker: Terry
en: Redcoats. David's to be tried for treason. And executed more than likely.

speaker: David
en: Connor, glad you're here. I want to show you something. I've collected these kegs. I might suggest building an ambush in the event we need it. They'll likely outnumber us at least 2 to 1.
