speaker: David
en: I hear them coming.

speaker: Officer
en: David Walston. Turn yourself in and stand before a military tribunal on charges of treason and desertion.

speaker: David
en: I don't want any part of this war. Leave me be.

speaker: David
en: There's more coming! I'm sure of it! Get ready!

speaker: David
en: Connor, I'm sorry. For bringing this violence on the village.

speaker: Connor
en: We protect our own. The British will not risk losing more soldiers for one deserter. You are free of it now.

speaker: George
en: For the support of the glorious cause I beg they will accept my most cordial thanks for this distinguished testimony of their approbation. But, lest some unlucky event should happen, unfavourable to my reputation, I beg it may be remembered, by every Gentleman in the room, that I, this day, declare with utmost sincerity, I do not think myself equal to the Command I am honored with. As to ...

speaker: Samuel
en: Truly, there is no man better suited to the task.

speaker: Charles
en: Really? I can think of several.

speaker: Connor
en: Charles Lee.

speaker: Charles
en: Do I know you?

speaker: Connor
en: I would not expect you to remember.

speaker: Samuel
en: Come Connor—there's someone I want you to meet. Sorry to pull you away like that, but the last thing we need is the two of you coming to blows. Connor, allow me to introduce you to our newly appointed Commander-in-Chief, George Washington.

speaker: George
en: Ah! So you're the one who saved Sam and John at Lexington.

speaker: Connor
en: It was the Patriots who did that, I merely lent support.

speaker: George
en: As humble as he is brave. We could use more men like you. I'm sorry, but if you'll excuse me—I should attend to Charles over there. He looks none too happy about being passed over for command. It was good to meet you, Connor.

speaker: Connor
en: Tell me you have news of Pitcairn.

speaker: Samuel
en: I'm told he's taken shelter in Boston, where he's guarded by a thousand Redcoats. The only way you're going to get at him, is if we draw him out. Lucky for you, we're launching an offensive against the city in order to do just that. Israel Putnam has been given command of our forces. Present this to him and he'll provide whatever aid you require. You'll find him at the encampment on Bunker Hill.

speaker: Connor
en: You have my thanks.

speaker: Samuel
en: No need. It's the least I could do. Pitcairn's a dangerous man. The sooner we're rid of him, the better.

speaker: Connor
en: I would say the same of Charles Lee.

speaker: Samuel
en: Now that's an altogether different beast. Let us leave it for another day. Best you head to Boston, Connor.

speaker: Patriot
en: Hold and state your business!

speaker: Connor
en: I'm looking for Israel Putnam.

speaker: Patriot
en: On who's orders?

speaker: Connor
en: Samuel Adams.

speaker: Patriot
en: Follow me.

speaker: Connor
en: This is not Bunker Hill.

speaker: Patriot
en: Aye. It's Breed's. There's been some... disagreement as to where we should encamp.

speaker: Connor
en: Any news from Boston?

speaker: Patriot
en: The Tories aren't moving. And anytime we try to press them, we lose a dozen men. I think Putnam and the others plan to assemble artillery on these hills. A good shelling might make the Redcoats rethink their strategy.

speaker: Connor
en: And what of John Pitcairn?

speaker: Patriot
en: That bastard is the cagiest of the bunch. He's appeared, time to time, to taunt us or send regards by way of cannon fire. It's all right, though. He'll have what's coming to him soon enough.

speaker: Patriot
en: Putnam's just up ahead. You can't miss him.

speaker: Putnam
en: I don't care much for your excuses, gentlemen. We should be building on Bunker Hill. Breed's is closer to the city, but it is also closer to their artillery!

speaker: Prescott
en: Our orders came from men so divorced from the situation, we are compelled by reason to employ our own faculties to make a proper determination.

speaker: Putnam
en: Were that I could understand even HALF that nonsense you just uttered.

speaker: Prescott
en: What's not to understand?! I'm trying to ensure our victory!

speaker: Putnam
en: What would you know about victory? I killed a she-wolf in her den, armed with only a knife. I escaped the Indians who sought to burn me alive. And, I was the sole survivor of a shipwreck at the . So you'll excuse me if I choose not to follow your advice.

speaker: Putnam
en: I rest my case. I'm going back to Bunker Hill. Good-day, gentlemen.

speaker: Connor
en: General Putnam?

speaker: Putnam
en: What?

speaker: Connor
en: I'm looking for John Pitcairn. I was told you'd be able to help me find him.

speaker: Putnam
en: He's tucked away inside the city with no reason to leave. So long as that ship continues its assault, we'll never flush him out.

speaker: Connor
en: But if the ship was silenced...

speaker: Putnam
en: Then poor John might be forced to get off his arse and come forward!

speaker: Connor
en: I shall fly this flag to signal my success.

speaker: Putnam
en: And I shall speak fondly of you at your funeral.

speaker: Aveline
en: Connor? I'm Aveline de Grandpré your... "brother" from New Orleans.

speaker: Connor
en: Yes. Achilles told me you would come.

speaker: Aveline
en: I seek a loyalist – Officer Davidson, of Lord Dunmore's .

speaker: Connor
en: That regiment passed through here. Look at the destruction they left. Their trail leads this way. We will follow them carefully.

speaker: Aveline
en: Over there! Through the trees!

speaker: Connor
en: A trap! Keep after the sentry. I will hold off these men.

speaker: Sentry
en: Unhand me!

speaker: Aveline
en: One chance to keep your life: where is Davidson?

speaker: Sentry
en: Who?

speaker: Aveline
en: Come on! Time's up!

speaker: Sentry
en: He's in the fort.

speaker: Aveline
en: That was easy. Why is it you call yourselves loyalists again?

speaker: Sentry
en: Easier to be loyal in the safety of the fort than out in the snow with a knife to your neck.

speaker: Aveline
en: Run home. Now. And don't let me see you again--you won't be able to run then.

speaker: Sentry
en: Y-yes ma'am.

speaker: Aveline
en: To the fort!

speaker: Connor
en: We climb.

speaker: Connor
en: Can you get across?

speaker: Connor
en: Can you find a way in? I will go around and divert attention.

speaker: Aveline
en: I had hoped it would not come to this. Now, in death, eternal freedom.

speaker: George
en: You mock me! I chose my destiny. That is real freedom. Perhaps one day you will know it too.

speaker: Aveline
en: I... Who is the Company Man?

speaker: George
en: The answer has been in your own backyard all along. Just open your eyes

speaker: Connor
en: Did you find what you sought?

speaker: Aveline
en: Oui (Yes), and much that I didn't. Connor, are you always... certain in the means and ways of the Brotherhood?

speaker: Connor
en: I... trust my own hands.

speaker: Aveline
en: Of course.

speaker: Connor
en: Travel safely.

speaker: Aveline
en: It's the arrival that concerns me.

speaker: Connor
en: Then you are on the right path.

speaker: Franklin
en: You!? And where ...? I ... I don't understand. Who am I?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Why did Arnold say that you could help me?

speaker: Franklin
en: Is this me? It is! This is myself! I've, I've come to myself! ... My god, what have I done?

speaker: Washington
en: I don't care for those who meddle in my plans.

speaker: Washington
en: Recoil before my vast power. Get thee hence! Back! You miserable wretch!

speaker: Washington
en: I will send you back to hell!

speaker: Washington
en: What black magic is this?

speaker: Washington
en: You cannot reach me! What?

speaker: Washington
en: Another magician's trick!

speaker: Washington
en: Here is the heat of my anger! Burn by divine fire! Behold the searing light! See the light!

speaker: Washington
en: What?! Where are you?

speaker: Washington
en: Welcome back.

speaker: Washington
en: Clever trick. Any other tricks?

speaker: Washington
en: Behold! He returns to light!

speaker: Washington
en: Escape! Escape as best you can!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Why did you disobey me, my son?!

speaker: Washington
en: Your mother cannot help you now.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: I wanted to protect you.

speaker: Washington
en: You failed to save your village. You failed to save your mother.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Never again, Ratonhnhaké:ton!

speaker: Washington
en: It's all falling away, falling away, falling away!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I had him! I had Franklin! Then ... Washington ... I ... I do not know.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Maybe I don't have to free Franklin from a prison. I have to free him from Washington's power.

speaker: Adams
en: Young man, do you need a doctor?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Samuel Adams!

speaker: Adams
en: Ah! Do I know you?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I ... I know of you, sir.

speaker: Adams
en: Ah... you are the famous man with the wolf hood.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I admire the work you have done, and are doing now.

speaker: Adams
en: We fight, but times are hard. We can use your assistance.

speaker: Maria
en: Help me! Help! Help me, please! I'm begging you to help me! Why won't you listen?! Please! Help me! Mister! Mister! My mother needs help! Please!? Please help her!

speaker: Connor
en: Where is your mother?

speaker: Maria
en: Follow me!

speaker: Quincent
en: Good for nothing wench!

speaker: Ellen
en: Let me go!

speaker: Quincent
en: Shut up!

speaker: Ellen
en: And stay away from my daughter!

speaker: Quincent
en: Bugger off before I crack you one. I guess you want a beating.

speaker: Connor
en: Leave.

speaker: Ellen
en: That wasn't necessary. I can handle myself. When he returns he'll try and give me twice the thrashing.

speaker: Connor
en: Why would you stay with such a man?

speaker: Ellen
en: This is my house and business! It's my tailoring that paid for the place. I'll take his drunken buffoonery over leaving behind what I built.

speaker: Connor
en: If I told you there was another place where you could live and work, free of him. Would you consider it?

speaker: Ellen
en: The catch?

speaker: Connor
en: No catch, our village is growing and in need of all forms of trade. Just business and a new life.

speaker: Ellen
en: I'll come and see if what you say is true.

speaker: Crewman

speaker: Faulkner
en: We're not flying the King's colors! They're sure to fire on us!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Gather up their colors. We will use them to disguise our ship.

speaker: Faulkner
en: You heard him boys! Haul in the flags and we'll hoist 'em up!

speaker: Crewman
en: Aye-aye, Mister Faulkner!

speaker: Faulkner
en: I forgot how a good sea battle could get my blood flowing! Sail around attacking ships. That's the life!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I know that feeling. It seems to run in my family.

speaker: Faulkner
en: Your father was a seafarer, then?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: My grandfather, Edward. He sailed with a rough crew, or so I am told.

speaker: Faulkner
en: For the king?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: For himself. But that is a long tale for another day, Mister Faulkner.

speaker: Faulkner
en: Slow down, lad! There's mines about! Don't shoot the mines. That'd give us away for sure!

speaker: Faulkner
en: There they are. We've fooled 'em with our flag! Christ! They're on top of us! Better shoot first. Catch 'em with their knickers down! Shoot the mines now, lad! Blow those boats to kingdom come!

speaker: Crewman
en: The guns are out of commission!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: We have no fire power. We will have to ram them.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Deploy full sail, Mr. Faulkner! Then abandon ship! You, too, Kanen'tó:kon. I will see you on shore.

speaker: Faulkner
en: Full sail, boys!

speaker: Franklin
en: My spectacles! Thank God!

speaker: Washington
en: Quite a sight, isn't it?

speaker: Franklin
en: Stay away from me! I will not come under your power again!

speaker: Washington
en: No need to worry.

speaker: Washington
en: No! No! No, please!

speaker: Washington
en: Get ... this ... off me!

speaker: Bluecoat
en: Yes, your Highness. Yes.

speaker: Washington
en: Never touch that! There was another one. Disperse and find him.

speaker: Bluecoat
en: Yes, your Highness!

en: was a virtual representation of one of Ratonhnhaké:ton's genetic memories.

speaker: Robert
en: Ship graveyard's just around the point. Can't miss it. The men say Abel Owens was aboard one of the doomed vessels. If it's true, you'll find what's left of him here. Scavengers love the graveyard! So be on your guard!

speaker: Connor
en: If Abel Owens' ship wrecked around here, they must have been looking for something themselves.

speaker: Connor
en: Another ship. Scavengers.

speaker: Connor
en: Put that down.

speaker: Scavenger
en: Piss off! I found it! 'Tis mine!

speaker: Connor
en: Stop!

speaker: Scavenger
en: Leave me be! I found it!

speaker: Connor
en: What you carry is mine!

speaker: Scavenger
en: Nice try!

speaker: Connor
en: Not that easy.

speaker: Scavenger
en: It's not yours! Leave me alone! Why are you chasing me! I've done nothing wrong!

speaker: Connor
en: Stop and give me what I came for!

speaker: Scavenger
en: Ha ha! What's mine is mine! Rantipole!

speaker: Connor
en: Hand it over!

speaker: Scavenger
en: Sorry mate! Looks like you lost this treasure hunt!

speaker: Connor
en: Damn.

speaker: Scavenger
en: Fellas! Some hector in a hood's chasin' me!

speaker: Mercenary
en: We'll deal with 'im.

speaker: Connor
en: "Near the wolf's abode."

speaker: Soldier
en: Call yourself a soldier? Did you really think we wouldn't come looking for you? Deserter!

speaker: Connor
en: Are you hurt?

speaker: David
en: Nothing that won't mend. Thank you, stranger.

speaker: Connor
en: What were they doing?

speaker: David
en: This lot was dragging me through the countryside trying to make an example of a deserter... sorry now, who are you?

speaker: Connor
en: Connor. A deserter you say?

speaker: David
en: Don't much agree with the fight and I love this country so there you have it. Name's David Walston- my friends call me Big Dave. Might I ask where you live so I could repay the debt when I'm able? Might take us a while, us smithies don't earn much coin these days.

speaker: Connor
en: Our community is not far from here and we certainly could use the services of a smith. Would you consider plying your trade there?

speaker: David
en: Well, would make repaying you a spot easier. I just might!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I never felt better.

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: Get your shoulder into it! Break it! Break the goddamn door! Put some muscle on it, you lily-livered cod!

speaker: Franklin
en: They're crazed savages! Kill them, or Washington will have our heads.

speaker: Franlkin
en: Or at least mine.

speaker: Bluecoat 2
en: Not a blessed thing here!

speaker: Bluecoat 3
en: Ain't nobody here at all!

speaker: Bluecoat 4
en: I don't see a damned thing!

speaker: Franklin
en: Those are the savages! Attack!

speaker: Dread of Night
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ratonhnhaké:ton's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Hunter
en: Ever come across King Edward the Elk? You'd know if you had. He's never found a mate on account of his aggression. Most hunters leave him be for fear of his charge. Grumpy old bastard's afraid of nothing. Word has it he doesn't like horses too much but I'm not willing to risk my head on rumors.

speaker: Achilles
en: Connor! It has occurred to me that the times we live in will be looked upon by future generations with a certain degree of scrutiny, no matter the outcome. With that in mind, I think it valuable to record the goings on around the homestead- a true log of how people lived during this time of transition. Something to help color the portrait. What do you think?

speaker: Connor
en: When I find a moment, I will try.

speaker: Achilles
en: Very good.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: The Aquila is ready. Do you have a crew?

speaker: Faulkner
en: They're here.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Can they fight?

speaker: Faulkner
en: They're sailors! They do nothing but fight!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Let's go.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Swim! I'll hold them off until you're ready to sail!

speaker: Faulkner
en: Swim lads! Swim!

speaker: Crew
en: Snipers! You need to stop them! They're shooting at Faulkner! You must stop the shooters! They're shooting at the crew!

speaker: Putnam
en: Savage! Over here!

speaker: Putnam
en: One move, just one move, and he's dead. Call back your men and give yourself up.

speaker: Putnam
en: Shut it!

speaker: Putnam
en: What is this?

speaker: Putnam
en: I've done such horrible deeds. ... it's the scepter, but ... that's no excuse. Every man holds evil deep within. The Apple just brought it out.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Kanen'tó:kon. I do not care.

speaker: Crew
en: Land ho!

speaker: Oliver
en: Connor!

speaker: Connor
en: What is happening?

speaker: David
en: Found this guy skulking around the inn. I pressed him and it turns out he's looking for a deserter, goes by the name of Big Dave. Says he's alone. Isn't that right?

speaker: Scout
en: I am! I'm alone. I swear it.

speaker: Scout
en: Bloody hell!

speaker: David
en: Another one, Connor! If he gets back to his officers, I'm done for!

speaker: Connor
en: Where is he?

speaker: Oliver
en: Coward kicked me in the gingamabobs, then threw sand in Dave's eyes. But he's long gone now.

speaker: David
en: Not good, Connor.

speaker: Connor
en: No. We can expect visitors soon.

speaker: Haytham
en: Evening Connor. I see you made it here in one piece.

speaker: Connor
en: Recovered from your beating, then?

speaker: Haytham
en: Benjamin Church is holed up in an abandoned brewery on the waterfront. We should be done with this by sunrise.

speaker: Connor
en: Good. I would like to have those supplies returned as soon as possible.

speaker: Haytham
en: Of course, I wouldn't want to keep you from your lost cause. Come along then. Follow me.

speaker: Connor
en: Tell me something... You could have killed me when we first met – what stayed your hand?

speaker: Haytham
en: Curiosity. Any other questions?

speaker: Connor
en: What is it the Templars truly seek?

speaker: Haytham
en: Order. Purpose. Direction. No more than that. It's your lot that means to confound with this nonsense talk of freedom. Time was, the Assassins professed a far more sensible goal, that of peace.

speaker: Connor
en: Freedom IS peace.

speaker: Haytham
en: Oh, no. It's an invitation to chaos. Only look at this little revolution your friends have started. I have stood before the Continental Congress and listened to them stamp and shout. All in the name of liberty. But it is just noise.

speaker: Connor
en: And this is why you favor Lee?

speaker: Haytham
en: He understands the needs of this would-be nation far better than the jobbernowls who profess to represent it.

speaker: Connor
en: It seems your tongue has tasted sour grapes. The people have made their choice – and it was Washington.

speaker: Haytham
en: The people chose nothing. It was done by a group of privileged cowards seeking only to enrich themselves. They convened in private and made a decision that would benefit THEM. Oh, they might have dressed it up with pretty words, but that does not make it true. The only difference, Connor – the ONLY difference between myself and those you aid – is that I do not feign affection.

speaker: Haytham
en: Hold a moment. Church, you clever bastard!

speaker: Connor
en: What is it?

speaker: Haytham
en: I was hoping I could wave you past the guards, but he's replaced most of them with men I don't know. Hmmm. Well I should be able to pass without arousing suspicion. But you...

speaker: Connor
en: No. We do this together or not at all.

speaker: Haytham
en: Then what do you propose?

speaker: Connor
en: I will find a guard who is off duty and take his uniform.

speaker: Haytham
en: Very well. I will wait here then.

speaker: Connor
en: Of course you will.

speaker: Haytham
en: Oh I'm sorry. Would you like me to come along and hold your hand, perhaps? Provide kind words of encouragement?

speaker: Haytham
en: That should suffice. Follow me.

speaker: Guard
en: Hold strangers! You tread on private property. What business have you here?

speaker: Haytham
en: The Father of Understanding guides us.

speaker: Guard
en: You, I recognize. Not the savage.

speaker: Haytham
en: He is my son.

speaker: Guard
en: Tasted of the forest's fruits, did you? Off you go, then.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: You're late.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Come. We have work to do. The Clan Mother has asked us to gather materials for tonight. We'll start with the feathers. We can scout the area for bird nests from up there.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: See? Not so bad.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: No.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Now you.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Yes there is. Look for places where the bark knots.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Better?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: But for how long? Come spring two dozen men will have moved here. By fall there will be two dozen more. They will hunt in these forests. They will settle on this land. In less than a year there will be a hundred of them. In time they will swallow us whole.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Yes. But they are CLOSER than they were. We need to do something. If we do not act, if we do not fight, it will happen again...

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Fine. There. An eagle's nest. The feathers will be finer than the others.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: No one needs to know, do they? Let's see if we can make it there without touching the ground.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Do as I do. You are doing just fine! Just follow my lead! See? It's not so bad!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: It will seem faster on the way back. It always does!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Embrace it! It means you grow stronger!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Have some faith in yourself! You've made it this far!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Not yet.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: No.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Soon...

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Now we climb.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: How do you hope to improve if you don't push yourself?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: There should be some other nests nearby. Search those.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What? I did that on purpose.

speaker: Jefferson
en: Well, sir, I have never seen anything like what you did back there. A resourceful man like yourself could easily help the people.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: My goal is to take Washington down. The rest is none of my concern.

speaker: Jefferson
en: We'll never defeat Washington without the people of New York behind us.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: And what do they want?

speaker: Jefferson
en: They are starving. We will win their support if we feed them; however, all the food is controlled by John Fitzwilliams. He is the most corrupt official in a city filled with corruption.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Bring him to me and I will track him to his stores of food.

speaker: Jefferson
en: There's Fitzwilliams. You won't find a worse blood-sucker this side of the Atlantic. He sells the food at inflated prices and skims the extra for himself.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I do not care about him. We only care about getting people something to eat. Eventually, he'll lead me to his hoard.

speaker: Man
en: I've no money, sir, but my family's desperate for food.

speaker: Fitzwilliams
en: Shove off! If you were a real man, you'd go rob somebody to pay me!

speaker: Fitzwilliams
en: Hey, pretty missy. I'll give you some food, if you're real nice to me, if you know what I'm sayin'?

speaker: Woman
en: All your carrots are rotten. Especially your little one.

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: Fitzwilliams cornered the market on foodstuffs, by god.

speaker: Bluecoat 2
en: How does he get away with it? Right under Washington's nose!

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: Oh, don't you worry. The king gets a cut of every carrot and turnip all right.

speaker: Bluecoat 2
en: You think Washington's a part of this?

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: What are you? An innocent babe?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: You! ... Yes, you.

speaker: Warren
en: I wasn't doin' nothin'!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Thomas Jefferson needs someone to get this cart of food to hungry people.

speaker: Warren
en: To sell it?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Give it.

speaker: Warren
en: Free food for hungry folks? I'm your man, friend!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Get some friends. We'll take as many cartloads as we can.

speaker: Warren
en: Right there! Bluecoats! Up there! I'm in trouble over here! Come back!

speaker: Warren
en: Can't go through there! Blow up those kegs!

speaker: Warren
en: Wasn't sure I was gonna make it out alive, but, god damn! This is the most fun I've had all week! Thomas Jefferson, people! This here food is thanks to Mister Thomas Jefferson!

speaker: Man
en: Thomas Jefferson!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Just a few carrots and he has won their loyalty.

speaker: Hunter
en: You look like a man up for a challenge. There's a bobcat 'round these parts, wiley as they come. I've lost count of them who've tried to get him on account of his pelt, pretty near perfect. You got that you'd make a mint not to mention something of a reputation.

speaker: Samuel
en: Master Connor! Master Connor! Dad and Godfrey are fighting! You need to stop it!

speaker: Diana
en: Oh come off it, Terry. I'm fine!

speaker: Catherine
en: Leave it alone, Godfrey!

speaker: Terry
en: I told you I didn't need your help! If you'd listened, none of this would've happened!

speaker: Godfrey
en: Quit puttin' this on me. I told YOU we didn't need to be cuttin' that day! So shut your mouth!

speaker: Godfrey
en: You need some sense knocked into you! I'm going to beat you senseless.

speaker: Terry
en: I'm going to smash you, ya looby! Time I set you straight!

speaker: Connor
en: Are you alright? There is no need for this.

speaker: Terry
en: Bah. He's a block-head.

speaker: Diana
en: He'll cool-off in a spell. Just needs some time is all.

speaker: Connor
en: Are you not angry, Godfrey?

speaker: Godfrey
en: Me? Not at all! Terry's just got himself a temper and I won't let him get away with it. It's really no trouble. He'll calm down. The runt couldn't do much damage anyway!

speaker: Connor
en: Does this happen often?

speaker: Godfrey
en: Ha! I was just telling Lance how I can set the calendar by these events. It's really not a worry, Connor, but I appreciate your concern.

speaker: Dave
en: Connor! Connor!

speaker: Godfrey
en: Connor! Ellen's dullard of a man's trying to break down her door with his mates! We're on our way to stop it!

speaker: Connor
en: Ellen and Maria are free of you. I say so. The people behind me say so. Believe me when I tell you if I EVER see you on this land again, I will end you.

speaker: Quincent
en: You can have them.

speaker: Ellen
en: Thank you. All of you. Nobody has ever stood up for us before.

speaker: Dave
en: We protect our own, Ellen.

speaker: Ellen
en: This is my home, now. I'll find a way to show my gratitude to you all. I promise.

speaker: Timothy
en: Excuse me. Might I impose upon the kindness in your heart to give bed and board to a weary traveler?

speaker: Oliver
en: Oh, Traveler from where?

speaker: Timothy
en: Across an ocean. London.

speaker: Godfrey
en: English? Ha ha ha!

speaker: Timothy
en: Rest assured I'm not the King's man.

speaker: Timothy
en: A great kindness. Bless you.

speaker: Terry
en: We work hard for what we have here, old man. What is it you do exactly?

speaker: Timothy
en: I wish to provide God for those who seek His salvation, not spoon feed His word to those who already have their own. An outlook not shared by the Monarchy.

speaker: Corrine
en: Ollie and I have been missing our Sunday mass.

speaker: Ellen
en: I'd like Maria to read the bible. I'm sure if we all pitched in we could build a church. If you'd be our pastor. Connor?

speaker: Connor
en: Welcome... minister?

speaker: Timothy
en: Father. Father Timothy.

speaker: Timothy
en: Bless you. This will build a fine place of worship. I am most grateful.

speaker: Boone
en: It stands upright, as a man, but its whole body is covered in a thick pelt. Its gait is slow and lurching—I've seen it with my own two eyes. It's clever, always at a distance or with something between us—like it knows where I'm gonna be before I get there. Things go missing where it goes, that much is certain. All manner of trinket. It took a man's prize antlers clear off his cabin wall. Takes kills outta traps too, wrenching 'em open with his big mitts. Somebody should find it and bring back its head for the world to see.

speaker: Man
en: Hallo. You're the chap that was down the hill, yes? Welcome! Care for a leg of venison? Maybe a hen? I have some lovely wine, if you like. A !

speaker: Connor
en: No thank you. Who are you and what is this place?

speaker: Man
en: I'm just a man and this is my home! Doesn't look like much from the outside but that's sort of the point. Not much of a people person.

speaker: Connor
en: The locals think you are a demon of some sort.

speaker: Man
en: Is that what they're saying now? Probably frustrated on account of my naughty little habit. I take things. I know it's wrong, I do, but I just can't help myself. Thing is, I like my privacy. If I gave you some coin, might you keep my home a secret? I'd be much obliged.

speaker: Haytham
en: It's locked. Give me a moment.

speaker: Connor
en: Must be strange for you, discovering my existence as you have.

speaker: Haytham
en: I'm actually curious to know what your mother might have said about me. I always wondered what life might have been like had she and I stayed together. How is she, by the way?

speaker: Connor
en: Dead. Murdered.

speaker: Haytham
en: What? I am sorry to hear that.

speaker: Connor
en: Oh, you're sorry? I found my mother burning alive. I'll never forget her face as she sent me away. Charles Lee is responsible for her death by your order. And you're sorry?

speaker: Haytham
en: That's impossible. I gave no such order. I spoke the opposite, in fact – I told them to give up the search for the Precursor Site. We were to focus on more practical pursuits...

speaker: Connor
en: It is done and I am all out of forgiveness.

speaker: Haytham
en: Benjamin Church. You stand accused of betraying the Templar Order and abandoning our principles in pursuit of personal gain. In consideration of your crime, I hereby sentence you to DEATH.

speaker: Impostor
en: Now!

speaker: Impostor
en: You're too late. Church and the cargo are long gone. And I'm afraid you won't be in any condition to follow...

speaker: Impostor
en: We've chosen to stand with the victor. It's Britain who'll win this war! You always did prefer principle to profit. Perhaps that's why your little kingdom's started to crumble! It was a nice dream you had – but a dream is all it ever was... More of them! Look at the half-breed fight! Like some feral dog... Best we put him down, boys!

speaker: Connor
en: Where is Church?

speaker: Impostor
en: I'll tell you. Anything you want. Only promise that you'll let me live.

speaker: Connor
en: You have my word.

speaker: Impostor
en: He left yesterday for Martinique. Took passage on a trading sloop called the Welcome. Loaded half its hold with the supplies he stole from the Patriots. That's all I know. I swear.

speaker: Impostor
en: You promised...

speaker: Haytham
en: And HE kept his word. Let's go.

speaker: Connor
en: We need to get out of here.

speaker: Haytham
en: You don't say... Now is not the time for sight-seeing!

speaker: Haytham
en: So close, yet so far... You'll need to find a way around the flames.

speaker: Haytham
en: Get back here, traitors! Oh, how I'll enjoy making you pay for your betrayal! Did Church pay you well? Were you rewarded handsomely? And what good does your gold do you now? Is it magic gold, you think? Like the one they spun the fleece from? Do you think it will shield you from the flames?

speaker: Haytham
en: Stuck! See if you can find something to pry it open. Connor? What are you up to?

speaker: Haytham
en: Oh. No. Don't do that. There's no way of knowing what's on the other siiiii–

speaker: Haytham
en: –iiiiide!

speaker: Connor
en: We do now.

speaker: Haytham
en: Church has at least a day on us... We must move quickly if we're to catch him.

speaker: Connor
en: I have a ship we can use. Meet me on the pier when you're ready.

speaker: Norris
en: She will like it. It is perfect. No reason to be nervous. Vas-y, Maurice, c'est rien. (Come on, Maurice, it is nothing.) Connor.

speaker: Connor
en: Norris! What are you doing out here?

speaker: Norris
en: I want to give Myriam her knife. Maybe you come with me?

speaker: Connor
en: Of course. What is keeping you?

speaker: Norris
en: I am nervous.

speaker: Connor
en: I am certain she will love the blade you made for her.

speaker: Norris
en: What am I doing? Giving a woman a KNIFE as a gift? It's so stupid!

speaker: Connor
en: This is something she will appreciate and use.

speaker: Norris
en: Arg. I made the stupid thing. I might as well give it to her.

speaker: Norris
en: Allo, Myriam.

speaker: Myriam
en: Hello, Norris, hello Connor. I'd love to stay and chat but I promised Ellen a bale of furs this week and am not even close to making good. I need to get out into the bush right away.

speaker: Connor
en: Two hunters are better than one. I can help if you like.

speaker: Myriam
en: Would you? I'd be much obliged.

speaker: Norris
en: I bring something for you. Maybe it will help.

speaker: Myriam
en: I really must get moving. I will thank you properly when I get back...until then.

speaker: Myriam
en: Meet me at my northernmost hunting blind after you take your first skin.

speaker: Myriam
en: Connor? You out there? Connor? Need some back-up! Could use a little help here!

speaker: Poacher
en: Bloody hell. Not him.

speaker: Connor
en: The time for forgiveness has passed.

speaker: Poacher
en: Please don't kill me! I'll never come back! I'm sorry! I'm sorry! I won't come back again! I swear it!

speaker: Poacher
en: Please, mister. Please. Wasn't right for me to come back. I see that now. Just let me go and I'll stay away for good.

speaker: Myriam
en: If I hadn't had this blade, that lickspittle might've gutted me.

speaker: Connor
en: A timely gift from Norris, it would seem.

speaker: Myriam
en: Indeed. I must make sure to thank him properly.

speaker: Faulkner
en: Fort doesn't look as abandoned as it should. Looks occupied as can be.

speaker: Connor
en: I will need something to draw their attention, then. Once you lose sight of me, wait for ten minutes then bombard the fort. I will slip out under cover of the shelling.

speaker: Faulkner
en: Aye aye, sir. Sounds a trifle dangerous but I'm sure you're up to it. I doubt they let convicted pirates like ol' Lucky Lem out of his cell much, so if his little scroll is anywhere – it's there.

speaker: Captain
en: Form ranks! Present arms! Position one! Position two! Move!

speaker: Connor
en: I will have to circle around to avoid the courtyard.

speaker: Soldier
en: Ah, it's probably a gull or a rat... the only intruders we get here anyway. Preposterous. Send me across the ocean to play sentry on some meaningless isle. This is my last tour for a certainty. When I see the Captain I'll look him directly in the eyes and say "Sir! I am going home. I have had enough of these nonsense assignments".

speaker: Guard 1
en: Who would ever attack this fort, I ask you? Nobody. No reason to. They sent us here cause the captain did something wrong.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Like what?

speaker: Guard 1
en: Buggered if I know.

speaker: Guard 3
en: I wager he buggered something...

speaker: Guard 1
en: Come off it. And keep watch.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Yah yah.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Double time! We'll get the whip if we're late for the captain's address!

speaker: Guard 2
en: I'm hurryin'! I'm hurryin'!

speaker: Captain
en: Not a day passes without me overhearing you lot complaining of this assignment. "The fort is meaningless", "command is punishing the Captain for what happened in Poland". I have had enough! We are here – under orders, I need not remind you – to hold Fort Wolcott against the rebels at all costs. And that is all that need concern you. You are not trained to comment on strategy nor are you aware of rebel movements. So put a stop to it! The next man I hear questioning the validity of our post will receive 10 lashes and 7 days in the old dungeon– without rations. Is that clear?

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Yes sir!

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Yes sir!

speaker: Captain
en: Check the dirt-sheet for duties and details for the coming week. B Company will be in drills and without rum rations until they PROPERLY execute formations two and three. Such sloppy marching will not be tolerated.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Yes sir!

speaker: Soldier 4
en: Yes sir!

speaker: Guard
en: That lurcher is out of his head. Who would do that to a man? That's why you don't let soldiers get bored.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Jackanape deserved everything he got. Won't tolerate such behavior. Let that be a lesson to the rest of you.

speaker: Guard 2
en: He didn't mean anything by what he said.

speaker: Guard 1
en: You getting soft?

speaker: Guard 2
en: I just don't think it's right.

speaker: Connor
en: "It lies under the eagle's bed,"

speaker: Guard
en: Let's see what you got, rebel.

speaker: Richard
en: Fire!

speaker: Soldier 1
en: We're under attack!!

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Captain's dead! Cut down by cannon shot!

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Rouse B Company! To the battlements!

speaker: Soldier 4
en: Move to the west wall!

speaker: Soldier 5
en: Bloody hell, where'd they come from?!

speaker: Soldier 6
en: To the armory!

speaker: Solider 7
en: Who's in command?!

speaker: Soldier 6
en: Form up! Form up!

speaker: Guard
en: Rebel! Bring him down!

speaker: Connor
en: I need to get to the Aquila.

speaker: Faulkner
en: You're late, captain.

speaker: Connor
en: Those occupying the fort were less than thrilled by my presence.

speaker: Faulkner
en: And?

speaker: Connor
en: And what?

speaker: Faulkner
en: The damned scroll, ya muckworm! Was it there?

speaker: Connor
en: That it was, Mister Faulkner.

speaker: Robert
en: Our charge, captain. The Belladonna under . She appears Spanish for all intents and purposes, but rest assured she's a French vessel.

speaker: David
en: French are bringin' in a boatload of powder and guns for Old Georgie and his Patriots. Some Colonial boats were s'posed to escort her up the coast but they left her behind. She been waitin' ever since.

speaker: Connor
en: We will make sure Washington gets what he is expecting.

speaker: Frenchman
en: Where is le Capitaine? (the captain?)

speaker: Connor
en: I am the captain.

speaker: Frenchman
en: You are late.

speaker: Connor
en: We came as quickly as the wind allowed.

speaker: Frenchman
en: Too slow.

speaker: Connor
en: And what happened to your escort?

speaker: Frenchman
en: Le Randolph started with us then departed without warning. Typique. (Typical.) This is why le Lieutenant insisted I come aboard. Partons. (Let's go.)

speaker: Robert
en: We'll go when we're good and bloody ready.

speaker: Frenchman
en: Quoi? (What?)

speaker: Robert
en: The Atlantic is a dangerous place for a lone ship, especially one laden with such desirable stock. You must be glad to see us.

speaker: Frenchman
en: Bof. It is hot here. My Lieutenant is not excited for the cold of the North.

speaker: Robert
en: Is this man being serious?

speaker: Connor
en: Keep a sharp eye, Mister Faulkner. Anybody searching for the Belladonna could be upon us in an instant with this fog.

speaker: Robert
en: Aye, captain. I've got a monkey's fist in me gut.

speaker: Crew member
en: English are on us, cap'n!

speaker: Frenchman
en: The power of the French Navy is clear!

speaker: Robert
en: They picked the wrong ship to pirate. Why in God's name are the English here in such force?

speaker: Connor
en: I do not know, but we must get the Belladonna out of this fog.

speaker: Frenchman
en: Do your job, capitaine! (captain!) Defend La Belladonna! We must protect her! La Belladonna is taking fire! The Belladonna does all the work!

speaker: Robert
en: Another wreck for the deep!

speaker: Richard
en: English frigates!

speaker: Crew member
en: Ha ha! Come one, come all! We're waiting for you!

speaker: Frenchman
en: Why are there so many?

speaker: Connor
en: It does not matter! We fight!

speaker: Robert
en: Aye. We're sitting ducks on the pond in this soup and you can be sure they've more on the way.

speaker: Frenchman
en: But what can we do?

speaker: Robert
en: Naught but pray they don't find us again.

speaker: Crew member
en: MAN O' WAR!

speaker: Frenchman
en: Grand Dieu! (Good God!) La Belladona's mainmast is down, capitaine! (captain!) We must stay close to her!

speaker: Robert
en: Bloody hell! Pummel that leviathan!

speaker: Connor
en: No! We board her. I must know how the English knew about the Belladonna. We take her a prize, men!

speaker: Frenchman
en: Board her? Es-tu fou? (Are you crazy?)

speaker: Crew
en: Arg! Arg!

speaker: Robert
en: Hook us in! Bring her close! To arms! To arms!

speaker: David
en: Man the swivels! Cover from the quarter deck!

speaker: Robert
en: Secure the aft lines! Tie off the bow!

speaker: Crew member
en: Arg!

speaker: Connor
en: How does the British Command know about the Belladonna?

speaker: Captain
en: British Command knows nothing of this.

speaker: Connor
en: Then how are you here?

speaker: Captain
en: We were led here by a Patriot. Nicholas Biddle.

speaker: Connor
en: Who does Biddle work for?

speaker: Captain
en: I think you know, Assassin.

speaker: Robert
en: What did the captain tell you?

speaker: Connor
en: Nicholas Biddle led them here. He set

speaker: Connor
en: The Randolph.

speaker: Robert
en: The Randolph?! Beat to quarters!

speaker: Connor
en: Belay that order! He is putting us to his rudder. We cannot leave the Belladonna undefended.

speaker: Robert
en: But sir!

speaker: Connor
en: She is incapacitated and vulnerable. Let him go. We will see each other again soon.

speaker: Duncan
en: Ah! Connor! Your work precedes you! Now it's time to finish the job. I'm told this chap just materialized from the ether and nobody has the stones, to you know... challenge him. Until now. We need a gang, a gang of our own though - fight fire with fire.

speaker: Barkeeper
en: About time we did something about those brutes. I want in.

speaker: Duncan
en: Good on ya! That's one for the lads. Come on, let's gather the rest.

speaker: Barkeeper
en: Bar's closed. Get out!

speaker: Connor
en: He was a Templar.

speaker: Duncan
en: What, like the KNIGHTS Templar? Jesus, I thought they were just a spook story.

speaker: Connor
en: They are very real.

speaker: Duncan
en: I'll take your word for it. Well, it's been a real pleasure. If you ever need a hand in a whatever it is you're up to, I'm your man.

speaker: Prudence
en: Help! Somebody, please help me! Connor! Thank the Lord!

speaker: Connor
en: Prudence! Are you alright? What are you doing out here in the woods?!

speaker: Prudence
en: Connor! Thank goodness. The baby's coming!

speaker: Connor
en: We need to get you to Dr. White.

speaker: Prudence
en: No! I can't move! Take my horse! Bring him here. GO!

speaker: Connor
en: Dr. White! Come with me. Now.

speaker: Lyle
en: What's wrong?

speaker: Connor
en: Prudence is in labor in the forest.

speaker: Lyle
en: In the forest? What in bloody hell is she doing out there?!

speaker: Connor
en: Does not matter.

speaker: Lyle
en: We need to get Warren.

speaker: Connor
en: Now?!

speaker: Lyle
en: Yes!

speaker: Connor
en: Warren! Are you here!?

speaker: Warren
en: Over here. What's the trouble? Where is she?!

speaker: Lyle
en: Tell me how she seemed to you.

speaker: Connor
en: In great pain. She could not move herself.

speaker: Lyle
en: Was she pale? Was there blood?

speaker: Connor
en: Not that I saw.

speaker: Lyle
en: Might be we have some time.

speaker: Warren
en: We must hurry!

speaker: Prudence
en: Hello Dr. I think I can manage at the moment...

speaker: Warren
en: Is she alright doctor?!

speaker: Lyle
en: No, she's not alright she's having a baby and HERE by the looks of it.

speaker: Lyle
en: There he is! Looks to be in fine health as well. Has a good set of lungs on him. Now I don't mean to rush you, but we need to get both you and- does he have a name yet?

speaker: Warren
en: Hunter.

speaker: Connor
en: Faulkner's guess better be right. Why anyone would believe the Northwest Passage exists is beyond me.

speaker: Connor
en: The Octavius. Hendrick van der Heul's first and last captaincy.

speaker: Connor
en: Hendrick van der Heul. Captain Kidd's quarter master turned captain himself. The path you sought never existed, Hendrick. I hope your suffering was short.

speaker: Connor
en: I need to get out of this thing! I must get out.

speaker: Connor
en: That was close!

speaker: Connor
en: Whoa!

speaker: Connor
en: I must not get caught in here. There is not much time.

speaker: Connor
en: "And abreast the rock that doesn't fit."

speaker: The Ghost War, Act 1
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ratonhnhaké:ton's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: The Ghost War, Act 2
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ratonhnhaké:ton's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: The Giant and the Storm
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ratonhnhaké:ton's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Jefferson
en: Our plan is working, my friend. Washington's troops are scattered. The palace is unguarded.

speaker: Franklin
en: This will help you along. The mechanism is rather tricky, but I'm sure you'll be able to unravel it.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Very well. I will see you once I have succeeded.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Why is this loose?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What target was up here?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: These doors were forced open.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Mother, you failed to stop Washington, but maybe I can follow you to him.

speaker: Soldier
en: There is someone in the palace! Shoot anything that comes through there! You! Patrol the area, make sure no one has already gotten in.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Dried blood. Too much for a human.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: There are teeth marks on this.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Someone broke through here.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Mother. It is time I finished what you began.

speaker: Warren
en: You want to tell him, my love?

speaker: Prudence
en: I'm pregnant!

speaker: Connor
en: Congratulations!

speaker: Warren
en: It's been a long time coming. It does present a slight problem, however. There's no doctor for miles.

speaker: Connor
en: Well, then we should find one.

speaker: Warren
en: I know of one that may consider moving here. His name is Dr. Lyle White. It's been a turn since we last saw him but you might try his old house in Boston.

speaker: Connor
en: Dr. White?

speaker: Apprentice
en: No. He's the drunken sot around the corner. If you can get his attention tell him I quit. All this ire on him. Not worth getting caught up in it. I have a family.

speaker: Civilian
en: Murderer!

speaker: Lyle
en: You believe everything you read in the broadsheets?!

speaker: Civilian
en: Go to hell, you monster!

speaker: Lyle
en: I did nothing wrong! It's the Redcoats! Open your eyes!

speaker: Civilian 1
en: You make me sick!

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Doctor Death! You earned that name! Bastard!

speaker: Civilian 3
en: Fight back! You devil spawn!

speaker: Lyle
en: Leave me be! 'Tis all lies!

speaker: Connor
en: Dr White?

speaker: Lyle
en: Yes.

speaker: Connor
en: My name is Connor.

speaker: Lyle
en: And what can I help you with? Another quote for the broadsheets for you to twist against me?

speaker: Connor
en: I am here to make you an offer.

speaker: Lyle
en: Don't you know who I am? I'm the doctor the British have been slandering all over town. "White Death"? No?

speaker: Connor
en: I was given your name by my friends Warren and Prudence. Prudence is with child and requires a doctor's hand.

speaker: Lyle
en: Prudence is PREGNANT!? Ha! They have been trying for years it seems. Maybe getting away from Boston is exactly what I need.

speaker: Connor
en: Time passed quickly after that – my days a blur of study, training, and work. What little free time Achilles allowed me was spent learning about the Templars. About Charles Lee and my father. I longed to confront them. To put an end to their schemes. To ensure my people would remain untroubled and free. But I knew it was too soon. That to approach them now would see me killed. All my work would be for nothing. Patience. Restraint. These proved the most difficult subjects for me. But in time I mastered them as well. Days became months. Months became years. And as my skill and knowledge grew – so too did I.

speaker: Robert
en: Come aboard and feast your eyes, boy! No no no no, not the left foot! Never the left foot. Horrible luck. Step with your right foot first.

speaker: Connor
en: She is... solid.

speaker: Robert
en: Aye. Weatherly and sleek. She'll fetch 12 knots in a stiff gale, ne'er a ship from here to Singapore can outrun her on her best day. Wha'dya say we take her out and show you what she can do first hand.

speaker: Connor
en: Where would we go?

speaker: Robert
en: As it happens she still needs guns and the officers to command them. We'll launch straight away. Don't worry, lad, I'll make sure you sprout good sea legs. Haul in the mainsail! Get up the rigging! Hand over fist! Come on, men!! Let's get her out where she needs to be!

speaker: Robert
en: Come on, lad! No time like the present! Double time, boy, it's time you learned! Take the helm. Come on, come on! She won't bite!

speaker: Robert
en: You're connected to her now – Listen and feel. She's idle. If you call for half sail, the men'll hop to it and she'll pick up.

speaker: Connor
en: Half sail!

speaker: Robert
en: Ha ha! The Aquila flies again. D'ya feel it, lad?! Set a course for Martha's Vineyard. We'll find our guns and officers there. She's a nimble vessel but the faster she goes the more cumbersome she grows and the firmer your hand needs to be. Enjoy this stretch of open water 'fore we come upon those shallows. Call for full sail if you like. Wind looks to be shifting. Stay alert, Connor. Gusty winds can be difficult to manage. Now take us through these shallows. Careful not to run up on 'em. The sandbars'll slow us down but the rocks'll put a hole through her hull. And if you want to make a quick tack, call for half sail - she's more maneuverable then. Mind those other vessels. Hold your tack to keep your right of way.

speaker: Robert
en: Cottages. We're close. Drop anchor. We'll go ashore, buy our guns and find our officers.

speaker: Robert
en: Oh, hullo, Miss Mandy. You're looking every bit as ravishing as I remember.

speaker: Amanda
en: After all these years you sail all the way to the Vineyard to pay me compliments?

speaker: Robert
en: We're looking for David and Richard Clutterbuck.

speaker: Amanda
en: Nice to see you, too.

speaker: David
en: Robert Faulkner. Where the hell you been?

speaker: Robert
en: Sorry for leavin' like I did lads, but where I was going... no one could know... You two working much?

speaker: Richard
en: Nah... between contracts at the moment.

speaker: Robert
en: Well, we're looking for gunnery officers. What would you two say to working with me again?

speaker: Richard
en: We'd be for gettin' into a few more scraps.

speaker: Robert
en: Good show! The Aquila is a fine vessel. We're fitting all the guns as we speak...

speaker: David
en: Looks like your friend's about to catch a beatin'.

speaker: Connor
en: Where is Charles Lee?

speaker: Church
en: I don't much care for your tone, boy.

speaker: Robert
en: Hey... You don't want to be doin' that, Biddle.

speaker: Biddle
en: Bobby Faulkner turned to wet-nursing? Good you finally realized you're a SHITE sailor.

speaker: Amanda
en: Whoa whoa whoa! Not in here gentlemen. Better still, not at all. Bobby, take your friends and get out.

speaker: Robert
en: Let's go boys. Our guns ought to be ready. Come on.

speaker: Robert
en: What the bloody hell was that about?

speaker: Connor
en: The older man is a Templar. Who was he with?

speaker: Robert
en: A Templar? The young buck was Nicholas Biddle. Nobody. Sails before the mast – midshipman for the Crown.

speaker: Connor
en: Are the guns ready?

speaker: Robert
en: Aye, but we won't jump in over our heads. We'll find a suitable target and show you how they work. We've fitted her with a modest amount of guns to start but rest assured there's ample room to add more should you feel the need. Looks like a British frigate with half seas over. Should do nicely for a spot of target practice. Bring her around broad side and when all guns are on target call 'fire'.

speaker: David
en: Round shot for a start!

speaker: Robert
en: Well done boy! Now aim all guns at her bow and do as much damage as possible.

speaker: Deckman
en: Some ol' powder in there.

speaker: Robert
en: Good! Now give the swivel guns a turn. More precise. Hit those old powder barrels and light up the sky.

speaker: Deckman
en: Woooo! Ne'er gets old.

speaker: David
en: Not bad for a spud, cap'n!

speaker: Robert
en: You are a fast learner.

speaker: Connor
en: Provided something interests me.

speaker: Robert
en: Ah... getting a taste for the open sea are we? We'll make a jack tar out of you yet. Now we should be getting back. The Old Man is like to have my hide for keeping you out so long...

speaker: Connor
en: Why is he shooting at us?

speaker: Robert
en: Destroying property of the crown. Disturbing the King's peace. Take your pick.

speaker: Connor
en: What do we do?

speaker: Robert
en: Naught else to do but fight back! Sink the bastard!

speaker: David
en: Use the swivels on 'em, cap'n!

speaker: Deckman
en: English frigates!

speaker: Robert
en: I'll be betwattled, another one! Where in the bloody hell did she come from?! Brace!

speaker: Robert
en: Carry on, sailor. Not bad for your first voyage, eh boy? Now we best be getting back or the Old Man will have my guts for garters.

speaker: Peg Leg
en: I got 'em! All of 'em! You find what I need and I'll give 'em to ya! Simple! You got a ship! Could find 'em all to boot!

speaker: Connor
en: Who is that man?

speaker: Robert
en: Him? Some ol' salt always going on about letters he's got from Captain Kidd. Nonsense, really, but he don't hurt no one, so I leave him be. Talk to him if you fancy, but be warned – he'll chew your ear off. Anyway, the Aquila's here for you, should you get a pang for the open sea. Now I implore you to head up the hill 'fore the Old Man comes out of retirement just for me.

speaker: Achilles
en: Three weeks... and not even a goodbye before you left.

speaker: Connor
en: Sorry...

speaker: Achilles
en: Well? What are you waiting for?

speaker: Achilles
en: Put them on.

speaker: Achilles
en: Once upon a time we had ceremonies on such occasions. But I don't think either of us are really the type for that. You've your tools and training. Your targets and goals. And now you have your title. Welcome to the Brotherhood, Connor.

speaker: Boone
en: I'd been out in the puckerbrush for six weeks. Game was scarce in the area and my belly needed fillin' so a broke for the coast and some crab or lobster from the tide pools. That's when I saw it. A lighthouse said to have been abandoned years ago, but there it was fires a burnin'. Then the sound happened. A moaning in the wind. My heart crept up my throat so high I could taste it. Just then a ten point buck started and I took after it. Got the buck but never went back to the lighthouse. Spirits in there I wager, and I'd challenge any man to set foot inside.

speaker: Woman
en: You're heading up that way?

speaker: Man
en: Beaches up there are teeming with crab. Nobody goes there on account of the lighthouse. I figure so long as I keep away from it, no reason for those troubled souls to bother me.

speaker: Local 1
en: I'd do it. I would!

speaker: Local 2
en: Hogwash.

speaker: Local 2
en: Show me the pounds and I'll sleep in the haunted lighthouse, for one night.

speaker: Local 3
en: Crying in the wind. I've heard it. My wife heard it, it's there, no mistaking it. Spirits.

speaker: Local 4
en: You believe in that?

speaker: Local 3
en: I didn't until I heard it with my own ears.

speaker: Achilles
en: Your work is nearly done, Connor. You know what must come next.

speaker: Connor
en: Yes. I must pay a visit to Haytham.

speaker: Achilles
en: Free yourself of sentimentality. He may be your father, but he is not, and never will be, your friend.

speaker: Connor
en: I know. At one time I had hoped he could be reasoned with.

speaker: Achilles
en: A naïve hope, but an one. I trust you will not hesitate when the time comes.

speaker: Connor
en: No. I will not.

speaker: Achilles
en: Good. Then there is hope for us.

speaker: Haytham
en: That's it? In some strange way, I expected better of you.

speaker: Connor
en: Don't make me do this. We could work together!

speaker: Haytham
en: Your sentimentality will be your downfall. Should you get another opportunity, I'd suggest you don't hesitate to take it.

speaker: Boone
en: I've never seen him myself but I've heard the stories from here to Kentucky. A German mercenary - Hessians is what they call 'em - was fighting a battle when a cannonball took his head clean off. His whole battalion was routed and they lost the encounter. But the lad didn't die. He's been wandering the bush on horseback around the battlefield ever since, searching for his head, chasin' innocents when he sees 'em, taking their domes for his own. He wears a pumpkin for a head now, until he finds what he's looking for. Like I said, I haven't seen 'em, but I have seen the bodies he leaves lying about, headless and grotesque. God rest their souls.

speaker: Henderson in Distress
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ratonhnhaké:ton's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Time passed. The child grew inside me. And then he entered the world. He had his father's features, but enough of me that he did not appear a stranger. In the end it mattered little. My people loved him as their own. I miss Haytham sometimes. He may have even loved me, in his own way. But his eyes... His eyes were ever fixed on the future—one in which he and his Templar brethren controlled all. My greatest fear is that one day I shall look into the face of my son and see the same dark hunger there.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Good morning, mother.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Hmmm... And what are you up to?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Nothing. I, uh... I was only...

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Go on. But do not venture past the valley.

speaker: Child 1
en: This way!

speaker: Mother 1
en: Stay out of the mud! It took me days to wash the stains from your clothes! No better than beasts...

speaker: Mother 2
en: Be home by sunset!

speaker: Child 2
en: Yes mother.

speaker: Child 3
en: Yes mother.

speaker: Man
en: Careful!

speaker: Child 3
en: Sorry!

speaker: Child 2
en: Go home! Shoo! Home!

speaker: Man
en: Take care, children, that you do not leave the valley.

speaker: Child 2
en: Maybe we should go back...

speaker: Child 1
en: They say there are wolves out here large as bears...

speaker: Child 2
en: ... and strange men who shoot fire from their hands.

speaker: Child 3
en: I heard they live in stone villages...

speaker: Child 1
en: ... filled with victims taken from these woods!

speaker: Child 2
en: Don't listen to them.

speaker: Child 1
en: Almost there!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What will we play?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: One, two, three four...

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: ...One hundred!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: There you are!

speaker: Child 1
en: Awww...

speaker: Child 2
en: How did you know? Can we go fishing later? We should look for shells when we're done! I'm hungry.

speaker: Child 1
en: I'll do better next time. You'll see. I can't believe you found me... I've got the best idea for my next hiding place...

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Boo!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Your turn!

speaker: Church
en: What have we here?

speaker: Lee
en: You look... familiar. Where have I seen you before?

speaker: Lee
en: That wasn't very nice.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Let me go!

speaker: Lee
en: Listen to that, he knows English.

speaker: Hickey
en: Smart for a savage.

speaker: Lee
en: Spirited, too.

speaker: Lee
en: We have... questions for your elders. Only tell us where your village is, boy, and you can go.

speaker: Johnson
en: Best do as he asks, child.

speaker: Lee
en: I could snap your neck, you know. A little more pressure and POP! The sad little flame of your life extinguished. You are a nothing. A speck of dust. You and all your ilk. Living in the dirt like animals, oblivious to the true ways of the world. The wiser among you recognize the shape of the future. They throw themselves at our feet and beg mercy. But not you, it seems. No... You cling desperately to your ways. Too ignorant to know your folly. But I am not unkind.

speaker: Lee
en: And so I spare you, that you may carry word to your people. Let them know the sooner we are given what we seek, the sooner you can return to your pathetic, empty lives. A fair trade, is it not?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What... is your... name?

speaker: Lee
en: Charles Lee. Why do you ask?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: So I can... find you.

speaker: Lee
en: I look forward to it.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: No! Mother! Where is my mother?

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: In here...

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Coming! Help us! I am here, I am here. It is going to be fine.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: No, my son. You must leave. Now.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Not without you.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: It's too late for that. You must be strong, Ratonhnhaké:ton. You must be brave.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Stop it. Stop it!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: You will think yourself alone, but know that I will be at your side. Always and forever.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: NO! STOP! LET ME GO! LET ME SAVE HER!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: I love you.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: MOTHER!

speaker: Dobby
en: While you were putting a stop to this madness I was sniffing out who's responsible.

speaker: Connor
en: His tactics are familiar to me.

speaker: Dobby
en: Is that right? Well, don't know who the man is but he's not for Patriots or British. He's got a fortified camp built around the main water supply in the area. All the seized crops, all the meat, everything is being moved there then resold at dizzying prices.

speaker: Connor
en: How do we get in?

speaker: Dobby
en: I got some local men ready to get in on the fight.

speaker: Dobby
en: He was a madman!

speaker: Connor
en: Not mad, beguiled by a set of dangerous but attractive ideals.

speaker: Dobby
en: Is that right? And who exactly are you?

speaker: Connor
en: Someone who seeks to relieve men like him of their power.

speaker: Dobby
en: After seeing what you can do, I'll leave it at that. But if you ever need an extra blade, I'll stand by you.

speaker: Connor
en: It is done.

speaker: Achilles
en: Johnson is dead?

speaker: Connor
en: No. He retreated when we destroyed the tea.

speaker: Achilles
en: Only to hatch some new scheme, I'm sure... You should have killed him.

speaker: Connor
en: There was no need.

speaker: Achilles
en: Time will tell if you speak the truth.

speaker: Connor
en: Kanen'tó:kon? Why are you here? Has something happened?

speaker: Connor
en: How is this possible? We destroyed the tea.

speaker: Achilles
en: The Templars are nothing if not resourceful. You should have heeded my warning.

speaker: Connor
en: Of course. Can you tell me where they are meeting?

speaker: Connor
en: Wait for me here.

speaker: Johnson
en: Brothers, please! I am confident we will find a solution!

speaker: Elder
en: We are not your brothers.

speaker: Johnson
en: Do we not seek the same things? Peace, prosperity, fertile land.

speaker: Elder
en: You seek land, true enough. Land that is not yours, nor any person's.

speaker: Johnson
en: I only wish to keep you safe! There are those who would betray and manipulate you. Or worse yet - take the land by force.

speaker: Elder
en: We are all too aware of the expeditions your people send against us.

speaker: Johnson
en: What do you mean, my people? We are all ONE! We should act as such.

speaker: Elder
en: How? By signing our lands over to you? Then we'll be as one - in your debt forever.

speaker: Elder
en: Sir William may have a point... What hope do we have against their black powder and iron?

speaker: Elder
en: The spirits will guide us as they always have.

speaker: Elder
en: Did they not guide us here?

speaker: Elder
en: Yes. That we might unmask the great betrayer.

speaker: Elder
en: This is a mistake. We should sign.

speaker: Johnson
en: Peace. Peace! Have I not always been an advocate? Have I not always sought to protect you from harm?

speaker: Elder
en: If you wish to protect us, then give us arms. Muskets and horses that we might defend ourselves!

speaker: Johnson
en: War is not the answer!

speaker: Elder
en: We remember ! We remember you moved the borders! Even today men dig up the land - showing no regard for those who live upon it. Your words are honeyed, but false. We are not here to negotiate. Nor to sell. We are here to tell you and yours to leave these lands.

speaker: Johnson
en: So be it. I offered you an olive branch, and you knocked it from my hand. Perhaps you'll respond better to the sword.

speaker: Elder
en: Are you threatening us?

speaker: Johnson
en: Yes. Do you still doubt?

speaker: Johnson
en: Ah! Thought you might send one of your own to oppose me. An unwise decision, as you'll now learn! Call off your dog or everyone dies!

speaker: Johnson
en: Ah, no. What have you done?

speaker: Connor
en: Ensured an end to your schemes. You sought to claim these lands for the Templars...

speaker: Johnson
en: Aye. That we might PROTECT them! Do you think that good King George lies awake at night hoping that no harm comes to his native subjects? Or that the people of the city care one whit about them? Oh, sure, the colonists are happy to trade when they need food or shelter or a bit of extra padding for their armies. But when the walls of the city constrict - when there's crops that need soil - when there's... when there's no enemy to fight - we'll see how kind the people are then.

speaker: Connor
en: The colonists have no quarrel with the Iroquois.

speaker: Johnson
en: Not yet. But they will. 'Tis the way of the world. In time, they'll turn. I... I could have stopped it. I could have saved you all...

speaker: Connor
en: You speak of salvation, but you were killing them.

speaker: Johnson
en: Aye. Because they would not listen! And so, it seems, neither will you.

speaker: Connor
en: May the Faceless One grant you the peace you claimed to seek.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: No. We still have meat and skins to collect.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I will teach you. There is a place close to the village rich with game. We will hunt there.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: The shot must be quick. The kill clean. This rabbit is a gift. We must return nature's kindness with our own.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Take the time to aim. A missed shot will startle your prey and end the hunt.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Now to skin it.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Quick cuts. Steady and certain. It's not just the meat we want - but the skin as well. To act in haste will spoil the bounty. Now I'll show you how to use a snare. First we must find a place where animals are likely to gather – a burrow, a feeding spot, a watering hole. Look for signs of recent activity.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: See? There was a rabbit here recently. This is a good place to set a snare.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Let us set another. Set your snare here.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Well done. Let us try for bigger game while we wait.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: No. Arrows and musket shot will ruin the hide. This one I'll take with my hands. I must move carefully. If the deer sees us, she will flee. Watch...

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I will need to draw her in with bait...

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Now to collect our bounty.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: We should check the snares.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: We need more, but time is short. Both of us must hunt if we're to finish.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I've faith in you. Have some in yourself.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I should return.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Kanen'tó:kon? What happened? Damn.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: We should get back. Hopefully the others will understand why our bounty is thin.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: How?

speaker: Jacob
en: We were just discussing the result of your work. It seems these military men are after you.

speaker: Connor
en: I have caught their attention.

speaker: Jacob
en: It does make our goals harder to achieve. The man we're after has gone into hiding, protected by his soldiers.

speaker: Connor
en: We fight our way in, then.

speaker: Jacob
en: Not possible, even for a man of your abilities. But I have another – less conventional – idea. You will be our prisoner and we shall present you for the bounty.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: That him? Doesn't look like much.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Doesn't matter now does it? The commander'll have his way with him. I wish I could be there to see.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Look at that! They got the lout! Well done, mate.

speaker: Soldier 4
en: You're gonna get what's coming to you half-breed.

speaker: Templar
en: People! Bear witness to what happens to rebels in my part of New York. These men defied the curfew set in place for safety. They assaulted his majesty's soldiers and conspired against the authority of the military. Such blatant disregard for protocol, designed to protect the citizens of New York, will be punished by death. We seek not to control you, to oppress you, we seek only to ensure your safety in the face of conflict and aggression. The civilians of New York must be protected at all costs, no matter their allegiance. It seems these three men sought to jeopardize your wellbeing. I will not tolerate it.

speaker: Jacob
en: That man. He thought what he was doing was right.

speaker: Connor
en: He did. As do his brothers.

speaker: Jacob
en: Who was he, really?

speaker: Connor
en: There are powerful organizations who seek control, nothing more. This man belonged to one.

speaker: Jacob
en: It does not surprise me. I don't know who you are but if you should need my help, I am happy to give it.

speaker: Washington
en: Ah. It is you. At last.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Commander Washington. If you give up the Apple, I will let you live.

speaker: Washington
en: Give up the Apple?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: It controls you.

speaker: Washington
en: Is that what you believe? I believe I control it. Although I never considered the possibility that it could control someone. Perhaps it can.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: You have been corrupted by the Apple's power.

speaker: Washington
en: Corrupted? Well, that raises an interesting question: Do you wish me to give up the Apple in order to ... save my soul? ... Or do you wish the Apple for yourself, so you can control the nation?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: ... The true rulers are the people.

speaker: Washington
en: Let's not deceive ourselves. It's an absurd thought, but let's suppose I were beholden to this Apple, how would you behave differently?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I would use it for the good of everyone.

speaker: Washington
en: Possession of the Apple is both a burden and a blessing. Tell me, when you shake the earth, do you feel that you are a slave to the people? ... Or do you wish to be their master?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: The people want you brought down.

speaker: Washington
en: But you didn't answer the question. I am the only King here.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I will end you for all you've done!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: My son, I am so worried for you. The Sky Journeys have lead you astray. Give up your fight for the Apple, please, my son, please!

speaker: Connor
en: Now's your chance! Take the Apple! Take it! TAKE IT!

speaker: Connor
en: Commander!

speaker: Washington
en: Take it! Take it from me. I do not want it!

speaker: Connor
en: No man should possess a power so absolute.

speaker: Washington
en: Sink it into the sea. Weight it and sink to the bottom-most reaches of the ocean!

speaker: Sailor
en: Where we headed, anyway?

speaker: Phantom
en: Commander Washington.

speaker: Washington
en: I thought I was alone.

speaker: Phantom
en: I'm sorry to interrupt.

speaker: Washington
en: It's quite all right.

speaker: Phantom
en: Things appear to be at a stalemate.

speaker: Washington
en: I'm afraid so.

speaker: Phantom
en: Might I suggest, Commander, that a republic cannot survive in a world with so many contending powers.

speaker: Washington
en: I beg your pardon?

speaker: Phantom
en: Elected bodies, to be sure. The war was fought for this. For this nation to prosper, for this nation to thrive, the weakness of a republic must be balanced by a powerful man at its center. A powerful man, Commander, who, if... if I may be so bold, would be elevated in the eyes of the world if he were given the title of King.

speaker: Washington
en: Sir. I believe I can answer you in complete candor. Your proposal raises the greatest mischief that can befall my country! You could not have found a person to whom your schemes are more disagreeable. Let me conjure you then, if you have any regard for your country, concern for yourself or posterity, or respect for me ... to banish these thoughts from your mind, never communicate, as from yourself, or any one else, a sentiment of the like nature.

speaker: Connor
en: We are done here.

speaker: Sailor
en: You want to go back?

speaker: Connor
en: Yes. Back. Take us back.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Thank you. It's not safe here. Go home. You have repaid my kindness.

speaker: Putnam
en: I must speak with Arnold myself.

speaker: Bluecoat
en: Yes sir. I'll arrange a detail to escort you immediately.

speaker: Putnam
en: I do not need one. You are acting commanding officer in my absence. If anything should go wrong ... well, your widow will be provided for. Dismissed.

speaker: Bluecoat
en: Yes, sir.

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: This is the worst.

speaker: Bluecoat 2
en: It's not so bad! The bear's in the cage. He don't look too strong to me.

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: Bear'd soon eat us as look at us.

speaker: Bluecoat 2
en: He looks friendly enough.

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: Hmph. Friendly until he's hungry.

speaker: Bluecoat 2
en: Even so, our duty ain't as bad as Addie's.

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: Why? What has he got to do?

speaker: Bluecoat 2
en: Clean the cage!

speaker: Bluecoat 3
en: The bear! Get the bear! General Arnold will have our heads!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I have waited a long time to end your treachery. You escaped me once, but today you die.

speaker: Arnold
en: Who are you? What is happening?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: You know who I am.

speaker: Arnold
en: I've never seen you before in my life! Washington's Apple. He uses it to control men; you... you have to believe me. I... I was not in my right mind.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What you did at West Point was of no one's mind but yours.

speaker: Arnold
en: West Point? I... I've never set foot in that fort in my life.

speaker: Arnold
en: Please. Washington, he's gone mad. You, you have to bring him down. He's no more a man but a monster. Find Benjamin Franklin in Boston. He can help you – but you have to, you have to free him.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Free him from where? Where?

speaker: Putnam
en: Got you.

speaker: Putnam
en: O-ho! Enjoy your nap? It's a shame about ol' Arnold, but, ha-ha! I had to laugh at your expression when I hit you! Great big eyes and then, out! Out like a light!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: God damn you, Putnam!

speaker: Putnam
en: You woke up just in time. We'll be arriving in Boston, the town that will soon be mine! Washington will love it: "Look, sir! The man who defied you! The man you shot point blank! I give him to you as a little gift! He wears a wolf hat, too!"

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: You have gone mad! All of you!

speaker: Putnam
en: With that, he'll kick out Ben Franklin for sure and Boston will be mine. It's in the bag – just like your head! Oh yes. You will make for quite the gift!

speaker: Traveler
en: If you're hungry, I've extra.

speaker: Connor
en: No thank you... Where is everyone?

speaker: Traveler
en: Gone west. Been a while since they left. Seems some fellow from New York was granted the land by congress.

speaker: Connor
en: What?

speaker: Traveler
en: Seein' it happen more and more. Government SAYS they don't take land that's already owned, but, uh...

speaker: Connor
en: How could this have happened?

speaker: Traveler
en: We're on our own now. No more Merry English parts and labor. Which means we gotta go at it ourselves. Gotta pay for it too. Sellin' land is quick and easy and not quite so nasty as taxes. And since some say they're what started the whole war, ain't no rush to bring 'em back. Clever men, these new leaders of ours. They know not to push it just yet. Too soon for taxes. Too... British.

speaker: Connor
en: Thank you.

speaker: Traveler
en: Be safe.

speaker: Connor
en: My father is dead. Charles Lee now leads the Templar Order in his place. I see now why ours is an eternal war. For each piece taken from the board, another is placed upon it. Back and forth we go. Across the world. Across the ages. Some days, mine feels an impossible task, but I cannot afford to be consumed with doubt. The people need me. Now, more than ever. I must stop the Templars. I will kill Charles Lee.

speaker: Charles
en: We gather today to remember a man of peerless vision, who sought to change the world. And change the world he did. Look around. Even now the British prepare to retreat - their spirits broken - their forces splintered. The Patriot leadership shall soon follow - either into our service or into the ground. And then, my friends, all of this will finally be ours! We have Haytham to thank for this. He and all those others who sacrificed for our cause. But he was not content merely to save the people of America, no, he sought to save those sworn to our destruction. He sought to save the Assassins. Aye. It seems a mad thing, now. And it cost him his life. The Assassins are a cruel and terrible coven. They speak only the language of death. Too late he learned the truth of this. Murdered by his own son. He gave his life as he lived, in service to a dream we all share. And so we must fight on. We will vanquish our enemies. We will spread our word.
