And in time, my brothers and sisters, in time we will have our New World.

speaker: Charles
en: He sent me away... That day at Fort George. He feared for my safety. I should have stayed. He said there was no danger.

speaker: Connor
en: He was wrong.

speaker: Charles
en: I will kill you, Connor. This, I swear. Not here, though. Not today. No... First - first I'll destroy all you hold dear. I'll burn that homestead of yours to the ground - and roast the severed heads of your precious "founding fathers" in its flames. And when I've finished with them, all the rest will burn as well. Your merry band of Assassins. The human refuse that lives on your land. Your village and its people. All of it - gone!

speaker: Connor
en: You can try, Charles. But as with all your schemes, this too will end in failure.

speaker: Charles
en: Get him on his feet. He will wait. He will watch. And then - when he's seen all his life's work brought to ruin... Only then will I allow him to die. Take him away.

speaker: Soldier
en: I could do this all day. In fact, I think I will!

speaker: Connor
en: Where is Charles Lee gone?

speaker: Mercenary
en: The harbor... to catch a ferry...

speaker: Captain
en: I believe these men meet your requirements.

speaker: Mercenary
en: You believe incorrectly. They're sick and weak. We're looking to build an army, not fill an almshouse.

speaker: Mercenary
en: It would take months to get them into fighting shape. We don't have the time.

speaker: Prisoner
en: No. Please. We'll do anything you want. Anything! Only take us with you!

speaker: Captain
en: Quiet, whelp!

speaker: Mercenary
en: Your merchandise is useless to us.

speaker: Captain
en: Perhaps we should discuss this back in my cabin?

speaker: Captain
en: I am sorry to have disappointed.

speaker: Mercenary
en: As you should be. For us to have come all this way for nothing... Tell me now why I shouldn't have you thrown into the sea.

speaker: Captain
en: No need to be rash. Only give me a little more time. I'll scour the other ships if I must. I'm certain there are prisoners who will meet your needs.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Very well. You have two days.

speaker: Captain
en: Thank you.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Present yourself to the Green Dragon Tavern in Boston with the men you've chosen. We shall meet you there along with our master.

speaker: Stephane
en: Hello, Connor! Welcome back.

speaker: Connor
en: Is everything in place?

speaker: Stephane
en: Oui. (Yes.) Lafayette waits for you inside the tunnel beneath the city.

speaker: Stephane
en: Sometimes I worry... That these Patriots—for all their talk of liberty and equality—will fall back into the old ways!

speaker: Lafayette
en: It will depend greatly on who is chosen to lead them. A man of humble means—who has worked to earn his place... I think a man like that is less likely to dream of thrones.

speaker: Stephane
en: All men dream of thrones. It is in our nature...

speaker: Lafayette
en: Then what would you do?

speaker: Stephane
en: Ensure their leader is sterile. Without an heir, the threat of succession is ended—and might be left to the people once more.

speaker: Lafayette
en: Connor! This tunnel will take you into the military district.

speaker: Connor
en: And the Admiral?

speaker: Lafayette
en: He waits for you to light the signal—and then the strike begins!

speaker: Stephane
en: And we will be there as well!

speaker: Connor
en: Need to get... inside the fort...

speaker: Connor
en: I am in no condition... to fight... need to stay... away from the guards...

speaker: Connor
en: Where are you, Charles...?

speaker: Haytham
en: Gone.

speaker: Haytham
en: Come now, you cannot hope to match me, Connor. For all your skills, you're still but a boy—with so much left to learn.

speaker: Connor
en: Give me Lee!

speaker: Haytham
en: Impossible. He is the promise of a better future. The sheep need a shepherd.

speaker: Connor
en: He has been dismissed and censured. He can do nothing for you now.

speaker: Haytham
en: A temporary setback. He will be restored.

speaker: Connor
en: We have an opportunity here. Together we can break the cycle, and end this ancient war. I know it.

speaker: Haytham
en: No. You WANT to know it. You WANT it to be true. Part of me once did as well. But it is an impossible dream.

speaker: Connor
en: We are blood, you and I. Please...

speaker: Haytham
en: No, son. We are enemies. And one of us must die.

speaker: Haytham
en: You act as though you have some right to judge. To declare me and mine wrong for the world. And yet everything I've shown you—all I've said and done—should CLEARLY demonstrate otherwise. We did not harm your people. We did not support the Crown. We worked to see this land united and at peace. Under our rule all will be equal. Do the Patriots promise the same?

speaker: Connor
en: They offer freedom.

speaker: Haytham
en: Which I've told you—time and time again—is dangerous! There will never be consensus, son, among those you have helped to ascend. They will all differ in their views of what it means to be free. The peace you so desperately seek does not exist.

speaker: Connor
en: No. Together they will forge something new—better than what came before.

speaker: Haytham
en: These men are united now by a common cause. But when this battle is finished they will fall to fighting amongst themselves about how best to ensure control. In time it will lead to war. You will see.

speaker: Connor
en: The Patriot leaders do not seek control. There will be no monarch here. The people will have the power—as they should.

speaker: Haytham
en: The people never have the power. Only the illusion of it. And here's the real secret: they don't want it. The responsibility is too great to bear. It's why they're so quick to fall in line as soon as someone takes charge. They WANT to be told what to do. They YEARN for it. Little wonder, that, since all mankind was BUILT to SERVE.

speaker: Connor
en: So because we are inclined by nature to be controlled, who better than the Templars? It is a poor offer.

speaker: Haytham
en: It is truth! Principle and practice are two very different beasts.

speaker: Connor
en: No, father... You have given up—and would have us all do the same.

speaker: Connor
en: Surrender and I will spare you.

speaker: Haytham
en: Brave words from a man about to die.

speaker: Connor
en: You fare no better.

speaker: Haytham
en: Even when your kind appears to triumph... Still we rise again. And do you know why? It is because the Order is born of a REALIZATION. We require no creed. No indoctrination by desperate old men. All we need is that the world be as it is. And THIS is why the Templars will never be destroyed!

speaker: Haytham
en: Don't think I have any intention of caressing your cheek and saying I was wrong. I will not weep and wonder what might have been. I'm sure you understand.

speaker: Haytham
en: Still, I'm proud of you in a way. You have shown great conviction. Strength. Courage. All noble qualities. I should have killed you long ago.

speaker: Connor
en: Goodbye, father.

speaker: Connor
en: Old man. Achilles.

speaker: Timothy
en: What is it?

speaker: Connor
en: Achilles has passed.

speaker: Timothy
en: I'm so sorry.

speaker: Connor
en: He passed peacefully and with dignity.

speaker: Timothy
en: A service then?

speaker: Connor
en: Yes. Please prepare something... appropriate. I will see the grave is dug. Can you gather everyone?

speaker: Timothy
en: Prayer and sermon do not suit this occasion. Achilles was not a man of God. Not my God, at any rate. But he certainly believed in a guiding force, and he is at peace now and for that we can be grateful. We lay him to rest here, atop the bluff where he made his honorable and dignified life, so he can remain that comforting presence—the old man on the hill—that we have all grown to depend on. You all had your own relationships with him, your own moments and I implore you to return here when the time is right for you and share those stories with the waves and the trees. Achilles. You will be missed but never forgotten. Go safely, old man, safely to where your soul need rest.

speaker: Connor
en: I will make you proud, old man.

speaker: Connor
en: I never properly said goodbye to you. I was not ready. So here I am. The weight of my responsibilities never seems to diminish. There is always something else that needs fighting for. This is something you never warned me of, maybe because you thought I would have been deterred—you would have been wrong but I know you were not accustomed to that. Life carries on here. The people seem happy—they are certainly safe, at least for now. One of my brotherhood asked me something I have been struggling with, what happens if—when—we win? When we stop the Templars? It is a question I certainly do not know the answer to, perhaps you did not either. I miss you. As I miss my mother. I hope all is well with you, wherever you are. Goodbye, Old man, until it comes time for me to join you—then I will bother you once again.

speaker: Parker
en: Stand your ground, men! Don't fire unless fired upon! But if they mean to have a war, let it begin here!

speaker: Connor
en: Pitcairn.

speaker: Pitcairn
en: Disperse, you damned rebels! Lay down your arms and disperse!

speaker: Parker
en: What the deuce are you doing?! Hold your positions! Cravens! Traitors!

speaker: Connor
en: They are not coming back. You will have to make do with those who remain.

speaker: Parker
en: Don't you lecture me on how - Return fire! Return fire! You need to get to Concord and warn the others. Show this to whoever leads there. Should be a man by the name of James Barrett. Go on now.

speaker: Militiaman
en: Come on! We'll meet up with the others in Concord!

speaker: Militiaman
en: Get moving, men! We've little time!

speaker: Militiaman
en: Stick together, boys. And keep the pace!

speaker: Civilian
en: They're taking prisoners! Run!

speaker: Militiaman
en: To Concord, lads!

speaker: Civilian
en: Help! What's happening?

speaker: Militiaman
en: Get out! Everyone, run!

speaker: Civilian
en: They're taking prisoners! Run!

speaker: Civilian
en: Look! The Redcoats have taken captives! We have to help! They're over that way!

speaker: Civilian
en: No! Head for the hills!

speaker: Civilian
en: Dammit! Best get out of here!

speaker: Civilian
en: They've taken my brother and poor old Robert! We need to do something! They're over there!

speaker: Civilian
en: I'm not waitin' 'round to see what happens!

speaker: Militiman
en: I've got a surprise for those lobsterbacks!

speaker: Connor
en: Blood's been spilled in Lexington, and there's more to come. The Regulars are on the march.

speaker: Barrett
en: You don't say? And why do you think I've men up here? Go home, 'fore you get yourself killed. I've enough to worry about without some green boy looking to play at hero.

speaker: Dawes
en: I can vouch for him.

speaker: Connor
en: John Parker as well.

speaker: Connor
en: Where's Revere?

speaker: Dawes
en: Captured.

speaker: Connor
en: What?

speaker: Dawes
en: Fear not. That man's no stranger to sticky situations. He'll be fine, I'm sure of it.

speaker: Barrett
en: Ahem! you ladies finished gossiping? Parker seems to believe you're not completely useless. So I suppose there's a thing or two you might be able to help with... When the fighting starts, we'll need to hold those positions there. They're critical to the defense of Concord. Good boys, not used to soldiering. They need someone with experience to direct 'em. That something you can do?

speaker: Barrett
en: You'd best be telling the truth.

speaker: Connor
en: You have my word.

speaker: Barett
en: Then I suppose all that's left to do is wait...

speaker: Militiaman
en: Sir!

speaker: Barrett
en: MAN THE BARRICADES!

speaker: Barrett
en: No! Ensure my men hold those positions! If the Red Devils break through, we're finished!

speaker: Connor
en: What would you have me do?

speaker: Barrett
en: Listen carefully. The Redcoats will form firing lines. Order the men to shoot just before the line is ready. Too soon and they'll miss their targets. Too late and the enemy will open fire first.

speaker: Connor
en: Understood.

speaker: Barett
en: And if any of those bastards make it through, engage them! You must keep my men alive!

speaker: Connor
en: Wait for the signal! Hold fire! Make ready! Prepare yourselves! Wait for my signal! Fire now! Go! Open fire! Fire! Shoot!

speaker: Pitcairn
en: Fall Back! Fall Back!

speaker: Militiaman
en: We did it! They're turning tail!

speaker: Barrett
en: Takes a true monster to do something like this... At least they're gone.

speaker: Connor
en: I should have struck when I had the chance... Do you know where Pitcairn could've gone?

speaker: Barrett
en: Back into the withered bosom of the British no doubt - so that he might regroup and plan his next atrocity.

speaker: Connor
en: I need to find him. Every day I wait, more will suffer...

speaker: Barrett
en: Chin up, friend. Many who should've died today now live because of you.

speaker: Connor
en: And what of them?

speaker: Barrett
en: We did the best we can with what we've got.

speaker: Connor
en: It is not enough.

speaker: Barrett
en: Hm. It never is.

speaker: Achilles
en: Welcome back!

speaker: Connor
en: You left me in Boston!

speaker: Achilles
en: The training we've done here is all well and good, but experience is a better teacher by far.

speaker: Connor
en: What of my father?

speaker: Achilles
en: Into the wind, I'm afraid.

speaker: Connor
en: We have to find him!

speaker: Achilles
en: And we will... AFTER the house has been repaired.

speaker: Connor
en: But he's out there plotting who knows what.

speaker: Achilles
en: And what would you do when you found him? IF you found him? You're a boy with a few months of training. He's a man full grown who's spent decades honing his skills. If you're going to stand a chance against the Templars, you're going to need these.

speaker: Achilles
en: Go on. Before I change my mind.

speaker: Godfrey
en: Hey! Heeeeelp!

speaker: Adams
en: Hold on.

speaker: Adams
en: Use your lantern to light the lamps, Connor. They'll help us find our way should we get turned around.

speaker: Connor
en: I wonder why they built these tunnels...

speaker: Adams
en: Excellent. Let us move on. Uuuhh... Much as it pains me to say it, we must follow the rats — as they often move in the direction of an exit.

speaker: Adams
en: Well well! You were right. I apologize for ever doubting. No wonder Achilles has taken such an interest in you.

speaker: Adams
en: Arse! I don't suppose lock-picking is part of your repertoire?

speaker: Adams
en: Well done! The printer isn't far. Let us reconvene there.

speaker: Connor
en: Joseph Palmer retired to Jamaica – somewhere around this castle. Faulkner said the scroll would likely have ended up in Lord Lewis Hutchinson's private museum. This place has seen much evil.

speaker: Connor
en: Hutchinson's personal museum. Kidd's scroll must be here somewhere.

speaker: Connor
en: The shot must have come from the balcony.

speaker: Connor
en: The killer must have chased his prey, but through where?

speaker: Connor
en: The mechanism of the mask is broken.

speaker: Connor
en: I do not understand how anyone could live here. Small wonder Hutchinson went mad – this place feels mad.

speaker: Connor
en: There must be some clues around that can help me with this. The other clocks might tell me something.

speaker: Connor
en: "Close to a tree kissed by fire."

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Mr. Adams. I have a prisoner.

speaker: Adams
en: Franklin! You bastard! Take him out, have him shot!

speaker: Franklin
en: No, no, Sam! I've come to my senses! I want to help!

speaker: Adams
en: What of the murder of my cousin ? The families of ? What about the Old North Church that you burned with everyone inside?

speaker: Franklin
en: All horrible.

speaker: Adams
en: Do as I said.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: No. I believe he will help us. The only way to end this is to get to Washington. And Franklin knows Washington well.

speaker: Franklin
en: We've just learned that he is in New York.

speaker: Adams
en: But if we could join Jefferson's rebels in Manhattan, we could attack the King together. But how am I to escape the stranglehold around Boston? The docks are overrun with soldiers.

speaker: Adams
en: Looks like he must help us in such a way that he will not be caught... Perhaps he can triple the soldiers' rum ration. That way, we can catch them drunk at Boston Neck and break through.

speaker: Franklin
en: And once in New York, I can be of particular help!

speaker: Adams
en: I don't want to hear it.

speaker: Franklin
en: I created a very special means of protection for Washington's palace. An attack there would be completely unexpected.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: You can get me past these protections?

speaker: Franklin
en: You will need a metal of a specific weight. There's a blacksmith in town, loyal to me, he'll help you.

speaker: Adams
en: This is absurd.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I will get Franklin's metal and we will catch up with you.

speaker: Adams
en: This is a fool's errand, my friend, but I hope to see you in New York.

speaker: David
en: What can I do for you, Mister?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Benjamin Franklin has sent me. He asks something of you.

speaker: David
en: Franklin?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: He tells me you have an unusual metal. He would like you to give that to me.

speaker: David
en: Well, thing about that is...

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: The metal, please.

speaker: David
en: Fella came along the other day wanted his horse shod. Times bein' what they are, I was clean out a' iron. Man's got a right to feed his children, don't he? Sorry, mister.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: You used it for horse shoes?

speaker: David
en: Hi. Looked good, too. Real good. Feller rode away looking fine. Works in the citadel, that one.

speaker: Franklin
en: Oh, it's hot in there! I stoked the brick oven. I've got to get the heat extremely high in order to melt the metal. Did you get it?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I hope you have a crowbar.

speaker: Franklin
en: What for?

speaker: Hunter
en: Some folks were fixin' to settle on a plot not far from here. Seems a big black bear with a taste for human blood settled there first. Bring the beast down and some good people would be grateful.

speaker: Achilles
en: Connor. Come with me downstairs.

speaker: Connor
en: Should I search for something to fill that space?

speaker: Achilles
en: No rush. Eventually the right piece will present itself.

speaker: Connor
en: As you wish.

speaker: Achilles
en: There's a chest in a cave on the edge of the property, could you retrieve it for me? I would go myself but these old bones prevent me from getting to it. Take Norris with you; the cave entrance is blocked with heavy stone and will need to be cleared one way or another.

speaker: Connor
en: Norris. I am going to fetch something for the old man and he told me there might be some stone that requires clearing.

speaker: Norris
en: Yah? I will bring my explosifs (explosives).

speaker: Norris
en: Myriam is interesting.

speaker: Connor
en: Certainly not your typical colonial woman. A deadly shot.

speaker: Norris
en: She brought down that cougar! She is strong. Capable. She has no husband?

speaker: Connor
en: Not that I am aware of.

speaker: Norris
en: I never met a woman like her before. I would like to know her better.

speaker: Connor
en: You should speak to her then.

speaker: Norris
en: I might try. Hey! Don't splash, don't want to get the powder wet. Do you think she likes French men?

speaker: Connor
en: I see why he encouraged me to enlist your services.

speaker: Norris
en: Pas de probléme. (No problem.) We blow it up. Be my guest. Duck and cover.

speaker: Norris
en: Ha! That's a nice one!

speaker: Connor
en: Thank you.

speaker: Norris
en: Bienvenue. (You're welcome.) Doesn't look safe in there. Be careful. I'll be at the mine. What you said about Myriam is interesting...

speaker: Connor
en: That was close.

speaker: Connor
en: I have what you asked for. But I must know– who put it there and for what purpose?

speaker: Achilles
en: I did. I put it somewhere I knew only I could reach, but that was a long time ago.

speaker: Connor
en: Who does THAT belong to?

speaker: Achilles
en: These were the robes of the first Assassin to come to the colonies.

speaker: Connor
en: It is beautiful, old man.

speaker: Achilles
en: It is. I've found a painting for the space above the mantel. It's being held in New York. If you get a moment, I'd like you to pick it up for me.

speaker: Connor
en: Certainly.

speaker: Achilles
en: Good—it may not be there as the house where it was stored lay in the path of the great fire. If so, worry not.

speaker: Connor
en: It would have burned had it not been here. Achilles will be pleased.

speaker: Connor
en: I have the painting you sent me for. Would you like some help hanging it?

speaker: Achilles
en: Maybe not just yet.

speaker: Recruiter
en: Welcome to the Regulars. The most feared, respected and revered fighting force on God's green earth. Some of you are here by choice, others not. Regardless of the circumstances of your joining us, you are all brothers now. And the only way you have a chance of surviving is if you trust your brothers. One weak link can kill a whole squad on the field. I want you to think about that long and hard.

speaker: Clipper
en: That's one of them that's responsible for this - rounding up the young ones and shipping them off. We need to put an end to it.

speaker: Connor
en: What is your plan?

speaker: Clipper
en: Kill him, then the rest and set all them boys free?

speaker: Connor
en: It's a good plan but it lacks detail. How is your aim with that rifle?

speaker: Clipper
en: Can pop a muskrat's head from a quarter mile nine times outa ten - and the ten's a misfire.

speaker: Connor
en: That should do. Cover me up from up there.

speaker: Recruiter
en: The lot of you will be getting on that ship, heading for a different sort of training. Understand? You've been selected, not for your talents or fighting prowess, but because of the way you think. You will soon find out what all this means, but know it is a great honor. Some of you won't make it. Others will rise to new heights. Either way, you will give your life to a new cause.

speaker: Connor
en: We Assassins strive for peace through freedom. And the Templars - they want only to control.

speaker: Clipper
en: Well, I'm for freedom, I know that much. If your Order needs a good rifle, sign me up.

speaker: Merchant
en: Another one. Alright, let's get it over with, then. Won't get far with me on my feet. Try and get me down. Standing toe-to-toe? This is easy.

speaker: Merchant
en: Oof! That smarts.

speaker: A Midnight Engagement
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ratonhnhaké:ton's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Connor
en: William Johnson is dead—and with him the Templar plot to steal the land of my people. But in ending this threat, I have revealed another. On his body was a letter addressed to John Pitcairn, containing orders to root out and destroy Patriot weapons and supplies. Should he succeed in this, the colonists will be unable to maintain their resistance and the Templars will surely take control. So long as Pitcairn lives, the danger remains. I need to find him. He needs to die.

speaker: Connor
en: I thought it might bring clarity. Or instill a sense of accomplishment. But all I feel is regret.

speaker: Achilles
en: Hold fast to that. Such sacrifices must never come lightly.

speaker: Connor
en: I had to do it. Not only for my people, but for all the others Johnson would have harmed.

speaker: Achilles
en: It's a start. But to truly be free of Templar influence, all of them must be dealt with in turn. Even your father.

speaker: Connor
en: I know.

speaker: Achilles
en: You speak the words, but do you believe them? Seems we've company.

speaker: Connor
en: What is it?

speaker: Achilles
en: A request for aid from Paul Revere. Seems the Redcoats are up to something in Boston. Guess you made an impression on the Sons of Liberty.

speaker: Connor
en: They mistake me for one of their own. Please tell Mister Revere he has my sympathies, but I cannot help at present.

speaker: Achilles
en: You might wish to reconsider: John Pitcairn is mentioned by name.

speaker: Connor
en: Where am I to go?

speaker: Courier
en: Mister Revere's house in Boston. If you'd like I can...

speaker: Revere
en: Ah, Connor. What a relief! You came! Allow me to... to introduce you to William Dawes and Robert Newman.

speaker: Connor
en: Your letter said John Pitcairn was here.

speaker: Revere
en: Aye. He's readying an assault on Lexington, where Adams and Hancock have taken shelter. After that, he will march on Concord—hoping to destroy our weapons and supplies. You must help us!

speaker: Connor
en: Only tell me where to find him and I will put a stop to this.

speaker: Revere
en: He has dozens, if not hundreds, of soldiers at his command. You cannot hope to match him by yourself. But fear not—for you will not have to! We have an entire army of our own—merely awaiting the order to take up arms.

speaker: Connor
en: Then you must call upon them.

speaker: Revere
en: Indeed, you and I will cross the and rouse the boys. William, I need you to take the overland route and do the same. Robert, I need you up in Christ Church. Light the signal. Two lanterns—our enemy comes by sea! No time for dawdling, my friend! We have lives to save. Come on!

speaker: Revere
en: Ah. They've only left a single horse. We'll have to ride together.

speaker: Revere
en: Ah, you take the reins. I'll navigate. Quickly, Connor! Get on the horse. I'll guide you towards those we need to alert! Follow my directions and we'll be done in no time!

speaker: Revere
en: None of this looks familiar. Wrong way, Connor. Something is wrong. We are off course. Give me a moment and I will get my bearings. Hmmm. This is not right... Turn back, Connor - —you're going the wrong way. No. Wrong place. Where are we? This is all wrong... Hmmm. No. Turn around. Where we want to go is behind us. We've gotten lost somehow. I have made this crossing a dozen times—why is everything suddenly so foreign? Pressure must be getting to me. Oh bother. Everything looks the same at night... Does any of this look familiar to you, Connor? Not here, Connor. Left. To the left, Connor. Go left up here. Turn right. Go right, Connor. To the right, Connor, to the right! I believe we are on course. Excellent! We are right on course. This way, Connor. Yes, this is exactly where we need to be! Keep going. Yes! This is it! This is the way!

speaker: Revere
en: Redcoats! What are they doing here?

speaker: Connor
en: They must be scouts.

speaker: Revere
en: Be careful Connor. We mustn't let them warn the others!

speaker: Revere
en: Might be safer if we approach the houses on foot. Let us continue the search on foot... This is it. You have got the right place.

speaker: Revere
en: Let everyone know that the Regulars march for Lexington and Concord.

speaker: Rebel
en: The British are coming!

speaker: Revere
en: Back in the saddle, my friend. We have more people to warn.

speaker: Revere
en: Did you hear that? Could be Redcoats. Careful. Careful, Connor. There might be other scouts around. Be on the lookout for Redcoats...

speaker: Revere
en: Might be safer if we approach the houses on foot. This is it. You have got the right place.

speaker: Revere
en: Spread the word! The Regulars are coming out.

speaker: Rebel
en: At once!

speaker: Revere
en: We should dismount for this. It'll be quicker and quieter. This is it. You have got the right place.

speaker: Revere
en: The regulars are coming!

speaker: Redcoat
en: Here. WE'RE HERE. GET THEM!

speaker: Revere
en: Find a way to get rid of them, Connor! Faster! We need to get away from them! We need to lose them! We've gotta shake those redcoats!

speaker: Revere
en: That was much too close for comfort. Let us take care to avoid any further surprises...

speaker: Revere
en: Might be safer if we approach the houses on foot. This is it. You have got the right place.

speaker: Revere
en: Where the devil is he?

speaker: Connor
en: Are you sure we are in the right place?

speaker: Revere
en: Sure I'm sure! Prescott?

speaker: Prescott
en: Evening, gents.

speaker: Revere
en: Listen, the Regulars are out. You need to rally your men... And put on some trousers!

speaker: Prescott
en: At once.

speaker: Revere
en: Welcome to Lexington, Connor. Now let's find Hancock and Adams. Hmmm. No sign of Dawes. I hope he's alright.

speaker: Adams
en: Paul. Connor. Good to see you.

speaker: Connor
en: You need to leave. The Redcoats are coming.

speaker: Adams
en: Aye, so William's told us. Let them conduct their little search. They'll find nothing.

speaker: Connor
en: You don't understand. Pitcairn intends to kill you.

speaker: Revere
en: I'm afraid it's true.

speaker: Adams
en: I suppose we have no choice then, but to go. What of you three?

speaker: Revere
en: Dawes and I will continue on to Concord. Connor, it's best you stay here and help our man John Parker hold the town. It'll give us time to spread the word.

speaker: Connor
en: Winter approaches. The air is still and sharp with grim expectation. The others sense it too, and go about their work with uncommon urgency. I would like to help them, but more pressing matters now demand my attention. The Templars have targeted George Washington directly—and will not rest until he is dead. I had hoped to shield him from this knowledge, but Thomas Hickey ended any hope I had of staying silent. And so I have resolved to share everything I know—of the Templars and their plots—of who I really am. Achilles finds fault in this, and we argue every day. But there is simply too much now at stake to maintain restraint.

speaker: Achilles
en: Don't do this, Connor!

speaker: Connor
en: Then what would you propose we do? Sit and watch while the Templars take control? We are sworn to stop them. Or have you forgotten?

speaker: Achilles
en: Assassins are meant to be quiet. Precise. We do not go announcing conspiracies from the rooftops to all who pass by.

speaker: Connor
en: Who are you to lecture anyone? You locked yourself away in this crumbling heap and gave up on the Brotherhood entirely. Since the day I arrived, you've done nothing but discourage me. And on the rare occasions you've chosen to help you've done so little, you may as well have done nothing at all.

speaker: Achilles
en: How dare you!

speaker: Connor
en: Then tell me. On whose watch did the brotherhood falter? Whose inaction allowed the Templar Order to grow so large that it now controls an entire nation!

speaker: Achilles
en: If I sought to dissuade you, it was because you knew nothing! If I was reluctant to contribute, it was because you were naïve. A thousand times you would have died and take God knows how many with you. Let me tell you something, Connor: Life is not a fairy tale and there are no happy endings.

speaker: Connor
en: No. Not when men like you are left in charge.

speaker: Achilles
en: In your haste to save the world, boy—take care you don't destroy it!

speaker: Connor
en: Commander.

speaker: Washington
en: Connor.

speaker: Connor
en: Any word on Lee?

speaker: Washington
en: Not yet. My apologies, I've been distracted. Supply caravans meant for the camp have gone missing. I suspect treachery. A traitor named Benjamin Church, recently released from prison, has vanished as well. The two events are surely related.

speaker: Connor
en: What was his crime?

speaker: Washington
en: He was caught sending letters to the Loyalists detailing our troop strength. He claimed it was a scare tactic, that we might avoid war. A poor lie.

speaker: Connor
en: I will find Church for you.

speaker: Washington
en: Why? What reason have you to help?

speaker: Connor
en: Does it matter?

speaker: Washington
en: As you wish. We've received reports of trouble along the southern road. Might be he's responsible. I suggest you begin your search there.

speaker: Connor
en: Father.

speaker: Haytham
en: Connor. Any last words?

speaker: Connor
en: Wait.

speaker: Haytham
en: A poor choice.

speaker: Connor
en: Come to check up on Church? Make sure he'd stolen enough for your British brothers?

speaker: Haytham
en: Benjamin Church is no brother of mine. No more than the Redcoats or their idiot king. I expected naïveté. But this... The Templars do not fight for the crown. We seek the same as you, boy! Freedom. Justice. Independence.

speaker: Connor
en: But...

speaker: Haytham
en: Hmmm! But what?

speaker: Connor
en: Johnson. Pitcairn. Hickey. They sought to steal land. To sack towns. To murder George Washington.

speaker: Haytham
en: Johnson sought to own the land that we might keep it safe. Pitcairn aimed to encourage diplomacy—which you cocked up thoroughly enough to start a god-damned war! And Hickey? George Washington is a wretched leader. He's lost nearly every battle in which he's taken part. The man's wracked with uncertainty and insecurity. Only look at Valley Forge to know my words are true. We're all be better off without him. Look, much as I'd love to spar with you, Benjamin Church's mouth is as big as his ego. You clearly want the supplies he's stolen, I want him punished. Our interests are aligned.

speaker: Connor
en: What do you propose?

speaker: Haytham
en: A truce. Perhaps... perhaps some time together might do us good. You are my son, after all, and might still be saved from your ignorance. I can kill you now if you'd prefer? Excellent! Shall we be off?

speaker: Connor
en: Do you even know where Benjamin Church has gone?

speaker: Haytham
en: I'm afraid not. I'd hoped to ambush him when he or one of his men returned here. It seems I'm too late. They've come and cleared the place out.

speaker: Connor
en: I may be able to track him.

speaker: Connor
en: There were rations inside the crates. Medical supplies and clothing as well. Snow has obscured the tracks, but enough remains that we can still follow.

speaker: Driver
en: Just my luck... Going to freeze to death if I don't get this fixed...

speaker: Connor
en: Are you Ben Church's man?

speaker: Haytham
en: Well played.

speaker: Connor
en: It was not wise to run.

speaker: Driver
en: W-what do you want?

speaker: Connor
en: Where is Benjamin Church?

speaker: Driver
en: I don't know! We was riding for a camp just north of here. It's where we normally unload the cargo. Maybe you'll find him th

speaker: Haytham
en: Enough of that.

speaker: Connor
en: You did not have to kill him.

speaker: Haytham
en: Let's not waste time with all this pointless banter. Go catch up with the rest of Church's men. Infiltrate that camp of theirs and see what you can discover.

speaker: Connor
en: What about you?

speaker: Haytham
en: Never you mind. Just do as I ask.

speaker: Driver
en: Was a good haul today. Saw a bit of gunpowder in those crates. We'll get extra for that.

speaker: Man
en: Aye. Church'll be pleased and we'll be rich.

speaker: Driver
en: I almost feel sorry for the Yanks, shiverin' and starvin' out there. It's a hard way to go.

speaker: Man
en: All they need to do is raise the white flag.

speaker: Driver
en: They shoulda done that a long time ago. All this fighting serves no purpose. The Crown's sure to win in the end. To waste all these lives chasing a fool notion... Breaks my heart, it does.

speaker: Driver
en: Alright, looks to be in order.

speaker: Man
en: Go and see the foreman. There's another run planned for tonight. I'll go bring the wagon and meet up with you later.

speaker: Driver
en: Oi! Where's the foreman?

speaker: Man
en: Center of camp, near the tree. Can't miss him.

speaker: Driver
en: Thank you kindly.

speaker: Man
en: Won't be thanking me when you hear what he's got planned...

speaker: Rotting Tooth
en: About time you showed up! Listen here. Boss wants us to try something new tonight. A raid. No more convoys. We're to steal from the Yank camp itself.

speaker: Driver
en: Valley Forge?

speaker: Rotting Tooth
en: That's right.

speaker: Driver
en: You sure about this?

speaker: Rotting Tooth
en: It's not my business to be sure or not sure! I just do as Church asks. If you're so concerned, take it up with him.

speaker: Driver
en: Is he here?

speaker: Rotting Tooth
en: Course not. Hiding in New York the last I heard, trying to keep a low profile—what on account of him not wanting to go back to jail and all.

speaker: Driver
en: Alright. I'm in.

speaker: Rotting Tooth
en: Course you are.

speaker: Man
en: Look what we found!

speaker: Man
en: He was creepin' round the camp all suspicious-like.

speaker: Man
en: Must be a Yank spy!

speaker: Rotting Tooth
en: No. He's something else. Something special. Isn't that right, Haytham? Church told me ALL about you.

speaker: Haytham
en: Then you should know better than this.

speaker: Rotting Tooth
en: You're not really in a position to be makin' threats are ya?

speaker: Haytham
en: Not yet.

speaker: Haytham
en: Once you've dealt with these louts, meet me in New York.

speaker: Connor
en: What? You mean to just leave? Now?

speaker: Haytham
en: If you can't handle a couple of mercenaries then we've really no business working together.

speaker: Connor
en: Unbelievable.

speaker: Boone
en: I'm not one for sailing but I know it's out there. Some call it a kraken, others just a sea monster. They say it's fifty feet long if it's an inch and it rolls ships for sport. You won't find me out on the high seas searching for the beast, that's a guarantee I can give you, but it's a riddle that needs solving.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: You seen the serpent?

speaker: Civilian 2
en: You bet your arse I've seen the serpent. Thing was horrifying.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Where was it?

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Just out past the breakwater. Came up to the surface to have a look then plunged right back down again. The parts I saw was thirty feet, who knows how much remained under water?

speaker: Civilian 3
en: Jack says there's an old man that's always around when the beast appears.

speaker: Civilian 4
en: Jack's say a lot of things.

speaker: Civilian 3
en: But this be one I believe. They say he commands the thing.

speaker: Civilian 4
en: Pfff. Some old man ordering a kraken about. What a bunch o' fluff.

speaker: Civilian 3
en: Dunno, mate. A lot o' men I trust spin the same yarn.

speaker: Civilian 5
en: You hear the serpent weaver died?

speaker: Civilian 6
en: The ol' thief's buried not far from here. Man was a blight. Good riddance.

speaker: Civilian 7
en: That old fellow people said called the kraken bought the farm not long ago. Nobody's seen the beast since.

speaker: Civilian 8
en: So it was true then!

speaker: Civilian 7
en: Didn't say that. Maybe you could ask his widow, she won't leave his grave.

speaker: Widow
en: You come to pay your respects? You're the first. He didn't have many friends. People just didn't understand. He was a good trader. He was a good husband. I never wanted for anything.

speaker: Jacob
en: So you are the man taking up arms in our part of the city. Glad to be hearing it.

speaker: Connor
en: The military seems to be controlling this area.

speaker: Jacob
en: Yah. Martial law has been declared. For what purposes, I do not know, but there is not a need. I do what I can, but it is hard.

speaker: Connor
en: I may be able to help.

speaker: Jacob
en: Very well. I need information on the man responsible for this. He has men all over the place—corrupt Redcoats. Maybe you can get them to talk.

speaker: Jacob
en: Hallo, friend. The martial law is quite the same. You are needing to start making an impact.

speaker: Civilian
en: You must be him. I've been waiting too long. I know who the traitors are and they are bringing lists of the patriot leaders around here to the redcoats right now. Find a way to swap this fake list with the real ones and the rebellion can fight on!

speaker: Connor
en: How do I meet your commander?

speaker: Soldier
en: Won't happen. He only trusts his closest men. Even if you find him you won't get anywhere near him.

speaker: Jacob
en: Ah, the tides of change are coming in. Remain vigilant, and maybe we succeed in putting an end to this.

speaker: Deborah
en: Might I have a word? Name's Dobby Carter. Couldn't help but notice you're getting involved in the goings on in our borough. Thought we might be of service to each other.

speaker: Connor
en: What is happening here?

speaker: Deborah
en: Ever since the war kicked off, merchants have been demanding high prices "for the good of the cause". Profiteering is what that is. It's high time the folks 'round the way got a fair shake.

speaker: Connor
en: How can I help?

speaker: Deborah
en: That easy? That's a change. Eh... Set up these up nearby when you get a chance—it's part of a bigger plan I got. Come see me when you're done.

speaker: Deborah
en: Merchants are still gouging people 'round here. We'll talk again soon.

speaker: Kid
en: If you could spare a bite for us? They beat us for begging! Just distract them for a moment and we'll take what we need.

speaker: Mercenary
en: I don't much care where you find it, just get the money or you'll suffer!

speaker: Civilian
en: Darling, take the children and stay out of sight. Bloody business that was, but I thank you nonetheless. I can rest easy knowing this extortionist won't be back threatenin' my family.

speaker: Civilian
en: Mister! Please! Can you help me?

speaker: Civilian
en: Praise be to God! I was reaping my yield and these lobsterbacks attacked me. I mean only to sell my produce in the borough. Please, they sent for reinforcements when I fought back. I only need to finish the harvest and I cannot rebuff them alone.

speaker: Civilian
en: Thank you stranger! This food will sell fast at a regular price—those men have seizing everything and driving up the cost. It's not right.

speaker: Deborah
en: You certainly don't disappoint! People are standing up all over the place. We're almost there.

speaker: Jamie
en: At least you're no beast like most of these "people". Anybody who's immune has already fled. Cowards.

speaker: Connor
en: And who are you?

speaker: Jamie
en: Jamie Colley. You need to keep doing what you're doing. Nobody else is. If we both get after it, we might be able to quell this monster of a disease.

speaker: Connor
en: I will do what I can.

speaker: Jamie
en: I'll be lending a hand to these doctors. Find me once you think you've done enough and maybe we can do more.

speaker: Jamie
en: What are you talking to me for? You haven't done anything about the outbreak yet.

speaker: Kid
en: Mister? Can you help me? My father's real sick. He needs a healer. Can you carry him to one?

speaker: Civilian
en: You are a good man. The sickness just exploded out of nowhere. I hope for my boy's sake that I survive it.

speaker: Connor
en: How did you get it?

speaker: Civilian
en: Don't know. Haven't talked to anybody with it.

speaker: Civilian
en: This blanket's filthy!

speaker: Merchant
en: It's a gift from the . Be bloody grateful.

speaker: Merchant
en: If you want a blanket, get in line. If not, move.

speaker: Civilian
en: Pst! Psssst! Get out of here ya filthy mongrel!

speaker: Civilian
en: My gratitude, mister. Those dogs got the fever, I reckon. That was good of you. The pox have got everything here out of sorts.

speaker: Jamie
en: It's a start. Keep going and then we'll talk real business.

speaker: Norris
en: Connor!

speaker: Connor
en: Norris.

speaker: Norris
en: You know Myriam?

speaker: Connor
en: Of course.

speaker: Norris
en: What does she like? I want to give her a gift.

speaker: Connor
en: I really do not know...

speaker: Norris
en: Alright.

speaker: Connor
en: Let me call on Prudence. She may be of service.

speaker: Connor
en: Prudence.

speaker: Prudence
en: Good day Connor.

speaker: Connor
en: Norris is trying to-- court...a woman. What do-- you-- women, like...in terms of gifts.

speaker: Prudence
en: A nice bunch of wild flowers always brightens my day. Who is it Norris fancies?

speaker: Connor
en: Best not say for now.

speaker: Prudence
en: Fair enough. Best ones are atop the bluff to the North West. A bit tricky to get to but they grow large and healthy in the full sun.

speaker: Connor
en: Norris. Are you in there?

speaker: Norris
en: Uh, oui! (yes!)

speaker: Connor
en: Oh, I will find you a little later, then.

speaker: Norris
en: Non! Non! (No! No!) It's all right. What is it?

speaker: Connor
en: Prudence advised a bunch of wild flowers.

speaker: Norris
en: Really? Are you sure? Doesn't seem right.

speaker: Norris
en: Not the right gift. She hated them! Bad news. She did not like the flowers. She tossed them aside.

speaker: Connor
en: But Prudence was certain.

speaker: Norris
en: I knew Myriam was not the type for flowers.

speaker: Connor
en: I will uncover this mystery myself, Norris.

speaker: Norris
en: Alright. But please don't let her see you. She will think I'm bizarre.

speaker: Myriam
en: Connor? Why are you poking around my camp? What are you doing? Can I help you, Connor? Is this something to do with Norris?

speaker: Connor
en: She might appreciate a new knife. That blade has seen its prime.

speaker: Connor
en: Norris. I looked around her camp and it seems she needs a new hunting knife. The one she is using has seen better days.

speaker: Norris
en: Ah oui? (Oh yeah?) That seems more right for her...I'll think on it. Merci! (Thanks!)

speaker: Robert
en: What do you make of it?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: They all appear to be parts of the same piece of leather. "It lies under the eagle's bed, near the wolf's abode, close to a tree kissed by fire and abreast the rock that does not fit." And a route to an island. The symbols remain elusive.

speaker: Robert
en: That's Oak Island. I've sailed past it half a hundred times. A forgettable isle to say the least.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: The location seems to be the easy part.

speaker: Robert
en: Aye, and we'll be waiting for you the moment you want to get after it.

speaker: Peg Leg
en: Ya actually found somethin'? Ha ha ha!

speaker: Robert
en: I'm a little on edge, captain. The prospect of Captain Kidd's treasure and the mysteries that lie with it have me a trifle spooked.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Stay your anxiety, it is likely only treasure.

speaker: Robert
en: I thought the same thing but considering what the man went through to hide it, I'm not so sure. All those scrolls lead us to the belly of this remote island. Awful out of the way, captain. What was Kidd hidin' for cripe's sake?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I do not know, but I am intrigued to find out.

speaker: Robert
en: Remember what was written: Close to a tree kissed by fire, near the wolves abode, under the eagle's bed and the rock that does not fit—whatever that means. Do you think they might be landmarks?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: That is it. Got it. I know where it is.

speaker: Robert
en: How in the? You figured it out? Oh! That's why you're the captain!

speaker: Robert
en: That's a bloody big piece of stone. Any ideas?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Perhaps some gunpowder would move it.

speaker: Robert
en: A nice big explosion eh? Might do the job. Will do well to scare away anymore blasted wolves, that's for certain.

speaker: Robert
en: Ought to be enough.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: This is what Captain Kidd suffered over for so long. Astonishing.

speaker: Robert
en: There he is! Thought we lost ya there for a moment, captain. Are you alright?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Yes. I think so.

speaker: Robert
en: What happened down there? What did you find?

speaker: Robert
en: That's it? A single gold coin? There was nothing else? Was the cache pilfered already?

speaker: Robert
en: What the devil?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I do not know how it works but I now understand why Kidd valued it so.

speaker: Connor
en: These are troubled times. The already uneasy alliance between the Crown and its subjects frays. And behind them both the Templars plot, pulling strings and moving pieces. History dictates they seek order through control. But how will they affect it here? Who supports them? And what conspiracies have they already spun? All these things I must determine, for only by knowing my enemy can I hope to stop them.

speaker: Achilles
en: Connor. Spare a moment?

speaker: Connor
en: Of course.

speaker: Achilles
en: Have a look.

speaker: Connor
en: What is it?

speaker: Achilles
en: A Sheng Biao—or rope dart, if you prefer. One of the many plans given to us by Shao Jun to

speaker: Connor
en: Sorry.

speaker: Achilles
en: Hmmm. We'll have to work on this.

speaker: Connor
en: Kanen'tó:kon.

speaker: Connor
en: What brings you here? Is the village alright?

speaker: Connor
en: What do you mean? What has happened?

speaker: Connor
en: You must refuse!

speaker: Connor
en: You have a name? Do you know who is responsible?

speaker: Connor
en: Where is Johnson now?

speaker: Connor
en: Sale? This is theft.

speaker: Achilles
en: Connor, take care. These men are powerful.

speaker: Connor
en: What would you have me do? I made a promise to my people.

speaker: Achilles
en: If you insist upon this course of action, seek out Sam Adams in Boston. He'll be able to help.

speaker: Achilles
en: What have you done?!

speaker: Connor
en: When my people go to war, a hatchet is buried into a post to signify its start. When the threat is ended, the hatchet is removed.

speaker: Achilles
en: You could have used a tree!

speaker: Paul
en: Look, sanctions and demonstrations won't suffice, Sam. We need to ACT. And I'm talking about more than a sternly worded letter.

speaker: Samuel
en: I sympathize with your frustrations, gentlemen. But surely you can understand my reluctance to kick the hornet's nest.

speaker: Paul
en: The Tories sting no matter what we do. Might as well make it count.

speaker: Samuel
en: Ah, Connor. Hello again. What brings you to Boston?

speaker: Connor
en: You.

speaker: Samuel
en: Would you excuse us fellows?

speaker: Samuel
en: Thank you. That conversation was about to turn unpleasant. Now, what can I do for you?

speaker: Connor
en: I was hoping you could help me locate William Johnson.

speaker: Samuel
en: Of course. I'm headed to a meeting with some men who should be able to help. Why don't you come along? It's good to see the people finally taking a stand against injustice...

speaker: Connor
en: Says the man who owns a slave.

speaker: Samuel
en: Who, Surry? I practice what I preach, my friend. She's not a slave, but a freed woman... At least on paper. Men's minds are not so easily turned. It is a tragedy that for all our progress, still we cling to such barbarism.

speaker: Connor
en: Then speak out against it.

speaker: Samuel
en: We must focus first on defending our . When this is done, we'll have the luxury of addressing these other matters.

speaker: Connor
en: You speak as though your condition is equal to that of the slaves. It is not.

speaker: Samuel
en: Tell that to my neighbor—who was compelled to quarter British troops. Or to my friend who's store was closed because he displeased the Crown. The people here are no freer than Surry.

speaker: Stephane
en: Hey, it's my home no matter what you thieves called 'taxmen' say! If the gumps in Parliament, who want my property, you tell them to sail across the pond and take it themselves!

speaker: Taxman
en: It's not open for discussion! Now open this door or these men will break it down!

speaker: Redcoat
en: Bollocks! We're coming in!

speaker: Samuel
en: I trust the mounting evidence is proof enough, Connor.

speaker: Connor
en: Continue on. I shall meet you at our destination.

speaker: Stephane
en: Justice for once. I dare the Governor to send more.

speaker: Connor
en: You alright?

speaker: Stephane
en: I'm fine. It's not my first dance. For all their teeth and claws these little foxes, they fight like puppies. Thank you, my friend. I'd buy you an ale, but I'm expected somewhere else.

speaker: Samuel
en: Connor! I'd like you to meet some like-minded friends. The owner of this fine establishment, William Molineux and the manager and chef of his newest venture, Stephane Chapheau.

speaker: Stephane
en: Ah, Connor and I just had a ball with some Redcoats enforcing some taxmen outside my home!

speaker: William
en: The collectors grow bolder and more forceful. Something we must address, Samuel.

speaker: Samuel
en: Then let us raise a banner. Something to let the people know that they are not alone. The docks are an angry place of late, protesters picketing the latest shipments of British tea. The eyes of the city are upon that stage...

speaker: Stephane
en: A Bostonian without his tea is a dangerous beast!

speaker: William
en: William Johnson is smuggling the tea off the ships—one of his men tried to sell me this. A sample of what I refused, but it's from those ships—no mistaking the stamp. He's charging a King's ransom, must be he's making a mint off those who buy it.

speaker: Connor
en: Where is he now?

speaker: William
en: I've never met the man.

speaker: Samuel
en: May I ask why you seek him, Connor?

speaker: Connor
en: He intends to purchase the land upon which my village stands without the consent of my people.

speaker: Samuel
en: No doubt the revenue from his little smuggling endeavor is financing the acquisition. A tax enforced on tea grants a boon to smugglers. I'll wager the same men who levy the taxes are selling the tea. A stage requires a spectacle and I may know the play. Connor, head back to the docks and see to the destruction of the tea. If you should need us return here.

speaker: Stephane
en: Allo, Connor. That tea is being illegally smuggled all around Boston by Johnson's men. If you see any crates in transit, perhaps you could put a stop to the delivery. And those maudits (damned) tax collectors are still at it. They could use a lesson or two eh?

speaker: Connor
en: Pardon me.

speaker: Taxman
en: Aw, come on, mate.

speaker: One of a Kind
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ratonhnhaké:ton's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What was that?

speaker: Jefferson
en: My friend, Paul Revere, disappeared three days ago. This soldier just confirmed the disappearance of his wife and son as well.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I am sorry.

speaker: Jefferson
en: Revere was an able and valuable man. He was endeavouring to loosen the Bluecoat grip on the city. Neighborhood by neighborhood, he was winning the people's trust and support.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I will take up Revere's work to help rally the city. If the citizens fight for us, we will replace Washington with a new leader.

speaker: Jefferson
en: This country must be led by the people.

speaker: Franklin
en: Washington is giving a speech. We may be able to get an idea of the size of his forces. Come with me.

speaker: Washington
en: Citizens of the United States! I come before you a humbled man. As I look out upon this vast land, I see each of you suffering, yes, suffering! And striving for a better life, a better future, a better America. Each one of you sacrificing, slaving for this great country, for freedom. And I humbly say to you, your sacrifices inspire me! They shall not be in vain!

speaker: Washington
en: I know this life is difficult: the ravages of war; food shortages; crime; the burdens caused by Jefferson's seditious murderers. But we, we have a greater purpose that will unite us and lift us above these trifling troubles. For us, the obliteration of these "rebels" will be but a foretaste of the feast to come. Citizens, as I stand here, I feel the four million hearts of our nation beating within my breast. Today I announce the great project of this nation. We are mustering vast armies. We are fashioning powerful armadas. We shall soon march upon our great, dark enemy: England!

speaker: Washington
en: We shall invade her shores and irrigate her fields with blood. English bones shall provide grist for our mills, and her people shall become our slaves. Each of you shall profit from the sweat of their labors! Our nation shall rise to its proper place as the greatest of all: The Most Sovereign Kingdom - The United States of America!

speaker: Man 1
en: Down with the King!

speaker: Woman
en: Fight for Jefferson!

speaker: Man 2
en: Fight for liberty!

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: Ratonhnhaké:ton! I am happy to see you.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Hello, my friend.

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: Have you seen my brother?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I last saw him just before I climbed the Red Willow tree.

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: We were tracking Bluecoats and lost sight of each other. I am worried that he is captured.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I fear you may be right.

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: Was your Sky Journey successful?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Very successful.

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: Perhaps you can join me in the search for my brother. Any secrets you learned from your journey may be very useful.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Such a great warrior must not be lost to us.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Of course I will help you.

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: We are almost there.

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: Last I saw my brother, he was right around here.

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: This is my brother's bow. It is certain that he was here.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: This old man's body is still warm. In this weather, it cannot be more than two hours since he died.

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: During your Sky Journey, tell me, what animal called to you?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: It is difficult to talk about. But I was fortunate to meet the wolf.

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: Ah! You journeyed to a powerful place. You are fortunate.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Perhaps.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: This fire is still smoking. They were just here.

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: The Bluecoats were here! Let's keep searching.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: After the fight, the prisoners were marched up the hill.

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: You seem to have the nose of the wolves!

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: This isn't right. Could you call on your Spirit Animal? I feel we will need help.

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: I see that I was right. Your Sky Journey has given you a powerful gift. I am certain it will help our search.

speaker: Bluecoat
en: What d'ya want with me? I didn't do nothin'. Wasn't hurtin' nobody – just huntin' deer! Them other fellers're who you want.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What others?

speaker: Bluecoat
en: Buncha soldiers. I know 'em. Nasty fellers. They was roundin' up injuns over yonder.

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: One of the braves, did he have a hand marked on his face?

speaker: Bluecoat
en: You mean like a big tattoo across his chin? Yeah, I seen that feller with 'em. Hard to miss.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Take us to this camp.

speaker: Bluecoat
en: Uh, sure. Sure. Whatever you gentlemen want.

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: The wolves! Use them!

speaker: Bluecoat
en: Help me! Savages! For the love of the King, help! Someone help me! They are going to kill me!

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: Brother!

speaker: Teiowí:sonte
en: My brother!

speaker: Teiowí:sonte
en: I knew you'd find us!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: It is thanks to Ratonhnhaké:ton.

speaker: Teiowí:sonte
en: Ratonhnhaké:ton! We will make sure that these people are taken care of.

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: You should return to the Clan Mother. She will want to hear of our adventure.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I must tell the Clan Mother. I can do anything now!

speaker: Hunter
en: You wanna impress some people? Bring down the alpha wolf in these woods. He's big, fast, mean and elusive. Only a couple of men have ever seen him and I tell you they wish they didn't.

scene: The Parting of the Blue Sea
speaker: Franklin
en: Thank god you're here! The rebels saw their chance when we drew Washington to the docks. They are attacking the pyramid!

scene: The Parting of the Blue Sea
speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Their escape is cut off. They will be cut to ribbons. I must get down there!

scene: The Parting of the Blue Sea
speaker: Jefferson
en: You! Can you perform such a feat again? Washington has us completely surrounded.

scene: The Parting of the Blue Sea
speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I will hold off any reinforcements! You fight your way back to the main gate.

scene: The Parting of the Blue Sea
speaker: Jefferson
en: Fall back men! Fall back!

scene: The Parting of the Blue Sea
speaker: Jefferson
en: Bluecoats firing from above. Take them out! They're firing down on us! Take those men out! Stop those men up there!

scene: The Parting of the Blue Sea
speaker: Jefferson
en: Destroy the gates to cut them off! Cut off their reinforcements! Destroy the gates! They just keep coming! Bring down those gates!

scene: The Parting of the Blue Sea
speaker: Washington
en: What is this disturbance?

scene: The Parting of the Blue Sea
speaker: Bluecoat
en: Your Highness. Some of the people are attacking the pyramid.

scene: The Parting of the Blue Sea
speaker: Washington
en: People. Attacking. ... I am the people.

scene: The Parting of the Blue Sea
speaker: Bluecoat
en: Yes, my Liege.

scene: The Parting of the Blue Sea
speaker: Washington
en: I am the people. I have given myself to the cause of freedom. Do they not see? I have sacrificed my entire life for them. Defeated the English! Gave them liberty! Me! And yet still they rebel! This is madness.

scene: The Parting of the Blue Sea
speaker: Bluecoat
en: You are our beacon, Your Highness.

scene: The Parting of the Blue Sea
speaker: Jefferson
en: You've saved my men. We must all scatter and disappear into the city. Who are you?

scene: The Parting of the Blue Sea
speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Ratonhnhaké:ton.

scene: The Parting of the Blue Sea
speaker: Jefferson
en: A pleasure, sir. We will meet later and plan our next move.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Oiá:ner!

speaker: Oiá:ner
en: Ratonhnhaké:ton. Arnold's men followed your trail back here. Your brothers fought well but there were too many.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I thought the tea...

speaker: Oiá:ner
en: Gives strength, not immortality.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: It gives me life! I've never felt anything like it!

speaker: Oiá:ner
en: You must be careful. Respect the power of the tea, Ratonhnhaké:ton. Your mother was right to worry about the danger.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I'm certain I can defeat anyone!

speaker: Oiá:ner
en: Good. First kill Arnold and stop the destruction here. Then kill Washington. You must succeed. Ratonhnhaké:ton. If not you...nobody.

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: Each man is as mad as the next. Putnam gutted a man yesterday for having dirt in his musket. I'm all for weeding out the weak but this is something else entirely. Be careful lad, we're on the right side but that doesn't mean we're safe.

speaker: Bluecoat 2
en: We dealt with those savages like we was supposed to. Tough as nails, they was. But we brought them down. Felt good. We have nothing to worry about.

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: Don't be so sure. We've got one more day in this place before we're relieved. And then it's off to the Valley Forge awaiting orders from Commander Putnam.

speaker: Bluecoat 2
en: Where's Arnold then?

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: He gone off into some sort of seclusion until the King sets his plans. Putnam is acting commander until Arnold comes back.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I would help you with your people, but I must get to Valley Forge.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: No need, but if I see you there, I will be happy for your help.

speaker: Hunter
en: Another hunter came through a few days ago telling a story I've heard before – fifteen point buck that's impervious to musket shot. They hit him every time but every time the big fella just gets right back up. I reckon a blade to his throat would do the job but he's hard to get close to.

speaker: Paving the Way
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ratonhnhaké:ton's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Bunyon
en: Here for a scrap? Let's get on with it, then.

speaker: Bunyon
en: You want a chance? You gotta hit me! Come on! Swing at me some more! Won't get far hitting me like that!

speaker: Bunyon
en: Right on my arse!

speaker: Franklin
en: Sam and Kanen'tó:kon have gone with what's left of the men to Boston Neck. I hope they make it.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: We should join them as soon as we can.

speaker: Franklin
en: First, I must melt this down. Then I need the diagram of my design. I left it with an officer as a kind of insurance policy. He can almost always be found at the tavern. Get that and I can file this shape to the correct precision.

speaker: Bluecoats
en: Look at that outfit. The likes of him don't belong in here. I prefer to drink without fellas like him around.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Benjamin Franklin sent me to you.

speaker: Officer
en: Sorry, my friend. You want something, you've got to beat me.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I do not have a lot of time.

speaker: Officer
en: That's my condition.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Very well, but let's make it quick.

speaker: Officer
en: Did you hear about the little fracas went down tonight? It was quite a battle. 'Battle' is bein' generous. More like a massacre. Bunch a' fellers got suckered by Putnam. Pretty funny.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What do you mean, got suckered?

speaker: Officer
en: Shootin' fish in a barrel, really. Dumb fish.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What are you talking about?

speaker: Officer
en: Putnam started a rumor that the Captain of the Guard was friendly to the rebels. Hilarious.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What!?

speaker: Officer
en: Yep. ol' Putnam tricked those Redcoats into comin' out all in a group to Boston Neck, then just mowed those stupid saps down.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Do you know this for a fact?

speaker: Officer
en: I was there. I saw ol' Adams take his last breath. Samuel Adams, hit the ground like a sack of flour. Fought back like a sack, too, frankly. Pleasure see him sent off to Hades.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: That's it!

speaker: Bluecoat
en: Get 'im, boys!

speaker: Bartender
en: Good riddance to those louts! They never paid anyway.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Was that checker player telling the truth? Did Adams run into a trap? I must find out.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Kanen'tó:kon's tomahawk! Are these ... are these his fingers?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: That's from Sam's uniform. Dried blood.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I have to be certain. Someone must have seen this.

speaker: Witness
en: Terrible, it was. Terrible! The rebels were overwhelmed, outnumbered four to one. I never seen such slaughter. Piteous, piteous slaughter.

speaker: Putnam
en: Fire!

speaker: Prudence
en: Oh, Connor. Do you have a moment?

speaker: Connor
en: What is it, Prudence?

speaker: Prudence
en: I feel silly bothering you with this, but Warren's taken our yield to market in Boston. Could you round up the livestock for me? I've tried but, this baby in my belly takes the wind out of me.

speaker: Connor
en: Of course. I will see to it.

speaker: Connor
en: Hip hip! This way! Not there... Faster than they look. The things I do for this place. Come on! Get in the pen!

speaker: Prudence
en: Thank you Connor. I could never have managed that.

speaker: Connor
en: It was my pleasure. Are you well?

speaker: Prudence
en: I am. And I couldn't be happier. Warren and I have been waiting a long time for this. And if truth be told, we could not dream of a better place to raise our family.

speaker: Bluecoat
en: Our beacon! ... Yes, yes. Our beacon. It watches over us. We love our King. He watches over ... us!

speaker: Putnam
en: I've got a present for you, Your Highness.

speaker: Washington
en: A present?

speaker: Putnam
en: I think you'll be rather pleased.

speaker: Washington
en: How very thoughtful, Putnam. Do you know any of this, Mister Franklin?

speaker: Franklin
en: No, it's news to me. What sort of present, General Putnam?

speaker: Putnam
en: The best sort. Come see!

speaker: Putnam
en: Rouse him!

speaker: Putnam
en: It's the one you blasted point blank in the village, sire.

speaker: Washington
en: Really? He survived? Remarkable.

speaker: Franklin
en: Yes, well, I've captured one myself, sire. In the next cell. A savage who joined that traitor, Sam Adams.

speaker: Washington
en: Have them both beheaded, along with a score of citizens taken at random, as an example to all.

speaker: Franklin
en: Random citizens? Isn't that rather harsh, Your Majesty?

speaker: Washington
en: "Harsh," sir!? Is it harsh to defend our freedoms? Is it harsh to extinguish those who would enslave us? Mr. Franklin, I suggest you examine your commitment to the cause, sir!

speaker: Franklin
en: Yes, yes, of course, Your Majesty.

speaker: Washington
en: Have the scaffolds made ready.

speaker: Franklin
en: My Liege.

speaker: Washington
en: Putnam, I fear Mr. Franklin is going soft. See to it that this so-called rebellion is crushed, and I'll consider rearranging just who is in charge.

speaker: Putnam
en: I already have a plan, My Lord.

speaker: Washington
en: As for you... Let's see how you survive with the loss of your head! Eh? Carry on, Putnam!

speaker: Putnam
en: Yes, Your Highness.

speaker: Putnam
en: Stay sharp, soldier!

speaker: Bluecoat
en: Over us, he watches. Our beacon watches. Our beacon watching over us. Our beacon, our beacon. He is.

speaker: Bluecoat
en: Don't you dare try anything! I've got my eye on you, I do.

speaker: Bluecoat
en: You'll have a nice view tomorrow, with your head up high on a pike and all!

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: Help! He's escaped! I need help!

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: Shut up, you! Help!

speaker: Bluecoat 2
en: What's happened?

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: He was here, then gone! There must be a hole or something.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Kanen'tó:kon! Alive? ... Oh, my friend, I cannot believe you're here!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: The Clan Mother brought me to health. Kanen'tó:kon, I was unable to protect my mother. I was unable to save the village.

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: We're locked in!

speaker: Bluecoat 2
en: How'd you let that happen?

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: It wasn't me!

speaker: Bluecoat 2
en: Christ! The King'll have our heads for this.

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: But he watches over us!

speaker: Bluecoat 2
en: Shut it, would ya!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: This is not everything.

speaker: Bluecoat 1
en: Help! He's escaped! I need help!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Wait here. I will let you through when it is clear.

speaker: Bluecoat 3
en: General Putnam is on another tear.

speaker: Bluecoat 4
en: Best to lay low.

speaker: Bluecoat 3
en: Had a man whipped for not shaving properly.

speaker: Bluecoat 4
en: That fellow got off easy.

speaker: Bluecoat 5
en: The King himself, here in Boston!

speaker: Bluecoat 6
en: Makes me nervous.

speaker: Bluecoat 5
en: It's our chance to distinguish ourselves in his eyes!

speaker: Bluecoat 6
en: Makes me very nervous.

speaker: Bluecoat 7
en: I'm in a pickle.

speaker: Bluecoat 8
en: How's that?

speaker: Bluecoat 7
en: Commander Franklin wants curfew imposed at ten o'clock, but then General Putnam told me to start at nine.

speaker: Bluecoat 8
en: You're mincemeat, my friend.

speaker: Bluecoat 7
en: Franklin is harsh, but Putnam is crazy. I better start at nine.

speaker: Bluecoat 9
en: Look at this rubbish we brought back. Useless!

speaker: Bluecoat 10
en: It's spoils of war now!

speaker: Bluecoat 9
en: The owner put up a hell of a fight.

speaker: Bluecoat 10
en: Old black geezer with the cane?

speaker: Bluecoat 9
en: That's the fella!

speaker: David
en: Connor! You have a minute, my friend?

speaker: Norris
en: How's it coming, Big Dave? You make any progress on the knife? I would like to give it to Myriam soon.

speaker: David
en: The steel Norris smelted is something else - I've rarely seen such fine metal. Trouble is, my old tools aren't hard enough to work it. The ones I need aren't hard to find- a shop or two in New York sell them at a good price. I'd do it myself but with the Regulars after my head, I'll stay here safe and sound if I can.

speaker: Connor
en: I have matters to attend to in New York. I will see to it the next time I journey there.

speaker: David
en: Sounds good!

speaker: Guard 1
en: Captain's on a warpath for that deserter.

speaker: Guard 2
en: What's his name? 'Big Man' or some-such-thing?

speaker: Guard 1
en: Big Dave. Did in a whole unit escaping, they say. Big Dave's in for a rough ride, seems to me.

speaker: David
en: Connor!

speaker: Connor
en: I have the tools you requested.

speaker: David
en: Ah! Excellent! I'll get right to work. Norris has been hanging around pestering me about his knife.

speaker: Connor
en: I thought you should know I overheard some Regulars talking. They are looking for you.

speaker: David
en: I imagine they are. I'll have to face them some time or another.

speaker: Jamie
en: About time you showed up.

speaker: Connor
en: What are you doing?

speaker: Doctor
en: I mean to start my inoculations. It's the most effective way to prevent the disease.

speaker: Jamie
en: Not a worry, a pity people are so damned stupid. Eh Connor?

speaker: Jamie
en: What's wrong with you?

speaker: Connor
en: An attack is coming. Are you ready for a fight?

speaker: Jamie
en: Always. You tell me where you want me and I'll make sure not a single man gets through.

speaker: Connor
en: The Assassins have long since branched out across the globe. The Colonies are no exception. The man you killed was a Templar.

speaker: Jamie
en: And here I was thinking you were helping me. I must say I'm honored. Huh. If you ever need my help again - don't hesitate.

speaker: Warren
en: Prudence! Prudence, where are you? Connor! Thank God you are here. Prudence is missing. She went out to gather some things this morning and never returned. I'm worried sick. What if she's hurt?

speaker: Connor
en: I will find her.

speaker: Warren
en: The dog might help track her down, he has a good nose. Come on, boy.

speaker: Warren
en: She has been gathering Evening Primrose almost every night. She is obsessed with the oil it yields. That is all going to stop now. I don't understand why she wants so damned much of the stuff!

speaker: Warren
en: She picked some here. She can't be far. We should split up to cover more ground.

speaker: Warren
en: Connor! Anything yet?! Prudence! Prudence! Where are you?!

speaker: Prudence
en: Help! Please! Somebody help me!

speaker: Prudence
en: Connor! Oh thank God! Please help me!

speaker: Prudence
en: Thank you so much, Connor. Thank you. I don't want to think of what might have happened if you'd not arrived. I saw some primrose growing there and the bear just came charging at me.

speaker: Connor
en: Why are you gathering primrose?

speaker: Prudence
en: Well. Warren and I have been trying to conceive a child for a – long time now. I read that evening primrose encourages fertility. I'm sorry. This is not a proper conversation given the circumstance.

speaker: Connor
en: I understand. Not another word on the matter.

speaker: Warren
en: Prudence! Are you alright, my love?!

speaker: Prudence
en: I'll be fine, thanks to Connor.

speaker: Warren
en: Thank you, Connor. Once again.

speaker: Guard
en: Up! Up with ya! I said GET UP! Walk.

speaker: Prisoner
en: Bye now!

speaker: Hickey
en: Ello Connor. Didn't think I'd miss your goin' away party, did ya? I hear Washington 'imself will be in attendance. Hope nuttin' bad 'appens to him.

speaker: Connor
en: You said there'd be a trial!

speaker: Hickey
en: Ah, no trials for traitors, I'm afraid. Lee an' Haytham saw to that. It's straight to the gallows for you!

speaker: Connor
en: I will not die today. The same cannot be said for you.

speaker: Guard
en: That's enough! Keep moving!

speaker: Achilles
en: You are not alone. Only give a cry when you need us...

speaker: Connor
en: Forget about me—you need to stop Hickey. He's

en: Your mother was a fool. Full of ideals and bull-headed. Now that King George's power has been threatened, he is making slaves of everyone! Ratonhnhaké:ton, it falls to you to make good on your mother's mistake. Journey to the Great Willow, climb her, retrieve the virgin boughs in her canopy. Drink their essence and gain the power to fight, to bring down this mad King George.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What power?

speaker: Oiá:ner
en: Gather your strength and I will show you.

speaker: Oiá:ner
en: You are ready. The Great Willow at the top of the mountain.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Yes. I will return with the boughs and perhaps some fresh meat to cook.

speaker: Oiá:ner
en: Never mind the meat. Just bring back the branches, boil them in water and drink the tea. Only then will you be ready to return and fight back with your brothers.

speaker: Teiowí:sonte
en: Drink her strength. Become one of us.

speaker: Oiá:ner
en: Leave no tracks leading here upon your return. Go.

speaker: Teiowí:sonte
en: I will meet you at the Red Willow tree.

speaker: Teiowí:sonte
en: You are on your own now.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: How dangerous is it?

speaker: Teiowí:sonte
en: Each journey to the Sky World is unlike any other. For some it is very dangerous. You will find your answers are at the very top of the willow.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I am sorry, Mother. I must speak to Washington, to make sense of this. It is the only way.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Was it just a dream? Could I... Could I actually ...?

speaker: Bluecoat
en: You best stop moving.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: My tomahawk! They have taken it! I shall enjoy getting it back.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: No one can stop me with such a power!

speaker: Franklin
en: He wanted to atone for what he'd done. ... He saved my life. And very nearly killed Washington.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: It will take more than a tomahawk.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: It will take great power.

speaker: Franklin
en: We do have this.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Useless.

speaker: Franklin
en: Don't be foolish.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: That trinket only opens doors!

speaker: Franklin
en: What are you doing?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: The Animal Spirits know things we do not know. If I journey to them, they may teach me.

speaker: Franklin
en: Are you all right?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Keep watch.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Why have you returned to this place? I weep for you, my son. Can you not see that you are lost?! You have defied me! You ignore my last wish! I cannot forgive you, my son.

speaker: Washington
en: You cannot match my power. I am freedom itself!

speaker: Washington
en: This time, I'll make certain of your death.

speaker: Franklin
en: You were feverish. What's happened to your eyes?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: We must separate to search out Jefferson and the rebellion.

speaker: Franklin
en: Very well.

speaker: Lyle
en: Connor, might I have a word?

speaker: Connor
en: What do you think of our little plot of land, Doctor?

speaker: Lyle
