en: It's quite beautiful. I'm grateful you found me. But to be truthful people outside our community still avoid me like the bloody plague. It baffled me for a time but then a courier delivered this to me. Before you found me the British demanded I not treat Patriots nor their supporters. I refused so they set about destroying my business. This tells me their smear campaign is still very much in effect. If things don't change, I may be forced to leave.

speaker: Connor
en: We need you here. I will do what I can to end this defamation.

speaker: Lyle
en: You might start by finding the courier who brought this to me. He works out of Boston.

speaker: Connor
en: I am here on behalf of Doctor White. It is time the campaign against him came to an end. Who is selling the papers that slander him?

speaker: Courier
en: You won't find argument from me—Doc Lyle healed my leg, good as new. The pamphlets are being distributed by a few paper boys around Boston.

speaker: Paper boy 1
en: Dr. Death! Get the news on Dr. Death!

speaker: Paper boy 1
en: I'll take that if you're giving it.

speaker: Paper boy 2
en: White Death! Come for healing, leave in a box!

speaker: Paper boy 2
en: Thanks mister. It's less than I get for this, though.

speaker: Paper boy 3
en: You've heard about him! Now read about him! The Doctor with a Grim touch!

speaker: Paper boy 3
en: It's not much but very kind of you.

speaker: Paper boy 4
en: Inform your families of White Death!

speaker: Connor
en: Where is the man printing these pamphlets?

speaker: Paper boy 4
en: Look, mister, there's a man who pays me to hand these papers out. So long as he's dolling the coin I'll be doing what he asks.

speaker: Connor
en: You will not distribute these pamphlets any longer. Understood?

speaker: Smuggler
en: I trust you're here for a tussle. I'll give you what you want.

speaker: Smuggler
en: Now!

speaker: Smuggler
en: Impressive. Very impressive.

speaker: Connor
en: My enemy is tenacious. When money failed them, they took to force. But I have slain Johnson and Pitcairn both, ending their plots. George Washington now rallies the colonists and their march towards freedom begins in earnest. Little wonder, then, that the Templars now want him dead. They seek to reshape this land into something cold and ordered. Something soulless. And he is an obstacle. I must save him, that his cause can flourish and my people remain safe. But the more I prod, the greater the chance I am discovered. The Templars believe their men lost to the revolution. In their eyes, the Assassins are gone and scattered—no longer a threat. But I fear they will soon discover the truth and me along with it. I must tread carefully...

speaker: Achilles
en: How fares the hunt, Connor?

speaker: Connor
en: There is progress, but I worry it is not enough.

speaker: Achilles
en: You must strike where you're needed most. What if you pursued Charles Lee and your father—what then of Paul Revere? And the soldiers at Lexington?

speaker: Connor
en: Soldiers? There were no soldiers in those towns—only men and women who were forced to defend themselves.

speaker: Achilles
en: Is this not why you fight? To protect your people? Your struggle is the colonist's struggle. In helping one, you help the other.

speaker: Connor
en: Encouraging words from one who thought mine a fool's errand.

speaker: Achilles
en: Make no mistake—I still do. But I can't help but feel some pride in your success.

speaker: Connor
en: And why should I give you any credit?

speaker: Achilles
en: Then don't. But first, return the robe. And the blades. And the darts. And all of the years of training and knowledge I have bestowed upon you. Return these and then your words may have some merit.

speaker: Connor
en: Or you could just admit that you were wrong.

speaker: Achilles
en: Oh child, please. You've killed two men—one more salesmen than soldier. You're gonna have to try a lot harder than that to impress me.

speaker: Connor
en: Is that so, old man? Or perhaps we should step outside? I will gladly demonstrate how easily I could trounce y

speaker: Achilles
en: Connor, this is Benjamin Tallmadge. His father was one of us, no need for secrecy. I think he has something he wants to say.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Achilles tells me you've uncovered a plot to murder the Commander in Chief.

speaker: Connor
en: Yes. But I have only false starts and dead ends to show for it.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Not anymore, my friend. Thomas Hickey's your man—and I aim to help you catch him.

speaker: Connor
en: How?

speaker: Benjamin
en: I'll explain on the way. You and I are going to New York.

speaker: Connor
en: So what is your stake in all this?

speaker: Benjamin
en: Same as yours. Peace. Stability. A land in which all might live side by side—free and equal.

speaker: Connor
en: Why not join the brotherhood, then?

speaker: Benjamin
en: My father was an Assassin. Quite good at his job, too, as I understand it. But... I hope to have children some day. It's hard to live in two worlds at the same time. So I choose to live in one.

speaker: Connor
en: I understand.

speaker: Benjamin
en: I still contribute as I can. It's why we're here now.

speaker: Connor
en: What can you tell me of Thomas Hickey?

speaker: Benjamin
en: He has been running a counterfeiting ring in the city. Locate the source of his operation, and we can have him arrested. He cannot harm the Commander if he is in prison.

speaker: Connor
en: Do you know where he is?

speaker: Benjamin
en: Not exactly. But I have an idea where we can begin the search.

speaker: Benjamin
en: There are rumors of bad bills circulated here. No doubt they come from Thomas.

speaker: Merchant
en: What are you up to? This isn't money! It's colored paper. You've cheated me for the last time! GUARDS!

speaker: Counterfeiter
en: Oi, Daniel—best put them bills away. The guards is on to us.

speaker: Daniel
en: How? What happened?

speaker: Counterfeiter
en: Damn shopkeep called me out! Brought the guards, but I gave them the slip.

speaker: Daniel
en: Boss is gonna be mad.

speaker: Counterfeiter
en: Not so mad as if I'd gotten caught. 'Sides, we've got most everything we need for the job, anyway.

speaker: Daniel
en: Best go tell him. I'll warn the others.

speaker: Man
en: I heard what happened at the market. Boss wants everyone back at the shop. Says we strike tonight.

speaker: Counterfeiter
en: He worried about that business with the guards? I'm telling you it's nothing. Haven't had a spot of trouble since I slipped away. Course, I'm takin' care to keep my distance.

speaker: Man
en: Can't believe we're really gonna do this.

speaker: Counterfeiter
en: We'll be heroes. The ones who ended all this talk of revolution. They'll set us up like kings, they will.

speaker: Man
en: Hmph! Revolution. Bunch a' trouble makers lookin' to upset the apple-cart cos some fool filled their heads with rubbish. Ruinin' it for the rest of us good folk.

speaker: Counterfeiter
en: Good folk? Really?

speaker: Man
en: Of course! You and me and Hickey? Just some hard-luck lads tryin' to survive in this cold, cruel world.

speaker: Thomas
en: Wot's this?

speaker: Connor
en: Thomas Hickey?

speaker: Thomas
en: Might be. What's it to ya?

speaker: Thomas
en: Ain't s'pposed to be none of your kind left. Suppose I'd best be rectifyin' that, then. Get 'im!

speaker: Soldier
en: There's another one! Grab 'im!

speaker: Connor
en: Be still. You will do no more harm.

speaker: Thomas
en: Your a right fool, meddlin' in affairs you know nuttin' about.

speaker: Connor
en: Washington's the only thing keeping the Continental Army together. You kill him—and you end all hope for freedom.

speaker: Thomas
en: Wrong, boy-o. Wit 'im gone, they'd have no choice but to promote Lee. And then

speaker: Soldier
en: You are both under arrest.

speaker: Thomas
en: Ah well, we were just havin' a scrap, officer! Ain't nuttin' wrong with two men settlin' their differences the ol' fashi'n way. Can't we come to

speaker: Connor
en: Quiet! What are the charges?

speaker: Soldier
en: Counterfeiting.

speaker: Connor
en: I had nothing to do with that!

speaker: Soldier
en: Course not.

speaker: Connor
en: Listen—there are more important things at stake here. This man is planning to

speaker: Clan Mother
en: I know you wonder why it is we do not wander from these woods. Why it is we do not join the other Kanien'kehá:ka in war.

speaker: Clan Mother
en: Tonight, you will have your answers. Our village sits on sacred ground. And it is our duty—above all other things—to keep it hidden from the world.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Even if it means allowing our enemies to gain strength?

speaker: Clan Mother
en: It is a difficult position for us. We are caught between the need to act—and the knowledge that doing so endangers us.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What is so important that you would see us imprisoned by ourselves?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What is it?

speaker: Clan Mother
en: A door.

speaker: Juno
en: Greetings guardian.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Are you... a spirit?

speaker: Juno
en: You may think of me as such.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Where am I?

speaker: Juno
en: You are where you were before. If you mean to ask what it is you now see—it is known as the Nexus. From here, probabilities are calculated so that the proper path may be chosen.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What path?

speaker: Juno
en: Yours.

speaker: Juno
en: Follow me.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What have you done to me?!

speaker: Juno
en: Selected a form familiar to your culture. It is designed to ease navigation.

speaker: Juno
en: We have waited millennia for your arrival. You—who will bring to him the last piece. That he may open the door.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I do not understand.

speaker: Juno
en: Nor need you. I sense my words cause pain... But such was not my intention. You are important, child. In more ways than you will ever know. As we speak, forces gather in secret, preparing to seize control of the land.

speaker: Juno
en: If they succeed, the sanctuary will be breached.

speaker: Juno
en: Yours is a special lineage. Past. Present. Future. Many are connected to you. Many who have changed the world. Who will change the world. So too, shall you.

speaker: Juno
en: I have called you here that you might know your duty. You must protect the sanctuary from those that would undo our work.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What sanctuary? What work?

speaker: Juno
en: Maintaining your current course will result in a negative outcome.

speaker: Juno
en: Premature access will destabilize the region.

speaker: Juno
en: Your village and its people will be destroyed.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What am I to do?

speaker: Juno
en: You will learn of a man who will provide additional training. Seek this symbol.

speaker: Juno
en: No doubt you have many questions. Time will see them answered. For now, you must follow. Leading is for later.

speaker: Clan Mother
en: Where, Ratonhnhaké:ton? Where did you see that symbol?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: The spirit showed it to me. She said I would meet a man who would show me the way forward.

speaker: Clan Mother
en: Hmm.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: The men from beyond the valley will return here. I've known it for a long time now. And so have you, even if you choose to ignore it.

speaker: Clan Mother
en: We are sworn to protect this place... But you are right as well. The world is changing, and we cannot hide forever.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I will not sit here and wait for our end.

speaker: Clan Mother
en: Then I release you. You may leave.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Why have you changed your mind?

speaker: Clan Mother
en: Because I cannot change yours.

speaker: Clan Mother
en: Take this. You will find what you seek in a place to the east. It was there I saw the symbol. It was borne by a man who will surely help you, as he once helped your mother.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Thank you.

speaker: Clan Mother
en: Yours is a noble heart. But I fear you expect too much. Go. Seek your symbol. Find your way.

speaker: Benedict
en: Ah, Connor. Just the man I wanted to see. Well done capturing the traitor. But I must ask more of you. There are some kegs of powder resting inside the fort. Bring them to the magazine. Dismissed.

speaker: Benedict
en: Are you well?

speaker: John
en: As well as I can be given the circumstances. You?

speaker: Benedict
en: Same. But we're close, so very close. We need to talk about this someplace with fewer curious ears.

speaker: John
en: Has Clinton agreed?

speaker: Benedict
en: It is done. Only the matter of my compensation remains, something of the utmost importance to me. Deliver this letter. Make absolutely sure he gets it. Please be cautious. A mistake at this stage would be, unfortunate. When we come out on the other side of this thing, I'll make sure you're rewarded Major André. Generously.

speaker: John
en: You mean John Anderson, sir.

speaker: Benedict
en: Yes.

speaker: Soldier
en: Sir.

speaker: Soldier
en: Sir.

speaker: John
en: Make sure we're not followed. If anybody sees us, kill them.

speaker: John
en: That's far enough for you two. Keep a keen eye and come for me when you see the smoke.

speaker: Soldier
en: Yes sir.

speaker: Soldier
en: We'll be waiting Major André.

speaker: Soldier
en: Halt!

speaker: John
en: Gentlemen. I hope you belong to our ?

speaker: Soldier
en: What party?

speaker: John
en: The .

speaker: Soldier
en: We do.

speaker: John
en: Good. I am an officer in the British Army and must not be detained. I will chalk this mishap up to fatigue.

speaker: Soldier
en: But we ain't British, friend, and you are under arrest.

speaker: John
en: That was merely a test, and you passed. I am an officer of the Patriots in truth. Here are my papers.

speaker: Soldier
en: Rubbish. Kill him and bring his head to the Commander.

speaker: Connor
en: No! Do not kill him! Search him instead.

speaker: Soldier
en: Blessed stars. His real name is Major André and he's with the British. He carries this letter on behalf of Major General Benedict Arnold.

speaker: Soldier
en: Arnold is our commanding officer.

speaker: Connor
en: Bind André's hands immediately and bring him to Commander Washington. I will see to Arnold.

speaker: Stinger
en: We fight. You won't best me with simple attacks.

speaker: Stinger
en: You can't counter me! You are impatient. You won't best me with simple attacks.

speaker: Stinger
en: Well fought.

speaker: Printer
en: You ask a great deal of me, Sam.

speaker: Adams
en: I know... But I wouldn't be here if it wasn't important. If it wasn't vital.

speaker: Printer
en: Fine. Just this once, though. In the future, such things will come at a price. Resetting the type is neither quick nor easy. To say nothing of the cost should I be discovered...

speaker: Adams
en: I shall not forget this kindness.

speaker: Printer
en: Nor I.

speaker: Adams
en: His work will see your last little bit of notoriety erased. Come—I'll show you how to leave now that order's been restored.

speaker: Adams
en: So now you've had a chance to see how it all works. Untoward actions will upset the citizens and inevitably lead to the guards being called. Depending on the severity of your transgression, they may simply search a bit before giving up and returning to their posts. But should you offend them severely or repeatedly—they'll become much more aggressive in their pursuit. I've shown you three ways to turn the tide. Remove wanted posters, bribe town criers, or visit a printer to create your own propaganda.

speaker: Connor
en: This feels wrong. Why not just speak to someone and explain my innocence?

speaker: Adams
en: You can't be serious?

speaker: Connor
en: We counter one lie with another. Words on paper instantly taken as truth. And all of it without question.

speaker: Adams
en: THEY loosed this beast! Or have you forgotten? I merely helped you tame and turn it 'round.

speaker: Connor
en: There must be another way. Something more honest.

speaker: Adams
en: Well, when you find it, let me know. But until then, we sculpt with the clay we have!

speaker: Connor
en: My apologies. I do not mean to sound ungrateful.

speaker: Adams
en: Quite alright. I was much the same at your age. You'll grow out of it in time.

speaker: Connor
en: And if I do not? If I refuse?

speaker: Adams
en: Then you'll likely wind up dead.

speaker: Adams
en: Here we are. Speak with the harbormaster and he'll see you home.

speaker: Connor
en: Thank you for everything, Sam. I promise one day to repay the favor.

speaker: Adams
en: Oh, I'm counting on it.

speaker: Connor
en: Like this?

speaker: Man 1
en: I hear they've resolved to send the three ships back – cargo and all!

speaker: Woman
en: Aye. But Governor Hutchinson refuses to let them leave. Wants us to take the tea, pay the duties, and say thank you kindly to the king.

speaker: Man 1
en: The King can kindly kiss my arse.

speaker: Man 2
en: You'd like that, wouldn't you?

speaker: Man 1
en: You can kiss it as well!

speaker: Woman
en: Enoug! What hope have we of resisting if we're arguing amongst ourselves?

speaker: Man 3
en: If Adams keeps giving these speeches, he's apt to end up in stocks.

speaker: Man 4
en: They wouldn't dare!

speaker: Man 3
en: I've seen men punished for far less.

speaker: Man 4
en: If the Tories think that'll quiet the people, the've another thing coming. They touch a hair on his head, and he becomes a martyr.

speaker: Man 5
en: Muskets'll do what words won't!

speaker: Man 6
en: Quiet! You want to be hanged for treason?

speaker: Man 5
en: There's nothin' treasonous 'bout callin' for freedom!

speaker: Man 6
en: Tell it the king and 'is cronies.

speaker: Man 5
en: Men like Adams - they talk and talk and nothing happens. Naught will change until we ACT!

speaker: Man 6
en: Give it time.

speaker: Man 5
en: I've given more than any man should. We all have!

speaker: Connor
en: What happens now?

speaker: Molineux
en: We wait for the signal.

speaker: Connor
en: What signal?

speaker: Adams
en: This meeting can do nothing further to save the country.

speaker: Molineux
en: That one.

speaker: Adams
en: Evening gentlemen. Shall we be off?

speaker: Connor
en: No.

speaker: Adams
en: What's the matter?

speaker: Connor
en: I have spent today drawn from one bit of madness to another with nothing to show for it. Before I go any further, I would like to know exactly what it is you intend.

speaker: Adams
en: Of course. First, we make our way to Nathaniel Bradlee's house to fetch the rest of our little group. Then it's on to Griffin's Wharf, where we board the ships and dump the tea. Simple as that.

speaker: Connor
en: Simple seems a bit charitable!

speaker: Adams
en: Cheer up, Connor, for tonight we are all victors! The Sons of Liberty get to send a message to England and you rob William Johnson of his financing. Your village will be saved. I've an idea: why don't you lead the way? That should keep us out of any further trouble, am I right?

speaker: Adams
en: Dammit! More guards!

speaker: Molineux
en: We need to turn the crowd's anger to our advantage.

speaker: Stephane
en: Say the word, Connor, and I will make it so!

speaker: Revere
en: Regulars!

speaker: Stephane
en: We need to keep those bastards at bay while the tea's being dumped. Let me help. I am yours to command.

speaker: Adams
en: We've done it!

speaker: Stephane
en: Connor! We saved the last one for you.

speaker: Stephane
en: Best we get out of here, eh?

speaker: The Battle of the Wabash
en: was a genetic memory.

speaker: Known Owners
en: Little Turtle (Mihšihkinaahkwa) Current Status: Unknown This Apple of Eden only acts as an element of contention between the Natives and General St. Clair and is not expected to end up in the hands of the Witnesses during this Sequence. For this reason, the Reader can freely decide which Apple of Eden to assign to Little Turtle, choosing one among those presented in other Sequences of this book, or in the Assassin's Creed - Animus Handbook.

speaker: The Spymaster
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ratonhnhaké:ton's genetic memories stored in the Abstergo Cloud and relived by an Assassin hacker in 2023 through the Animus.

speaker: Lance
en: Hey, Connor. A word, Connor? Do you have business in New York on occasion? I only ask because I ordered a package from France and it's long overdue. I've written the post master and he's yet to respond. I thought you could inquire if you had the chance.

speaker: Connor
en: I will pass by the next time I am there.

speaker: Connor
en: I've come to inquire on a package arriving from France on behalf of Lance O'Donnell.

speaker: Post master
en: Was picked up and signed for by his apprentice a couple days back. Patrick O'Hara.

speaker: Connor
en: Patrick O'Hara is Mister O'Donnell's former apprentice. Would you happen to know where he is?

speaker: Post master
en: Sure- he's been hanging around the docks the last few days. Should be round the way.

speaker: Patrick
en: Here! Take these pages and hide them! Don't let that guy get his hands on 'em!

speaker: Connor
en: I have your plans. What are they for?

speaker: Lance
en: You got them!? This, Connor, is the design for a chair that FOLDS. Genius. You won't regret this!

speaker: Lance
en: Got a moment, Connor? Connor! I don't mean to be a bother, but I wanted to ask you something. When my cart went up in flames I lost most of my tools. I've got some spares back at my shop in Boston but as you know, I'm not really welcome around there. I thought- if it wasn't too much trouble- you could help me retrieve them?

speaker: Connor
en: What would you have me do?

speaker: Lance
en: Watch my back while I gather them. Meet me in Boston at my old shop.

speaker: Lance
en: Connor! Good to see you.

speaker: Lance
en: Been trying to avoid eye contact with my old neighbors, so far so good. Not so worried now you're here.

speaker: Connor
en: How are you doing otherwise?

speaker: Lance
en: Oh, alright I suppose. Things never really go as planned...but that's life.

speaker: Connor
en: Really, how do you mean?

speaker: Lance
en: You know, you make a plan and it all goes awry and nothing gets better, only slightly different.

speaker: Connor
en: Sounds like you have had a string of misfortune. It will pass.

speaker: Lance
en: What are you doing here?

speaker: Shop owner
en: Sweeping my steps if it please you.

speaker: Lance
en: Since when are these your steps?

speaker: Shop owner
en: Since I bought them three weeks ago.

speaker: Lance
en: From who?

speaker: Shop owner
en: The owner. Via his apprentice. Owner shipped off outta town, what's it to you?

speaker: Lance
en: I AM THE OWNER!

speaker: Shop owner
en: Not anymore, mate. Sorry. Better sort things out with your apprentice. He's often at the pub over there but I'm sure you already knew that.

speaker: Lance
en: Patrick!

speaker: Patrick
en: Lance.

speaker: Lance
en: Patrick! What gave you the right to sell my shop?!

speaker: Patrick
en: Well you were run outta town. I thought you'd never come back so I sold it all- the shop, the tools. It's rough luck. Anyway, it's been great chatting but I must be off. Have a nice life.

speaker: Lance
en: What rot. Tools are a woodworker's lifeblood, he'd never sell them. I bet he's got them stashed somewhere.

speaker: Connor
en: Then we follow him.

speaker: Patrick
en: I'll load these in the cart come night fall and be in New York free of this rubbish for good before the month is out.

speaker: Lance
en: Well that's something at least. Thank you. I still can't believe he sold my shop. I'll see you back to the homestead.

speaker: Ring
en: Shake it off! Stand tough! Can't win a fight if you can't take a hit! He's down! Chin up! Boom! Well struck! That was nothing! HAA! On his back! Yeah! Pound 'em! You've got 'em on the back foot! He's unstoppable! You can't beat him! That's my man!

speaker: Ring
en: Fight!

speaker: Ring
en: Winner!

speaker: Ring
en: Fight!

speaker: Docker
en: Uh-oh! Looks like the crowd's turned on ya! Careful now! Can never have too many friends!

speaker: Ring
en: Winner! Looks like we got a real contender!

speaker: Ring
en: Fight!

speaker: Surgeon
en: How are you feeling? Not well? You might want to hurry up. Shame you won't be standing long enough to finish the fight.

speaker: Ring
en: Dance like the best, fall like the rest!

speaker: Ring
en: Fight!

speaker: Ring
en: We have a NEW CHAMPION!

speaker: Achilles
en: I'll miss the peace and quiet. But we can certainly use the wood.

speaker: Connor
en: The manor needs a lot of work.

speaker: Achilles
en: That. And other things. Meet me at the small shack by the shoreline when you have time. There's something else you need to see.

speaker: Connor
en: What is it?

speaker: Achilles
en: An... asset.

speaker: Peg Leg
en: I found 'em! People say they's a myth but I 'ave em! Cap'n Kidd had a secret to be sure. Jus' get me a ship and a crew and we'll find out what it was he held so dear. I met 'im once – the Cap'n – he was seven feet tall if he was an inch. I tell ya. Legs like tree trunks and a smithy's arms. Almost broke my hand shakin' it hello. I could feel it then – when I met him – no weapon made by man could harm 'im.

speaker: Robert
en: GO 'WAY!

speaker: Robert
en: Said 'go way', boy. D'ya not speak the King's English? Oh, I didn't see you there, old man. I'd of set my home in order if I'd known you'd be callin'.

speaker: Achilles
en: The boy's name is Connor. He's here to restore the property.

speaker: Robert
en: Restore? ...RESTORE! Pardon my manners! She's still the fastest in the Atlantic – sure she needs some attention... minor things mostly but with a little affection she'll fly again.

speaker: Connor
en: Who is 'she'?

speaker: Robert
en: WHO is SHE? Why the Aquila, boy! The Ghost of the North Seas!

speaker: Connor
en: The boat?

speaker: Robert
en: B–b– a BOAT?! She's a SHIP, boy, and make no mistake about it! I thought you brought him here to restore order? I reckon he's the greenest thing on the frontier!

speaker: Achilles
en: Connor, meet me back at the manor when you've finished here.

speaker: Connor
en: You said it requires repairs... You able?

speaker: Robert
en: SHE does need work – a ship is a 'she', boy – and yes I can refit her but I'm lacking in the proper supplies. Some... Some quality timber would help me get started.

speaker: Connor
en: I can see to that. How long before it – SHE is able to sail again?

speaker: Robert
en: Just get me the timber, boy and I'll raise a crew.

speaker: Achilles
en: Ah, there you are! I've something to show you. Come, take a look.

speaker: Connor
en: What is it?

speaker: Achilles
en: A ledger. It lets us manage the homestead's dealings.

speaker: Connor
en: And these?

speaker: Achilles
en: Ah, that was years ago. Before the . Before the Templars. Before everything collapsed... But that's all in the past. Better we focus on what's in front of us. Take up the ledger and I'll teach you how it all works.

speaker: Connor
en: How dare you call upon me after Monmouth?

speaker: George
en: I have nobody else to turn to. The Culper Ring informed me that Westpoint's been infiltrated. I believe they intend to murder Major General Benedict Arnold.

speaker: Connor
en: I still do not see why you need me.

speaker: George
en: The loss of such a figure would be devastating to the cause. It must be done without my soldiers' knowledge. The mere idea of the Patriots being breached would be crippling to morale, to the war. Will you do it?

speaker: Connor
en: It will be done. But never call on me again.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Where'd Travis get off to?

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Heard his son has got the sickness, Arnold sent him home.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Not what I heard. I heard he's proper disappeared.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Wherever he went, his replacement is something of a bore. Quiet fellow. Keeps to himself. Not like Travis was, always up for a laugh.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: I know what you mean. Feels like the new chap is gonna strangle me in my sleep.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Hahahah. Come off it.

speaker: Benedict
en: What in God's name are you doing?!

speaker: Connor
en: That man was a British spy. He intended to kill you, Major Arnold.

speaker: Benedict
en: What?

speaker: Connor
en: General Washington learned of the plot and sent me to foil it.

speaker: Benedict
en: Indeed. Hm. We need all the support we can muster. Some of my men are leaving on a munitions delivery to a nearby camp and I need you to escort them. Find John Anderson upon your arrival. He'll have further instructions. Questions?

speaker: Connor
en: No.

speaker: Benedict
en: Good.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: So I trained. In running. In climbing. In fighting. In falling. And for every lesson that concerned the body, there were two that concerned the mind. Language. Philosophy. Logic. The arts... Achilles taught most often of the Assassins and Templars. Their structures, origins, and purpose. Centuries of history condensed into a few short days... I told him of the men who had burned my village. Of Charles Lee and my promise to him. Achilles explained that Lee and his followers were Templars. And that they were led by none other than my own father. If I was to serve the Order, these men would become my targets. So I worked harder. Learned faster. But for all of my progress, it was clear that I still had much to learn. My training had only just begun.

speaker: Achilles
en: Good morning.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: To you as well. You taking a trip?

speaker: Achilles
en: I've decided to do something about the house. And you're going to help me. Get in.

speaker: Achilles
en: Don't stare.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Sorry.

speaker: Achilles
en: Come on.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: This place is incredible. The people. The sounds and smells. I could walk these streets for days and know not even half its wonders.

speaker: Achilles
en: I thought the same as you upon a time. These days I much prefer the quiet of the countryside.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: But there is so much LIFE here. So many opportunities.

speaker: Achilles
en: For a few, my boy. For a few... There's a store close to here. You're to buy the items on this list. Tell them where the carriage is—and they'll see that's it loaded. Understood?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Yes.

speaker: Achilles
en: Good. You're also going to need a new name. Your skin is fair enough that you might pass for one with Spanish or Italian blood. Better to be thought a Spaniard than a Native. And both are better still than I.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: That is not true.

speaker: Achilles
en: What's TRUE and what IS aren't always the same.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What would you call me, then?

speaker: Achilles
en: Connor. Yes. That will be your name. Alright then. Off you go.

speaker: Citizen 1
en: I grow tired of this! It seems every day a new tax is levied—a new rule enforced—without our consent! The . The . The . Oh, Chancellor Townshend must have thought himself so clever when he papered these thefts and made them law. But the says we've a right to refuse! That there will be no taxation without representation! Tell me—who represented us in Parliament? Spoke on our behalf? Signed in our stead? Give me a name! Only you can't! And do you know why? You can't tell me who represented us because nobody did!

speaker: Merchant
en: You lost?

speaker: Connor
en: I need the items on this list.

speaker: Merchant
en: Will you be paying with coin or trade?

speaker: Merchant
en: Some of these things I have. Some I don't. Lumber's hard to come by since my supplier up and vanished. I have the tools and pitch, though. Nails too. Where do you want this delivered?

speaker: Connor
en: Our wagon is near the state house.

speaker: Connor
en: I should return to Achilles.

speaker: Citizen 1
en: Who stands in Parliament for Boston? For New York? For Virginia? No one! But is represented. And and . and . The list goes on. one and all. What is become of the rights of Englishmen? Are we not entitled to have a say in our governance? Who are they to silence our voices? To insist we be represented by strangers? Have you forgotten the and how we responded? We spoke up! We resisted! So they stood down! We were heard and it was repealed! But now... Now too many are silent. Or worse—they excuse it! The taxes are not so high, they say. The money is put to good use, they say. Fie, I say! Fie we should ALL say! Though the taxes may be small, they were enacted and enforced without our consent. As to their use? They pay governors and judges! And if it's Britain pays them, it's Britain whom they are beholden, not us! Do none see the danger here?

speaker: Connor
en: What happened?

speaker: Achilles
en: That's what we're going to find out. Follow me.

speaker: Preston
en: I say again: disperse! Congregating in this manner is forbidden!

speaker: Citizen 2
en: We're not going anywhere, bug!

speaker: Citizen 3
en: Oi! Why don't you go back to England?!

speaker: Preston
en: No good can come of this chaos! Return to your homes and all will be forgiven!

speaker: Citizen 4
en: Never!

speaker: Citizen 5
en: Not until you've answered for your crimes!

speaker: Citizen 6
en: You're right cowards, pointing guns at unarmed folk!

speaker: Citizen 7
en: You don't scare us!

speaker: Citizen 8
en: We ain't afraid!

speaker: Achilles
en: There!

speaker: Connor
en: Is that my father...?

speaker: Achilles
en: Yes. Which means trouble is sure to follow. I need you to tail his accomplice. This crowd is a powder keg—we can't allow him to light the fuse.

speaker: Connor
en: But

speaker: Achilles
en: But nothing! Do as I say and go!

speaker: Citizen 9
en: Oi! You there. What's all the fuss about?

speaker: Shooter
en: Fire at the Town House...

speaker: Connor
en: Your plot has ended.

speaker: Shooter
en: Not quite.

speaker: Montgomery
en: Damn you, fire!

speaker: Connor
en: I need to find Achilles.

speaker: Messenger
en: You there! Careful now... I'm here to help.

speaker: Connor
en: Who are you?

speaker: Messenger
en: Just a messenger. Mister Adams wants a word.

speaker: Connor
en: What? Why?

speaker: Messenger
en: You'll need ask him that yourself. He'll meet you tonight near Faneuil Hall. I suggest laying low until then.

speaker: Troubled Waters
en: was a virtual representation of one of Ratonhnhaké:ton's genetic memories, relived by Desmond Miles in 2012 through the Animus.

speaker: Boone
en: The first time I saw the light was back in Boston. I was trading my biggest take of the season when the fire rose behind Beacon Hill. Went straight up in the night sky, passed the moon. Then it was gone. I wasn't alone. Those next to me had their heads cocked the same - craned as far back as it could go - mouths agape. Couldn't tell you what it was but I can tell you it wasn't of this earth.

speaker: Sailor 1
en: Doctor! You need to help me!

speaker: White
en: You won't lose your leg, that much I can promise you. But it will hurt some for a time longer. Looks worse than it is, just keep it clean and you should be fine. Connor! I simply can't get to all these men in reasonable time. I need help. From you, from anyone!

speaker: Connor
en: I think I have someone for you.

speaker: Connor
en: Diana. Come with me. I need your help.

speaker: Diana
en: Of course. What's the matter?

speaker: Connor
en: Dr. White is overwhelmed and needs some extra hands.

speaker: Diana
en: I'm no doctor, Connor.

speaker: Connor
en: Maybe not, but I have seen you care for people before. You have the way of it.

speaker: White
en: Diana! Perfect. I'm told you have a healer's hand. Please see to this young man. Connor, if you could help the two gentlemen out front.

speaker: Sailor 2
en: Thanks, skip. Good of you to help. I should be alright.

speaker: Sailor 3
en: Many thanks, cap'n.

speaker: Sailor 4
en: That's a spot better, sir. Thanks.

speaker: Sailor 5
en: Caught a piece of shrapnel in the shoulder. Bad luck. Thank you, captain.

speaker: Sailor 6
en: Caught some burns off a rope. It happens. Thanks, skipper.

speaker: White
en: You did well, Connor. But Diana, you impressed me greatly.

speaker: Diana
en: Well thank you, doctor. I haven't studied the practice or anything.

speaker: White
en: Maybe not, but your instincts are superb and you have a healer's touch. If you had the time, I would be grateful for your help on more regular basis.

speaker: Diana
en: Might be Catherine could watch the young ones a few days a week.

speaker: White
en: And if she can't, we'll find someone who will.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: He tried to destroy the entire town. It is all my fault.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I do not understand. Washington knows me. He is a man of reason, if nothing else. But that was not the man I once called my friend.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Are you confused? When would you have ever met that monster?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I met him ... I ... Mother, this is all wrong. Washington, the violence, all of it!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: We must get back and warn our people in the village before the Mad King spreads his destruction there.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: The Lexington I knew was the scene of a great triumph. Now it is a place of disaster.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: This way. It will be faster.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Mad King George is on a warpath and intends to destroy our village. We need every able body to protect it, come with us.

speaker: Teiowí:sonte
en: We know. Oiá:ner sent us to collect boughs of the Great Willow. She means for us to defend our people.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: To make the tea?! Has she lost her senses?! The tea's pitfalls overshadow its power. You must not do it.

speaker: Teiowí:sonte
en: You have seen what it can do? Is it dangerous?

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: I have seen it. It is worse than dangerous, it is a promise of madness, even death for those lacking the constitution.

speaker: Kahionhaténion
en: We cannot disobey the Clan Mother.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Believe me, the tea of the Great Willow is folly. Come back with us.

speaker: Teiowí:sonte
en: We will fulfill the Clan Mother's request. We will collect the boughs. Speak to Oiá:ner and if you can convince her, we will burn them.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: I intend to.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What is the Tea of the Great Willow?

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Something our people should never have discovered. It is the tea brewed of the Great Willow's virgin boughs and consumed by our warriors. It grants certain—strengths, Ratonhnhaké:ton, but for every physical boon it gives, it robs a piece of the mind. It must never be made.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Did you drink it?

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Never. But I have seen what happens to those who do. You are the son of a man of violence. It would affect you far more than anyone else. I will not allow you to drink it.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Thank the maker we are not too late.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: You intend to brew tea of the Great Willow? Have you forgotten the consequence of drinking it? I have not.

speaker: Oiá:ner
en: No, Kaniehtí:io, but when our people face a threat like the Mad King, there are no other paths.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: No other paths? We can fight them as human beings! My son and I have had success just the two of us. Imagine the strength of our whole village.

speaker: Oiá:ner
en: And how many of these fearless Bluecoats have you brought down at a time? Two? Five? Ten? Thousands will come to destroy us—thousands that YOU awoke. Our people's survival depends on the strength of the Great Willow.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: You are as mad as the King. Do what you will but my son will not drink the tea.

speaker: Oiá:ner
en: Then, like you, he will die.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Stupid old woman!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: What would you have us do, mother? We have no choice but to fight.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: I know. I have something that will help. Something from your father.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: My father?

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: He left it for you long ago, before he died.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: My father left those for me?

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: He was part of an order. A secret brotherhood

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I know who my father was and I know what those are.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: You do?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: They will certainly help.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: How do you know all this?

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: I can not explain. Everything is all wrong here! All of this should NOT BE. YOU should not be. I watched you

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: He is here!

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: Run! To the forest! Get out of here! They will show you no mercy! You must flee!

speaker: Washington
en: General Putnam, General Arnold. I sometimes despair of our project. I question my abilities and my strength. But with you two at my side, I believe we will bring liberty to this country and we will bring it with fists of iron! Can I have assurance of your loyalty?

speaker: Putnam
en: You have my solemn pledge.

speaker: Arnold
en: And mine.

speaker: Washington
en: Thank you, honorable gentlemen. This country will remember you.

speaker: Putnam
en: Give no quarter to the savages!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: You'll not succeed here!

speaker: Washington
en: You!? You survived? How astonishing. This time, I'll make certain of your death.

speaker: Ratonhnhaké:ton
en: MOTHER! Washington!

speaker: Washington
en: You are fighting the force of liberty! Away with you!

speaker: Washington
en: With my power, I will rule over a free world!

speaker: Washington
en: Give that here. For good measure.

speaker: Myriam
en: Need someone like you to help me.

speaker: Norris
en: My friend!

speaker: Connor
en: Norris! What are you doing?

speaker: Norris
en: She said yes!

speaker: Connor
en: Myriam?

speaker: Norris
en: We are getting married!

speaker: Myriam
en: I told you not to touch him, Norris!

speaker: Connor
en: Is it true?

speaker: Myriam
en: Yes!

speaker: Connor
en: Ha ha!

speaker: Timothy
en: So now that you've been told, might I have a word? We have MUCH work to do!

speaker: Connor
en: Of course! What would you have me do?

speaker: Timothy
en: Accompany me to the inn, I have business there. Norris is a stickler when it comes to tradition. Myriam knows not where her father is and they were hopeful that you might act his part at the ceremony.

speaker: Connor
en: I am not familiar with colonial wedding customs.

speaker: Timothy
en: It means you will walk with her during the ceremony and give her to Norris as her father would.

speaker: Connor
en: I would be honored.

speaker: Timothy
en: Wonderful. On to other business! Our weddings are complex beasts and require many hands working together to execute. We'll need Warren and Prudence to provide food, Ellen to make the appropriate clothes, Big Dave to smith wedding bands, me to conduct the service and Oliver and Corrine to host a banquet.

speaker: Connor
en: That IS a lot.

speaker: Timothy
en: We'll start here.

speaker: Norris
en: Connor.

speaker: Connor
en: Everything seems to be in order for the big day!

speaker: Norris
en: It is. Except I can't find Myriam.

speaker: Connor
en: I am certain she is making sure all is perfect. I will find her, my friend.

speaker: Sailor
en: Don't think she wants to marry you, mate!

speaker: Myriam
en: Leave me be!

speaker: Connor
en: Why do you run?

speaker: Myriam
en: Leave me be! I'm no house wife!

speaker: Connor
en: Nobody thinks you are one!

speaker: Myriam
en: That's what all this means!

speaker: Timothy
en: You may kiss your bride.

speaker: Ellen
en: Hello, Connor. Enjoying yourself?

speaker: Connor
en: I am. It is nice to see everyone together and happy.

speaker: David
en: Look at those two kids, it's a lovely sight. Norris is one of my best friends and he couldn't have found a better woman. Proud of him.

speaker: Ellen
en: Sometimes people are just right for one another. Norris and Myriam are a match made in heaven.

speaker: David
en: Or a match made by Connor, isn't that right?

speaker: Connor
en: I only helped Norris muster his courage. The rest came naturally.

speaker: Godfrey
en: ...and my little brother Joseph tossed him in the river!

speaker: Diana
en: Connor! We were just recalling our weddings.

speaker: Connor
en: Spirited events, I take it.

speaker: Catherine
en: Spirited? More like brawls than unions, they were! Ha ha.

speaker: Terry
en: Calling Jo "little" is like calling me Big Terry – boy's a bloody mountain!

speaker: Godfrey
en: My younger brother had a blow-up with one of Terry's cousins. A minor disagreement about some lass' dance card. I'll just say Terry's cousin sobered up right quick when it was over!

speaker: Diana
en: Poor boy! Sittin' there sopping wet on a stump while Joseph spun 'round with the object of his affection.

speaker: Terry
en: Ha ha ha. Was good for him! Taught him good things don't come easy!

speaker: Ellen
en: Excuse me, everyone. Thank you, I won't keep you long. I would like to present something to Connor and you all. I once said I'd find a way to show my gratitude for your courageous actions in my defense and this is what I give you today.

speaker: Ellen
en: This flag is a symbol of our strength and unity and I would hope you'd all be proud to fly it high above your homes and shops. I'll happily make one for each and every one of you if you so desire but this one is for you, Connor.

speaker: Connor
en: Thank you.

speaker: Myriam
en: Could you make a little more noise? Been fixin' to trap a cougar I've seen prowling about. The beast has snapped two of my snares already. From what I've seen its fur is white - mad as it sounds. Its hide would be worth a fortune to the right person.

speaker: Connor
en: I have never seen a cougar like that. I would like to help you.

speaker: Myriam
en: I'll follow you then. Stay quiet.

speaker: Myriam
en: Got his trail yet? Look at the size of those claw-marks! Better shoot true! He has a taste for fresh meat– seen this before. Looks fresh. He's close.

speaker: Myriam
en: There he goes! We won't get another chance at this! Come on Connor! We won't see him again after this! This is our only shot. Hurry up!

speaker: Norris
en: You must be here for my new friend! I was dumping a load and he went straight in. Lucky I wasn't in there...

speaker: Connor
en: Very. What are you thinking, Myriam?

speaker: Myriam
en: Flush and fire. Norris can back off, one of us goes in there to draw him out and the other waits out here to shoot.

speaker: Connor
en: I will go in.

speaker: Norris
en: Nice shot.

speaker: Connor
en: Thank you, Myriam.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Let's see if our man can fly.

speaker: Lance
en: Ah! What in God's name is going on around here?

speaker: Lance
en: Please!? Help? Me? Anyone? Please? Someone pull me up!

speaker: Lance
en: Thank you. Thank you.

speaker: Connor
en: Are you alright?

speaker: Lance
en: I think so...didn't do much to me aside from a good scare. Blaggards.

speaker: Connor
en: What did they want with you?

speaker: Lance
en: My purse, which was meager, and they decided they'd punish me for their trouble. Silly really, my tools and equipment WERE worth a king's share to the right man. In any case, I best get on my way. It's a long walk to the nearest inn. I thank you again for your kindness.

speaker: Connor
en: Have you no home?

speaker: Lance
en: Ah, well. I was a proud resident of Boston until recently, but I'm not a supporter of his majesty and well I was forced out of my wood shop and home by Loyalists.

speaker: Connor
en: There are plenty around here who could use the services of a skilled craftsman, if you were looking for somewhere to settle.

speaker: Lance
en: Is that right? I may look into that.

speaker: Connor
en: My next target will be William Johnson.

speaker: Achilles
en: He claims to be a friend of the natives.

speaker: Connor
en: He is no friend. He has put together money in an attempt to buy land from the Iroquois.

speaker: Achilles
en: Isn't it better to be bought than be taken by force?

speaker: Connor
en: Johnson has no right to buy the land. No one does.

speaker: Achilles
en: The rules and politics of this world are changing, Connor. Whether you want them to or not. Your victory here may only delay the inevitable.

speaker: Connor
en: So I should do nothing?

speaker: Achilles
en: You should do what you think is best.

speaker: Connor
en: Then I will put a stop to this.

speaker: William Johnson
en: What are you doing? I have only the best interests of your people in mind.

speaker: Connor
en: That is your opinion, not ours.

speaker: William Johnson
en: The correct opinion, you mean. One that would see them safe.

speaker: Connor
en: You should concern yourself with your own safety, for I will return.

speaker: William Johnson
en: Look what you've done. I was trying to help these people.

speaker: Connor
en: The Iroquois do not need your help.

speaker: William Johnson
en: They do. You just can't see it yet. Do you think the Colonists will be kind to them?

speaker: Connor
en: Why wouldn't they?

speaker: William Johnson
en: Another will eventually come to claim their land. It is only a matter of time. And when it happens, it will not be someone who respects their interests as I do.

speaker: Connor
en: You speak of respect, yet you came with armed soldiers.

speaker: William Johnson
en: I had hoped to not resort to them.

speaker: Connor
en: As I had hoped you could leave my people in peace.

speaker: William Johnson
en: Yes. You have made it abundantly clear that hope and reality do not always align.

speaker: Thomas
en: On the cold, cold ground.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Hear, hear!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Hard at work, I see.

speaker: Haytham
en: How did you...

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: It is time. We've set up camp to the north. Meet me there.

speaker: Haytham
en: Gentlemen! Let us away.

speaker: Benjamin
en: First it was too cold. Now it's too god-damned hot!

speaker: John
en: And humid too! It's a right swamp, I tell you.

speaker: William
en: To say nothing of the mosquitoes.

speaker: Haytham
en: Warm weather and bugs are soon to be the least of our worries.

speaker: Thomas
en: Wot? Ya mean the Bulldog? Please. We'll be in that one's beef soon enough and onto the next.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Where's your boy Lee gone off to?

speaker: Haytham
en: Returned to finish out his service under Braddock.

speaker: Benjamin
en: I imagine the Bulldog's none too pleased after the stunt we pulled.

speaker: Haytham
en: Lee's to spin a tale of my incompetence and beg for forgiveness. He's a way with words—especially when it comes to flattery. I expect he'll be welcomed back with open arms.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Which would give us a man inside.

speaker: Haytham
en: Precisely.

speaker: John
en: Unless you've underestimated our enemy.

speaker: Haytham
en: If I have, Charles will sense it first and make his escape. He's more clever than you think.

speaker: Thomas
en: When this is done I'm taking a week in New York. It's high time I went 'n' saw the sights.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Of empty whiskey bottles and women's breeches, no doubt.

speaker: Thomas
en: Heh-heh-heh. What other kinds of sights is worth seein'?

speaker: Haytham
en: I see you've been busy.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: All the men are from many different tribes—united in their desire to see Braddock sent away. The Abenaki. The Lenape. The Shawnee.

speaker: Haytham
en: And you? Who do you stand for?

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Myself.

speaker: Haytham
en: What would you have me do?

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: We will help the others to prepare. Follow.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: You will help the others to prepare.

speaker: Haytham
en: And my men?

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: They'll be put to work.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Follow.

speaker: Abenaki man
en: Arí:sawe says you are to be trusted...I hope her faith in you is not misplaced.

speaker: Haytham
en: What do you require?

speaker: Abenaki man
en: There is a cart close by to here I wish to fill with gunpowder. You will help me with this.

speaker: Shawnee man
en: Hello friend.

speaker: Haytham
en: Kaniehtí:io said you'd have work for me.

speaker: Shawnee man
en: We mean to hide ourselves in the trees and surprise the Bulldog with musket fire from above.

speaker: Shawnee man
en: But the wood are thick with his scouts. You must keep them away from us.

speaker: Haytham
en: Lead on.

speaker: Haytham
en: How might I serve?

speaker: Haytham
en: I'm not quite sure I understand. Do you speak English?

speaker: Lenape man
en: He speaks no language, because he has no tongue. Your kind took it from him.

speaker: Haytham
en: For what reason?

speaker: Lenape man
en: There was none.

speaker: Lenape man
en: He needs you to help us cut down those trees to build blockades.

speaker: Haytham
en: Of course.

speaker: Haytham
en: Everything is in place. I can't wait to see the look on Braddock's face when the trap is sprung.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: You take pleasure in this?

speaker: Haytham
en: You're the one asked me to help you kill the man!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: It does not please me to do so. He is sacrificed so that that land and the people who live on it might be saved. What motivates you? Some past wrongs? A betrayal? Or is it simple the thrill of the hunt?

speaker: Haytham
en: You misread me.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Braddock's men will be here soon. We should prepare for their arrival.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: They come.

speaker: George
en: Everything alright, sir?

speaker: Edward
en: Just savoring the moment. No doubt many wonder why it is we've pushed so far west. These are wild lands, as yet untamed and unsettled. But it shall not always be so. In time, our holdings will no longer suffice. And that day is closer than you think. We must ensure that our people have ample room to grow and further prosper. Which means we need more land! The French understand this and endeavor to prevent such growth. They skirt around our territory—erecting forts and forging alliances—awaiting the day that they might strangle us with the noose they've built. This must not come to pass! We must sever the cord and send them back! This is why we ride. To offer them once last chance: The French will leave or they will die!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Now is the time to strike.

speaker: Haytham
en: Wait. To scatter the expedition is not enough. We must ensure that Braddock falls. Else he's sure to try again. I will disguise myself as one of his own and make my way to his side. Your ambush will provide the perfect cover for me to deliver the killing blow.

speaker: Native 1
en: We await your signal.

speaker: Native 2
en: There, in front of us.

speaker: Redcoat 1
en: The wood's too thick. At this rate it'll be days before we reach Duquesne. We should follow the river instead.

speaker: Redcoat 2
en: The troop would be exposed there. We must maintain the element of surprise.

speaker: Redcoat 1
en: We're near 2,000 men. One scout is all they need to know of us... And then what? Swiftness would serve us better.

speaker: Haytham
en: Kill them!

speaker: Redcoat 2
en: Ambush!

speaker: Redcoat 3
en: How could anyone call this forest home? It's all mud and bugs and monstrous things...

speaker: Redcoat 4
en: Aye. Better we cut it all down. Clear a space for civilization—and not this wild dark.

speaker: Redcoat 3
en: No wonder the savages are so filled with fury. I'd be too if I had to live in such a place.

speaker: Redcoat 4
en: Don't know why so many refuse to throw in with us. Life in the cities is much more pleasant. Can you imagine? Ground for a mattress. Canopy of leaves for a roof. It's barbaric.

speaker: Redcoat 5
en: I'm telling you, we've packed the cart too high! The ground is uneven—its dangers hidden. One false move and the whole thing is sure to fall over...

speaker: Redcoat 6
en: With the French pushed back there'll be a lot of opportunities for us up north.

speaker: Redcoat 7
en: I hear the beaver pelts they gather fetch a fine price back home.

speaker: Redcoat 8
en: Aye—but for all the riches one might claim, the winter waits to take it all away.

speaker: Redcoat 7
en: Come now, it can't be that bad. Else the frogs wouldn't have lasted this long.

speaker: Redcoat 8
en: Oh—don't you know? King Louis filled the place with whores to keep his men from turning tail.

speaker: Redcoat 7
en: What?

speaker: Redcoat 8
en: Aye. Loaded up a dozen boats with the finest Paris had to offer. Called 'em the , they did. Sent to warm the men in ways the campfires couldn't.

speaker: Redcoat 7
en: I don't believe a word of it. Much as I'd like to...

speaker: Redcoat 8
en: If Braddock's mission is successful, we'll get to see for ourselves soon enough. Then we'll know the truth of it.

speaker: Edward
en: Have served, you mean.

speaker: Redcoat 9
en: Sir?

speaker: Edward
en: You are grateful to HAVE served.

speaker: Redcoat 10
en: General!

speaker: Edward
en: I'll not tolerate doubt amongst those I command. Nor sympathy for the enemy. I've no time for insubordination. He paid for his treachery as all traitors must. If we are to win this war against the French... Nay, when we win this war... It will be because men like you obeyed men like me—and did so without hesitation. We must have order amongst our ranks, and a clear chain of command. Leaders and followers. Without such structure, there can be no victory. Am I understood?

speaker: Haytham
en: Edward! Not so fun on the other end of the barrel, is it?

speaker: Redcoat 10
en: LOOK OUT!

speaker: Charles
en: Sir.

speaker: Haytham
en: Where are you off to, Edward...?

speaker: Haytham
en: I never took you for a coward, Edward.

speaker: Edward
en: Come on then.

speaker: Edward
en: Such arrogance. I always knew it would be the end of you. IS the end of you.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Don't.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Hurry! Before he gets away!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: I SAID GO!

speaker: Edward
en: I don't deserve this! You're a hypocrite, Haytham!

speaker: Haytham
en: I'm sorry Edward, but you've forced my hand.

speaker: Edward
en: Dammit!

speaker: Edward
en: Why, Haytham?

speaker: Haytham
en: Your death opens a door. It's nothing personal. Well, maybe it is a LITTLE personal. You've been a pain in my arse, after all.

speaker: Edward
en: But we are brothers in arms.

speaker: Haytham
en: Once, perhaps. No longer. Do you think I've forgotten what you did? All those innocents slaughtered. And for what? It does not engender peace to cut your way to resolution.

speaker: Edward
en: Wrong! Were that we applied the sword more liberally and more often, the world would be a better place than it is today.

speaker: Haytham
en: In this instance, I concur. Farewell Edward.

speaker: Haytham
en: It's done.

speaker: Haytham
en: Now I've upheld my part of the bargain. I expect that you will honor yours?

speaker: Haytham
en: You two—get the General back to camp.

speaker: Redcoat 11
en: At once, sir.

speaker: Haytham
en: The rest of you—fan out and search the area. Whoever did this can't be far.

speaker: George
en: General!

speaker: George
en: He lives!

speaker: Haytham
en: Dammit!

speaker: Haytham
en: It's done.

speaker: Haytham
en: You accused me of taking pleasure in this. Of desiring death.

speaker: Haytham
en: But the alacrity...It's how I make the act acceptable. I detach myself from it and silence the voice of dissent...the voice of morality. I was born to kill, you see. Quite literally. Raised in an order of assassins. Death—it's not simply something that I do...It's who I am.

speaker: Haytham
en: But I did not come all this way to reflect and regret.

speaker: Haytham
en: Now I've upheld my part of the bargain. I expect that you will honor yours?

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Follow me.

speaker: Haytham
en: No... No!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: You seem disappointed.

speaker: Haytham
en: I thought that I held a key that would open something here...

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: This room is all there is.

speaker: Haytham
en: I expected... more.

speaker: Haytham
en: What do they mean?

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: It tells the story of Iottsitíson, who came into their world and shaped it for what life might come. She had a hard journey, fraught with great loss and peril. But she believed in her children and what they might achieve. And though she is long gone from the physical world—her eyes still watch over us. Her ears still hear our words. Her hands still guide us. And her love still gives us strength.

speaker: Haytham
en: You have shown me great kindness, Ziio. Thank you. I... I should go.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: I am sorry you did not find what you seek.

speaker: Charles
en: Master Kenway. Did you find it, then?

speaker: Haytham
en: It was not the right place.

speaker: Charles
en: The others are waiting for you.

speaker: Haytham
en: Gentlemen.

speaker: Haytham
en: Please, sit.

speaker: Haytham
en: I fear our "temple" was no more than a painted cave. Although it did contain precursor images and script, which means we are close.

speaker: Thomas
en: Not close 'nuff it seems.

speaker: Haytham
en: We need to redouble our efforts and expand our order, and establish a permanent base here. Although the site eludes us, I am confident we will find it.

speaker: John
en: Truth.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Hear-hear.

speaker: Haytham
en: Furthermore, I believe it is time we welcomed Charles into our fold. He has proven himself a loyal disciple—and served unerringly since the day he came to us. He should be able to share in our knowledge and reap all the benefits that such a gift implies. Are any opposed?

speaker: Haytham
en: Very well. Charles, come, stand.

speaker: Haytham
en: Do you swear to uphold the principles of our order and all that for which we stand?

speaker: Charles
en: I do.

speaker: Haytham
en: And never to share our secrets nor divulge the true nature of our work?

speaker: Charles
en: I do.

speaker: Haytham
en: And to do so from now until death—whatever the cost?

speaker: Charles
en: I do.

speaker: Haytham
en: Then we welcome you into our fold, brother. Together we will usher in the dawn of a New World. One defined by purpose and order. Give me your hand.

speaker: Haytham
en: You are a Templar. May the Father of Understanding guide us.

speaker: All
en: May the Father of Understanding guide us.

speaker: Holden
en: Sir?.. Sir?.. Everything all right, sir?

speaker: Haytham
en: Yes, fine... I'm just preoccupied, that's all.

speaker: Holden
en: Don't forget your invitation. Master Birch will be meeting you inside.

speaker: Haytham
en: Thank you.

speaker: Holden
en: Where shall I retrieve you once you're done?

speaker: Haytham
en: Front of the opera house. And be quick about it. I don't expect to be here long.

speaker: Holden
en: I'll bring her 'round at once.

speaker: Clerk
en: Invitation, please.

speaker: Clerk
en: Shall I take your coat sir?

speaker: Man
en: Ladies and gentlemen, you are requested to kindly find your seats. Good evening, sir. This way, please.

speaker: Haytham
en: My apologies...

speaker: Birch
en: Evening Haytham.

speaker: Haytham
en: Reginald.

speaker: Birch
en: I can't tell you how happy I was to hear they'd mounted this revival. Gay's best work by far. Have you seen it before?

speaker: Haytham
en: Once. My father brought me here as a child, though I remember little of it. And I don't suppose tonight will afford me the luxury of a proper viewing either.

speaker: Birch
en: No, I'm afraid it won't. On to business then. Do you see him?

speaker: Haytham
en: He's seated in one of the above.

speaker: Birch
en: The stairs are watched. You'll need to find another way up.

speaker: Haytham
en: I already have.

speaker: Haytham
en: A thousand pardons... My apologies... So sorry...

speaker: Stagehand
en: Man the lines! Flats in place! Stand-by!

speaker: Actor 1
en: I've got a bit of stage fright!

speaker: Actor 2
en: A little 'll put a bloom in your cheek.

speaker: Stagehand
en: Flying in!

speaker: Actor 3
en: Jeremy's really burning up the boards tonight! He's a marvel.

speaker: Miko
en: Haytham... You should have come to me. We would have found another way...

speaker: Haytham
en: Yes. But then you would have known. For what it's worth, I'm sorry.

speaker: Miko
en: As am I.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Calm, please!

speaker: Guard 2
en: That man there! Seize him!

speaker: Suspect
en: But, I've done no wrong! I swear it!

speaker: Guard 2
en: Search him. Any weapons?

speaker: Guard 3
en: Nothing. We must keep looking. He must be in here somewhere.

speaker: Woman 1
en: What ever happened?

speaker: Man 1
en: A man was killed in the upper balcony.

speaker: Woman 1
en: Oh my.

speaker: Guard 4
en: I beg your pardon madam, did you notice anyone suspicious coming from that room up there?

speaker: Woman 2
en: No. I don't think so.

speaker: Guard 4
en: Are you certain? Try to remember.

speaker: Guard 5
en: Order! We must have order! Please friends, there is no danger!

speaker: Woman 3
en: We must leave at once!

speaker: Man 2
en: There's a killer about! I'm staying where it's safe!

speaker: Man 3
en: Move! Move!

speaker: Woman 4
en: Hey!

speaker: Man 4
en: Imbecile!

speaker: Guard 6
en: Where are you going?

speaker: Man 3
en: I need to get out! It's too close in here! I must get some air!

speaker: Guard 6
en: Calm yourself! I won't let you go until you're calm!

speaker: Holden
en: And how was the opera?

speaker: Haytham
en: Rather dull, truth be told.

speaker: Holden
en: Shall we be off, then?

speaker: Haytham
en: Aye. To Fleet and Bride.

speaker: Holden
en: By your command.

speaker: Birch
en: Fascinating... Gentlemen, I hold in my hand a key. And if this book is to be believed, it will open the doors of a storehouse built by Those Who Came Before.

speaker: Haytham
en: Ah... Yes, those who ruled, reigned, and then vanished from the world. Do we know what it is that would be held within?

speaker: Birch
en: It could contain certain knowledge. Perhaps a weapon. Or something as yet unknown, unfathomable in its construction and purpose. It could be any of these things. Or none of them. They are still an enigma, these precursors. But of one thing I am certain—whatever waits behind those doors shall prove a great boon to us all.

speaker: Haytham
en: Or our enemies. Should they find it first.

speaker: Birch
en: They won't. You've seen to that.

speaker: Haytham
en: I assume you know where this storehouse is?

speaker: Birch
en: Ah, Mister Harrison.

speaker: Harrison
en: Gentlemen.

speaker: Birch
en: How fare your calculations?

speaker: Harrison
en: I believe the site lies somewhere within this region.

speaker: Haytham
en: That's a lot of ground to cover.

speaker: Harrison
en: My apologies. Were that I could be more accurate...

speaker: Birch
en: That's alright. It suffices for a start. And this is why we've called you here, Master Kenway. We'd like for you to travel to America, locate the storehouse, and take possession of its contents.

speaker: Haytham
en: I am yours to command. Although a job of this magnitude will require more than just myself.

speaker: Birch
en: Of course. Upon this paper are the names of five men sympathetic to our cause. Each is also uniquely suited to aid you in your endeavor. With them at your side, you will want nothing.

speaker: Haytham
en: Well, then I'd best be on my way.

speaker: Birch
en: I knew our faith in you was not misplaced. We've booked you passage to Boston. Your ship leaves at dawn. Go forth, Haytham – and bring honor to us all.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Use the snowstorm to mask your approach. Having second thoughts?

speaker: Haytham
en: Hardly. But I'll have to approach this carefully.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Go on, then. I'll keep watch from here.

speaker: Haytham
en: Hmmm. I can hide in that cart.

speaker: Redcoat
en: What's in the wagon? I need a full inventory.

speaker: Driver
en: As you wish. Let's see - 2 barrels of salt, 12 pounds pork, 10 pounds beef, 7 dozen eggs, 16 wheels of cheese - none of it French, don't worry, 5 bottles of whiskey. Couple dozen new uniforms, boots, and leather for patching. Blankets. A cart of feed for the horses. Wot else... Wot else... That's it. That's all there is.

speaker: Haytham
en: Those cannons are likely to cause trouble. Perhaps I could sabotage them.

speaker: Fraser
en: Tell me you've good news?

speaker: Washington
en: General Braddock refused the offer. There will be no truce.

speaker: Fraser
en: Dammit! Why, George? What reason did he give?

speaker: Washington
en: He said a diplomatic solution was no solution at all. That allowing the French to retreat would only delay an inevitable conflict, one in which they'd now have the upper hand.

speaker: Fraser
en: There's merit to those words, as much as I hate to admit it. Still... can't he see this is unwise?

speaker: Washington
en: It doesn't sit well with me either. We're far from home with our forces divided. Worse, I fear Braddock's bloodlust makes him careless. It puts the men at risk. I'd rather not be delivering grim news to mothers and widows because the Bulldog wanted to prove a point.

speaker: Fraser
en: Where's the General now?

speaker: Washington
en: Rallying the troops.

speaker: Fraser
en: And then it's on to Fort Duquesne, I assume?

speaker: Washington
en: Eventually. The march north will surely take time. There's a copy of the plans in the command tent should you wish to review them.

speaker: Fraser
en: At least this will be ended soon.

speaker: Washington
en: I tried, John.

speaker: Fraser
en: I know, my friend. I know...

speaker: Haytham
en: That map will surely be of use. I need to find it.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: What news?

speaker: Haytham
en: Braddock has left to rally his troops. They're marching on Fort Duquesne. It'll be a while yet 'til they're ready, which gives us time to form a plan.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: No need. We will ambush them here, near the river. Go and gather your allies. I will do the same. I will send word when it is time to strike.

speaker: Jennifer
en: Father... did you always know how to sail a boat?

speaker: Edward
en: The Jackdaw is a ship, Jenny. Not a boat.

speaker: Jennifer
en: But did you always know?

speaker: Edward
en: No. No, I learned after leaving Bristol.

speaker: Jennifer
en: After you left mother?

speaker: Edward
en: Well, I didn't leave your... I didn't leave without saying goodbye, that is. It was an arrangement, you see? Between your mother and me.

speaker: Jennifer
en: She said you left her. She said you always talked about sailing a boat and making money in the New World.

speaker: Edward
en: I did always want to sail a ship, that's true. But not for a lark. To support us. To take care of her... and you.

speaker: Jennifer
en: Not me. Mother said you didn't know about me. She said you wrote only once a year, and that she never knew where to find you.

speaker: Edward
en: That's all true. And I'm sorry for that. If I had known earlier... I don't know. I might have come home. I hope that I would have.

speaker: Jennifer
en: Well... you were busy. That's what I think.

speaker: Edward
en: I was. But... that wouldn't have mattered.

speaker: Jennifer
en: Can I steer your boat?

speaker: Edward
en: Boat? I see no boat here. Do you?

speaker: Jennifer
en: Ugh. I mean ship, obviously. I don't see the difference anyway.

speaker: Edward
en: Ah! It's a very simple one, Jenny. A ship can carry a boat, but a boat cannot carry a ship.

speaker: Jennifer
en: Why, then everything is a ship, large and small, but for my toy boat. The one I take into the bath with me.

speaker: Edward
en: That's a clever way of seeing it. Is it hard to talk about Caroline, Jenny? About your mother?

speaker: Jennifer
en: Hmmm... no. She passed some years ago. I miss her, but it's all right.

speaker: Edward
en: Was she in pain?

speaker: Jennifer
en: I don't know. I don't think so. She was very happy for quite some time. Then not so happy. I didn't see her much after that. Then she was gone.

speaker: Edward
en: I... I'm sorry. I'm sorry I wasn't there for you.

speaker: Jennifer
en: It's all right. You're here now. And we're on an adventure!

speaker: Edward
en: Only a little one, I hope. I can't handle too many more surprises.

speaker: Jennifer
en: Do you think we'll see a whale?

speaker: Edward
en: Yes. There's a very good chance.

speaker: Jennifer
en: Hm! And what about pirates? Will I see pirates?

speaker: Edward
en: No. There's not much chance of that, I think.

speaker: Jennifer
en: Oh. That's rather sad. I should have liked to have seen one.

speaker: Edward
en: Tell you what, Jenny. As soon as these winds die a little bit, I'll let you steer the Jackdaw. One little trick at the helm before sundown.

speaker: Jennifer
en: Yay!

speaker: Suitor
en: Miss Jennifer Kenway. May I introduce myself...

speaker: Jennifer
en: Jennifer Scott, if you please.

speaker: Suitor
en: I'm sorry. I- I...

speaker: Edward
en: My daughter was raised by her mother, Caroline, until she passed away some years ago. Jenny prefers to use her surname to mine.

speaker: Suitor
en: Ah. Forgive my ignorance.

speaker: Edward
en: I will. She may not.

speaker: Haytham
en: Father, help me!

speaker: Edward
en: This little rascal, however, IS a Kenway. What's wrong, Haytham?

speaker: Haytham
en: I can't see the stage!

speaker: Edward
en: Up we go. How's that?

speaker: Haytham
en: Fine. But won't your arms tire?

speaker: Edward
en: Hey, I'm not so old as that! But if they do, then we shall quit this posh gig and go and meet your mother for some chocolate at . How's that sound?

speaker: Haytham
en: Yes, please!

speaker: Edward
en: Ok. Hush now...

speaker: Haytham
en: Gentlemen. I believe I've found the solution to our problem. Or rather, Odysseus has.

speaker: Thomas
en: Ody-ooh? 'E a new guy?

speaker: Charles
en: The Greek hero, you lobcock.

speaker: Haytham
en: Allow me to explain: We enter Silas' fort under the pretext of kinship. Once inside we spring our trap, free the captives, and kill the slaver.

speaker: Thomas
en: Dodgy, dodgy. I like it.

speaker: Haytham
en: Then let us begin. First we need to find ourselves a convoy...

speaker: Haytham
en: The convoy should be here soon. We'll attack on my signal.

speaker: Charles
en: Understood, sir.

speaker: Haytham
en: If we time this right, we can catch them all unawares...

speaker: Redcoat
en: The hell is this?

speaker: Thomas
en: A thousand pardons, sirs - seems we've 'ad ourselves an unhappy little accident.

speaker: Redcoat
en: Get it sorted - and quickly.

speaker: Thomas
en: Course, m'lord. At once.

speaker: Haytham
en: Charles - you and William will serve as vanguard. Let no man reach us.

speaker: Thomas
en: Wot about me?

speaker: Haytham
en: You and John will follow from a distance and keep watch over us. I'll signal you when I have need of your services.

speaker: Haytham
en: We're here to help you - along with those held inside Southgate Fort.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Free me.

speaker: Haytham
en: Not until we're inside the gate. I can't chance an inspection at the gate going wrong. I'll see you safe. You have my word.

speaker: Haytham
en: Do you know anything of Silas' operation? How many men we might expect? The nature of their defenses?

speaker: Haytham
en: You must be rather important to him if you were given your own escort...

speaker: William
en: Sir - we've enemies ahead. Shall I engage them?

speaker: Haytham
en: No. Let Jonathan and Thomas take care of it.

speaker: William
en: As you wish.

speaker: Haytham
en: I wish you'd trust us... Though I suppose it's only natural for you to be wary. So be it.

speaker: Thomas
en: I'm gonna enjoy this!

speaker: Officer
en: Halt! Identify yourselves! Where is Leftenant Jones? What's the meaning of this?

speaker: Haytham
en: Engage the enemy!

speaker: John
en: Your life is forfeit!

speaker: Thomas
en: You shoulda run, boy!

speaker: Haytham
en: God damned dogs...

speaker: Officer
en: What is it, boy? You - in the cart. I need to inspect your cargo.

speaker: Haytham
en: Let no man reach us!

speaker: Thomas
en: Looks like you're ta meet the reaper!

speaker: Officer
en: Ah-ha! Bringing fresh meat, eh?... Come here, I want to take a look before Silas uses her.

speaker: Haytham
en: On your guard, men!

speaker: Benjamin
en: Of course.

speaker: Charles
en: To arms!

speaker: Charles
en: Only say the word and I'll cut them down.

speaker: Officer
en: One moment there. Are you new? Who's your officer?

speaker: Haytham
en: Engage the enemy!

speaker: John
en: For the Order!

speaker: Thomas
en: Come on, then! Let's see how tough you are. Looks like you're ta meet the reaper!

speaker: Haytham
en: All clear!

speaker: Redcoat
en: Hold!

speaker: Haytham
en: Evening gentlemen.

speaker: Redcoat
en: State your business.

speaker: Haytham
en: Delivery for Silas.

speaker: Redcoat
en: Go on, then.

speaker: Haytham
en: See? I'm freeing you just as I said I would. Now if you'll allow me to explain

speaker: Haytham
en: Let her go.

speaker: Thomas
en: But she'll give us away.

speaker: Haytham
en: No she won't.

speaker: John
en: What's the plan?

speaker: Haytham
en: Free the captives and avoid detection.

speaker: Benjamin
en: What of Silas?

speaker: Haytham
en: He dies.

speaker: John
en: Signal when you're ready to strike.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Who are you with?

speaker: Benjamin
en: I don't follow.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Leftenant Wilkins?

speaker: Benjamin
en: Uhh, no, no, a man named, uh, Coswell. Leftenant Coswell.

speaker: Guard 2
en: I've not heard of him.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Coswell? Is he the chap with the gammy leg?

speaker: Benjamin
en: That's the one! That's the very man.

speaker: Guard 4
en: Saw at if memory serves. Put down the he did.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Ha, "Leftenant Coswell, hero of Culloden."

speaker: Guard 4
en: Bit of an arse as I recall.

speaker: Guard 2
en: I've never heard of him.

speaker: William
en: Who have we got, then?

speaker: Guard 5
en: What are you talking about?

speaker: William
en: Prisoners. Who are they?

speaker: Guard 5
en: Prisoners? There are no prisoners.

speaker: William
en: You know who I mean. The fellas we caught.

speaker: Guard 5
en: They do not exist. Understood? And, if they did exist, we would not acknowledge them. There are no prisoners.

speaker: William
en: Ah yes, of course. My mistake.

speaker: John
en: Stop slouching, soldier! I said, stop slouching!

speaker: Guard 6
en: Who are you to tell me what to do?

speaker: John
en: A good friend of Mr. Thatcher's.

speaker: Guard 6
en: Oh... I.. I see. My apologies.

speaker: John
en: You take care with your tongue in the future.

speaker: Guard 6
en: Certainly, sir. Upon my honor.

speaker: Charles
en: Greetings. How fares the watch?

speaker: Guard 7
en: Who are you?

speaker: Charles
en: Thomas Smith, newly recruited. Arrived from London just last week in fact.

speaker: Guard 7
en: And you're to patrol with us?

speaker: Charles
en: So said Silas.

speaker: Guard 7
en: Hmm.

speaker: Charles
en: I assume it's all rather straightforward? Watch for disturbances, ensure order is maintained?

speaker: Guard 7
en: Mm-hm.

speaker: Charles
en: Merchandise?

speaker: Guard 7
en: You don't know, you don't need to. Just do as you've been told and stay out of our way.

speaker: Charles
en: Of course. I must say, the weather in Boston is much fairer than back home.

speaker: Guard 8
