en: Wait until winter, and see if you still feel the same.

speaker: Guard 9
en: Or summer for that matter. The heat and wet, it suffocates a man.

speaker: Guard 8
en: And these uniforms. Ha, clearly sewn for the climes. Too thin when it's cold, too heavy when it's hot.

speaker: Charles
en: I assume it's quiet here most days?

speaker: Guard 9
en: Aye, on occasion we'll catch a smuggler trying to ferry contraband into the city. A small fine and stern warning usually sets them right.

speaker: Charles
en: Hmm, a nice change of pace from the campaigning back home.

speaker: Guard 9
en: Why do you think so many of us volunteered? Good pay, safe work, a chance to own some land.

speaker: Guard 8
en: The French would see an end to that.

speaker: Guard 9
en: I don't know. They seem content in the north. Sometimes I wonder if it's not we who provoke with our sorties and expeditions.

speaker: Guard 8
en: Ha! That's exactly what they'd want you to think.

speaker: Charles
en: Such a shame. The colonies are meant to be an opportunity, not another warfront.

speaker: Thomas
en: Oi, fellas. Apologies for me tardiness. Cutter had me working late.

speaker: Guard 10
en: You know Cutter?!

speaker: Thomas
en: Heh, well, who'd ya think got me this post? We're like brothers, me an' 'im. Now, what's it Silas want us doin'? We're here to rough up the prisoners? Relieve them of their finery? I 'ear some of them carry real silver. Wouldn't mind 'elping meself to a bit of it before we send them on their way.

speaker: Guard 10
en: No, keep clear of the merchandise. Don't speak of it either. We watch the gates and patrol the grounds.

speaker: Thomas
en: Understood, boss. I am yours to command.

speaker: Silas
en: An hour of quiet was all I asked. Instead I'm awakened not ten minutes later by this cacophonous madness! I expect an explanation - and it had best be good! How?! How did this happen!? My precious merchandise set free?! It's unacceptable! Rest assured I'll have the heads of those responsible! But first... first we clean up this mess! Seal the fort. Kill any who try to escape. I don't care if they be one of us or one of... them. To approach the gate is to be made a corpse! Am I understood?

speaker: Haytham
en: Push them back!

speaker: William
en: Go on, Haytham! We'll hold back the guards while you deal with Silas! Where did you receive your training? DID you receive any training? This is the best Boston has to offer? No wonder the French still pose a threat... With fighting skills like these, it's little wonder you were set to guard a fort. There's still time for you to flee... though not much.

speaker: Charles
en: No mercy! I'll deal with this, sir! For the Order! Back, rogues! You shall not have us!

speaker: Silas
en: No man passes through the gates! Do you hear me?! NO MAN! To allow a breach of this magnitude! I should kill you all! Kill anyone you do not recognize! Take positions, men! Ready your weapons! Take aim! Fire! Reload! Reload! Again! Where is Cutter?! Find him! Find him now!

speaker: Silas
en: He's here! Stop the interloper! Kill the intruders! All of them! He's the one responsible! Kill him!

speaker: Haytham
en: Benjamin! Glad to have you with us! I could use some help!

speaker: Benjamin
en: The Order stands united! I'll fillet you like a cod! Back! You vile pox! I'll deal with this wretch!

speaker: Silas
en: Who are you?

speaker: Haytham
en: Name's Haytham Kenway. You don't know me. But I believe the two of you are well acquainted...

speaker: Benjamin
en: I made a promise to you, Silas - one I intend to keep.

speaker: Charles
en: What happens now?

speaker: Haytham
en: We wait. Though not for very long, I suspect...

speaker: Catherine
en: You lying, cheating, no-good sonofabitch!

speaker: Haytham
en: Perhaps we've come at a bad time?

speaker: Catherine
en: Oh! Don't be foolish, dearies! Please. Sit. Fancy something to eat? A drink, perhaps? Or is it a bed you require?

speaker: Charles
en: We've already let rooms here.

speaker: Cornelius
en: Oh, yes! Of course! Masters Lee and Kenway, was it? I'll have your bags brought up. Do you require anything further?

speaker: Haytham
en: Only privacy.

speaker: Charles
en: This way.

speaker: Charles
en: Sir, William Johnson.

speaker: William
en: A pleasure. A good lad, if a bit earnest. I'm told you're putting together an expedition.

speaker: Haytham
en: We believe there's a precursor site in the region. I require your knowledge of the land and its people to find it.

speaker: William
en: Sadly, my research has been stolen. Without it, I'm of no use to you.

speaker: Haytham
en: Then we'll find it. Do you have any leads?

speaker: William
en: My associate, Thomas Hickey, has been making the rounds. He's quite good at loosening tongues.

speaker: Haytham
en: Well tell me where I can find him. I'll see if I can't speed things up.

speaker: William
en: We've heard rumors of bandits operating from a compound southwest of here. You'll likely find him there.

speaker: Haytham
en: Charles.

speaker: Charles
en: Sir?

speaker: Haytham
en: We'd best be off.

speaker: Charles
en: Of course.

speaker: Haytham
en: Thomas Hickey?

speaker: Thomas
en: Who's askin'?

speaker: Haytham
en: Haytham Kenway.

speaker: Thomas
en: Is that s'pposed to mean somethin'?

speaker: Charles
en: Show some respect, boy.

speaker: Haytham
en: Peace, Charles. William Johnson sent us in the hopes we might... expedite your search.

speaker: Thomas
en: Don't need no expidittin' - don't need none of your fancy London-speak, neither. I've found the men that done the theft.

speaker: Charles
en: Then why are you just lazing around?

speaker: Thomas
en: Figgerin' out how to deal wit those varlets.

speaker: Haytham
en: I have an idea.

speaker: Thomas
en: Well let's 'ear it.

speaker: Haytham
en: I'll kill the lookout and take up position BEHIND the guards. You two approach from the front. When I open fire on the group, you charge in. We'll have the element of surprise on our side. Half will fall before they've even realized what's happened.

speaker: Haytham
en: Get into position. But WAIT for me to take the first shot.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: You two - clear off!

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: Go on now - 'fore you make us mad.

speaker: Thomas
en: So much for the element of surprise...

speaker: Charles
en: Reinforcements!

speaker: Thomas
en: Oi! 'Aytham! Shoot 'em 'fore they reach us.

speaker: Charles
en: Use those spare muskets and you won't have to reload!

speaker: Mercenary
en: Fall back! Fall back! We'll be safe inside!

speaker: Charles
en: What now?

speaker: Thomas
en: We can blow the door with those. Go on. Shoot 'em.

speaker: Thomas
en: On wit the show, then. Guess they wasn't so safe inside after all... Bet this'll fetch a pretty penny...

speaker: Haytham
en: Save your looting for AFTER we've found Johnson's research.

speaker: Thomas
en: Yes master.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Lay down your weapons and I'll consider letting you live.

speaker: Haytham
en: I make you the same offer. We've no quarrel. I only wish to return this chest to its rightful owner.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Nothing rightful about Mister Johnson.

speaker: Haytham
en: I won't ask again.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Agreed.

speaker: Haytham
en: Your kind has no need for books and maps. Who put you up to this?

speaker: Mercenary
en: Never seen a person. It's always been dead drops and letters. But they always pay, so we do the jobs.

speaker: Haytham
en: Well those days are done. Tell your masters I said as much.

speaker: Mercenary
en: Who should I say you are?

speaker: Haytham
en: You don't. They'll know.

speaker: Thomas
en: Oi! 'Aytham! This one's got some shot on 'im. Ya might want to be grabbin' it on account of your pistol being parched.

speaker: Haytham
en: A shame so many had to die.

speaker: Thomas
en: Aye. Terrible tragedy that.

speaker: Thomas
en: Back to the Green Dragon, then. I need a drink.

speaker: Thomas
en: Careful gents. We've got company.

speaker: Haytham
en: Don't let go of the chest, Charles. We'll take care of this rabble.

speaker: Thomas
en: Look at those badgers! Runnin' around all hubble de shuff!

speaker: Charles
en: A little help, please!

speaker: Thomas
en: Quit yer cryin', I'm comin'!

speaker: Charles
en: Thomas!

speaker: Thomas
en: Wot?

speaker: Charles
en: Over there, that's what! Deal with them!

speaker: Thomas
en: Wait! Them bodies is sure to have loot on 'em. Would be a shame to let it all go to waste.

speaker: Charles
en: Are you mad?! In case you'd forgotten, we're in the midst of something.

speaker: Thomas
en: Aww. Why's you always got ta go an spoil the sport?

speaker: Charles
en: I hope whatever's in this chest is worth it...

speaker: Thomas
en: Come on, now. It's just a few fools with knives...they ain't so tough.

speaker: Charles
en: It's not the scoundrels I'm concerned with...

speaker: Haytham
en: That seems to be the last of them.

speaker: Thomas
en: Oi! Mister Johnson's gonna need to double my pay after all dis if he expects me to keep at 'is side.

speaker: Haytham
en: There you are.

speaker: William
en: My thanks, Master Kenway. Now tell my what it is you need.

speaker: Haytham
en: The images on this amulet - are they familiar to you? Perhaps one of the tribes has shown you something similar?

speaker: William
en: It appears Kanien'kehá:ka in origin.

speaker: Haytham
en: Can you trace it to a specific location? I need to know where it came from.

speaker: William
en: With my research returned, perhaps. Let me see what I can do. Thomas?

speaker: Thomas
en: Wot?

speaker: William
en: Rent yourself a room. And a bath as well... I suspect we'll be here for awhile.

speaker: Haytham
en: Some fresh air might do me good...

speaker: Haytham
en: Have a moment to talk?

speaker: Rupert
en: Ah, a fellow Londoner! Good to see I'm not the only man of means aboard. Rupert Martin, pleased to meet you.

speaker: Haytham
en: Haytham Kenway. Pleasure.

speaker: Rupert
en: Seems we picked an excellent time to leave the city.

speaker: Haytham
en: Oh?

speaker: Rupert
en: You didn't hear about the murder at the opera house?

speaker: Haytham
en: No. What happened?

speaker: Rupert
en: They're still trying to sort it out. And I suspect they'll be at it for a good while.

speaker: Haytham
en: Any word on the motive?

speaker: Rupert
en: They've ruled out robbery. So perhaps it was a business arrangement gone sour. Or something more personal... more lurid. Who knows. But I am glad to be away from it. The city grows more dangerous by the day.

speaker: Haytham
en: Good morning, Doctor.

speaker: Doctor
en: To you as well.

speaker: Haytham
en: A question, if I may. Do you serve aboard the ship? Or are you simply taking passage?

speaker: Doctor
en: A bit of both, actually. I've been commissioned by the Royal Navy to study maritime illness. I'll be observing the crew during the journey. We have found that sailors fare far better on the open seas than the rest of us. I hope to discover why that is.

speaker: Haytham
en: Well, I hope you are successful in your endeavors.

speaker: Doctor
en: As do I. Thank you for the kind words.

speaker: Haytham
en: Captain.

speaker: Smythe
en: Mister Kenway.

speaker: Haytham
en: I just wanted to thank you again for taking me aboard, and apologize for any inconvenience it may have caused.

speaker: Smythe
en: Inconvenience would be an understatement.

speaker: Haytham
en: I'm sorry, I don't follow.

speaker: Smythe
en: My ship was held in port for two days that we might accommodate you. I lost several contracts as a result.

speaker: Haytham
en: I had no idea...

speaker: Smythe
en: Of course not. You nobles are all the same...

speaker: Mills
en: ...and then all will be well.

speaker: Graves
en: You sure 'bout that?

speaker: Mills
en: Of course! Have I ever led you astray?

speaker: Graves
en: Nah... But it don't sit right wit' the others.

speaker: Mills
en: Have faith, my friend. You'll see.

speaker: Graves
en: Well, well. Seems our esteemed guest has deigned grace us wit' 'is presence! You might want to head back to your quarters. Top deck's no place for .

speaker: Haytham
en: So I thought. And yet, here you are.

speaker: Graves
en: Fancy yourself a joker, eh? Let's see how funny you find this.

speaker: Mills
en: That's enough, Graves.

speaker: Graves
en: Stay outta this!

speaker: Quill
en: Listen ta this, Hector—thinks he can swagger on up 'ere and declare himself king 'o the castle.

speaker: Mills
en: Please fellas—call this off. If the captain sees us

speaker: Quill
en: Ta hell with the captain! And ta hell with you, Mills! Whose side you on, anyway?

speaker: Graves
en: I'm ready to go again if you are.

speaker: Haytham
en: This is unwise.

speaker: Graves
en: Why's that? Ya think I'm afraid of ya?

speaker: Haytham
en: No. But you should be.

speaker: Haytham
en: Do you yield?

speaker: Graves
en: Never.

speaker: Graves
en: How do you like these odds?

speaker: Smythe
en: What's the meaning of this?

speaker: Haytham
en: Captain.

speaker: Smythe
en: Explain yourself at once, Mister Kenway!

speaker: Haytham
en: These fou

speaker: Mills
en: We were simply passing the time with a bit of sport, Captain.

speaker: Smythe
en: How about you pass the time by doing your god-damned jobs instead?! I wasn't aware I was paying you to loll about! A word, please—Mister Kenway?

speaker: Haytham
en: Oh, I nearly forgot.

speaker: Haytham
en: There's your knife back.

speaker: Smythe
en: I don't care for you, Mister Kenway. I've had nothing but trouble since you came aboard.

speaker: Haytham
en: Your problems have nothing to do with me.

speaker: Smythe
en: I beg your pardon?!

speaker: Haytham
en: You're a poor leader, ill-tempered and cruel. And it's clear your crew has no respect for you.

speaker: Smythe
en: Look—I don't want to argue. In fact, I need a favor...

speaker: Haytham
en: Oh? This is rich...

speaker: Smythe
en: I suspect some of the men intend to mutiny.

speaker: Haytham
en: Really, what a surprise.

speaker: Smythe
en: As I cannot trust any of them, I am compelled to turn to you.

speaker: Haytham
en: And why should I help you?

speaker: Smythe
en: Because if they do intend to betray, I'm the only hope you have of reaching America alive. Well? What will it be?

speaker: Haytham
en: If what you say is true, what other choice do I have?

speaker: Smythe
en: Thank y

speaker: Haytham
en: But let me be clear, should you ever dare to insult or threaten me again, I'll not hesitate to cut off your head myself. Are we understood? Excellent! Good day.

speaker: Helmsman
en: Hello, sir.

speaker: Haytham
en: Do you expect we'll have a pleasant crossing?

speaker: Helmsman
en: It is a quiet time of year—though rogue storms and troubled waters are not unheard of. But no need to fret. At worst they'll prove an inconvenience. I'm more concerned about pirates and rogue privateers.

speaker: Haytham
en: Have you encountered them before?

speaker: Helmsman
en: Aye. But the Providence is a strong ship—and her crew well trained. They will surely keep us safe.

speaker: Smythe
en: Mister Kenway.

speaker: Haytham
en: Captain.

speaker: Smythe
en: Whatever they're up to—I believe it's coming to a head.

speaker: Haytham
en: Then I'd best get to work.

speaker: Sailor 1
en: He's cut our rations again. Claims we're not "provisioned" for such luxuries.

speaker: Sailor 2
en: It's not right that he should feast on lamb and wine, whilst we're stuck with tinned fish and ...

speaker: Sailor 1
en: Someone needs to have words with him...

speaker: Sailor 2
en: Mills tried. Captain turned him away.

speaker: Sailor 1
en: Then he must try again, with more force, if need be!

speaker: Sailor 3
en: He's a shifty fella. Won't hardly take his hat off! Keeps his face hidden too, so we he can't see him watching

speaker: Sailor 4
en: Quiet! Here he comes. Make like you're working!

speaker: Sailor 5
en: You're not having second thoughts, are you?

speaker: Sailor 6
en: I know it needs to be done, but...

speaker: Sailor 5
en: But what?

speaker: Sailor 6
en: I have a wife and two daughters. What if it goes wrong?

speaker: Sailor 5
en: There's no one aboard doesn't agree with us. The longer we wait, the longer we go without.

speaker: Graves
en: You lookin' for another fight, that it? Go away.

speaker: Quill
en: I ain't got nothing to say to you.

speaker: Mills
en: Quite the basting you gave Graves and Quill.

speaker: Haytham
en: Wasn't by choice.

speaker: Mills
en: Aye. Blockheads, the both of them. Where are my manners. Louis Mills. Pleased to meet you.

speaker: Haytham
en: Haytham Kenway. So, should I be watching my back?

speaker: Mills
en: I think the boys learned their lesson. They're normally not so nasty. Honest, it's just the past few crossings have been a bit... rough.

speaker: Haytham
en: Oh?

speaker: Mills
en: Captain's trying to cut costs. Reduced rations, lower wages, more dangerous cargo... It's put the crew on edge.

speaker: Haytham
en: Is there cause for concern, then?

speaker: Mills
en: Not if I can help it. But the Captain needs to think about the way he treats his men...

speaker: Haytham
en: You there. I have some questions for you.

speaker: Sailor 5
en: That's nice. But I ain't got time to gossip. Probably wouldn't have anything useful to share anyway. You want information? Try the cook—or the doctor—everyone's always chatting them up.

speaker: Haytham
en: A word, doctor. If you have a moment.

speaker: Doctor
en: Why, have you taken ill?

speaker: Haytham
en: No, nothing like that. I was wondering if you had heard any rumblings of trouble on board.

speaker: Doctor
en: What sort of trouble?

speaker: Haytham
en: Unusual complaints or grievances. Men taking issue with the Captain or his

speaker: Doctor
en: You sound just like James. Like I've told him, I've been much too busy with my research to hear anything not work-related.

speaker: Haytham
en: And where might I find James?

speaker: Doctor
en: The galley's your best bet. Now, if you'll excuse me...

speaker: Cook
en: Won't be serving for another couple hours. Some biscuits in the barrel if you're desperate.

speaker: Haytham
en: Actually I've come with a question.

speaker: Cook
en: What's that?

speaker: Haytham
en: Have any of the men been acting strange recently? Said anything that struck you as out of the ordinary?

speaker: Cook
en: The boys cry about the rations, as if there's anything I can do about it. But beyond that I ain't heard much. My advice? Go find James. His ears are always open.

speaker: Haytham
en: And where might I find him?

speaker: Cook
en: Right behind you, actually. He's the one sitting on the barrel.

speaker: Haytham
en: Are you James?

speaker: James
en: Aye.

speaker: Haytham
en: Haytham Kenway. Pleased to meet you.

speaker: James
en: I know who you are.

speaker: Haytham
en: I was hoping you could answer some questions.

speaker: James
en: I figured as much... But not here. Follow me.

speaker: James
en: So what do you want to know?

speaker: Haytham
en: Have you seen or heard anything out of the ordinary since we left port? Anything that gives cause for concern?

speaker: James
en: Some of the men have been gathering at night on the upper deck. I've only caught bits of their conversations—so I couldn't say for certain what they're up to. But I suspect it bodes ill...

speaker: Haytham
en: Is it a mutiny they're planning?

speaker: James
en: All I know is they've little love for the captain. Mills has been trying to talk 'em down, but... there's only so much one man can do.

speaker: Haytham
en: Thank you for the information.

speaker: James
en: I only wish to see us reach the colonies alive.

speaker: Smythe
en: You must expose whatever they're plotting.

speaker: Haytham
en: Your crew is a tight-lipped bunch, but I'll see what I can do...

speaker: Smythe
en: Well, hurry up!

speaker: Helmsman
en: Evening, sir.

speaker: Haytham
en: How are things?

speaker: Helmsman
en: Calm and quiet—just the way I like it. What brings you topside?

speaker: Haytham
en: Thought I'd wander a bit. Stretch my legs. That's all.

speaker: Helmsman
en: Take care where you tread. The deck hides all manner of danger in the dark...

speaker: Haytham
en: What was that? Someone's throwing cargo overboard... But why?

speaker: Haytham
en: Curious. Most curious.

speaker: Smythe
en: Any news?

speaker: Haytham
en: Each night it's the same. I scout one area and they drop the painted barrels from another. I'm going to need to recruit an extra pair of eyes. Maybe James or Mills.

speaker: Smythe
en: Why are they doing this?

speaker: Haytham
en: Near as I can tell, the barrels serve as markers. They're leaving a trail. I fear it is only a matter of time before whoever's following it

speaker: Lookout
en: Ship sighted aft! She's making ready to fire!

speaker: Smythe
en: Beat to quarters, men! Ready the

speaker: Smythe
en: Brace! Everybody down!

speaker: Smythe
en: A warning shot. It seems they don't mean to sink us, but board us instead. Man the cannons! Make ready to fight!

speaker: Smythe
en: I want you below decks.

speaker: Haytham
en: Why? Let me help you secure the ship.

speaker: Smythe
en: Do you know how to rig a sail? To load a cannon? To wage war at sea? I didn't think so. Now return to your cabin—or do I need to have you escorted?

speaker: Smythe
en: Secure the hatch!

speaker: Mills
en: Haytham.

speaker: Haytham
en: Have you been topside? A ship's appeared and means to board us. But it's strange... There's no sign of mutiny aboard... It doesn't even make sense.

speaker: Mills
en: Ah, but it does.

speaker: Haytham
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Mills
en: Did you think you could escape from London so easily after what you did at the opera? That we wouldn't notice? That we wouldn't follow?

speaker: Haytham
en: Ahhh... So THAT'S what this is about...

speaker: Mills
en: Surrender and I will see that you are treated with honor.

speaker: Haytham
en: If you wish to treat me with honor, give me a sword.

speaker: Mills
en: Are you sure this is how you want to play it?

speaker: Smythe
en: I told you to stay below decks!

speaker: Haytham
en: I did as you asked, only Mills was there waiting for me. He's the one that drew that ship here. There was no mutiny—only him.

speaker: Smythe
en: What do they want?

speaker: Haytham
en: Me.

speaker: Smythe
en: Then they can have you!

speaker: Haytham
en: Is that so?

speaker: Smythe
en: They'll catch us anyway... There's nothing to be done.

speaker: Haytham
en: I can think of something...

speaker: Smythe
en: You wish us to sail INTO the storm?!

speaker: Haytham
en: It's our only chance.

speaker: Smythe
en: I won't do it.

speaker: Haytham
en: Then I will.

speaker: Smythe
en: Alright, alright.

speaker: Smythe
en: We need those ropes secured! I told you this was madness!

speaker: Haytham
en: Calm yourself. I'll fix your sail for you.

speaker: Smythe
en: We need more speed! Loose the sails! Haytham—you take the foremast. James—the main mast with you!

speaker: James
en: Aye, aye!

speaker: James
en: Hurry! I can't hold on much longer! The rope's too wet, I'm slipping!

speaker: James
en: Thank you! Thank you!

speaker: Smythe
en: Make ready for our arrival, men!

speaker: Haytham
en: Arrival? I see no land... only this interminable fog.

speaker: Smythe
en: The gulls tell us all we need to know. Climb into the crow's nest and you'll see.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Johnson's told me what you intend. As it happens, the man who held me is the same one that you seek. His name is Silas Thatcher.

speaker: Charles
en: That fancy lad is our slaver?

speaker: Benjamin
en: Don't let his velvet tongue deceive you. A crueler and more vicious creature, I've never known.

speaker: Haytham
en: What can you tell me of his operation?

speaker: Benjamin
en: He hosts at least a hundred men, more than half of whom are Redcoats.

speaker: Haytham
en: All this for some slaves?

speaker: Benjamin
en: Hardly. The man's a commander in the King's Troop, in charge of the Southgate Fort.

speaker: Haytham
en: We need to find a way inside... Hmmm... Let me think on it. In the meantime, I'll attend to our final recruit.

speaker: Charles
en: John Pitcairn's our man. I'll take you to him.

speaker: Redcoat
en: State your business.

speaker: Charles
en: New recruit.

speaker: Redcoat
en: More kindling for the pyre, eh? Go on, then.

speaker: Haytham
en: How'd you manage that?

speaker: Charles
en: Did you forget, sir? My commission is with General Braddock—when I'm not attending to you, of course.

speaker: Braddock
en: Pitcairn, you fool! Your acts are treacherous. Give me one good reason I shouldn't kill you right now. Were you planning to announce yourself? Or did you hope my men wouldn't notice your arrival?

speaker: John
en: Sir, if you'll allow me to explain...

speaker: Braddock
en: Oh, by all means. I should like very much to hear this.

speaker: John
en: I have not deserted, sir. I am here under Commander Amherst's orders.

speaker: Braddock
en: Show me a letter bearing his seal and you might be spared the gallows.

speaker: John
en: I have no such thing... The nature of my work, sir... it's...

speaker: Haytham
en: ...It's the sort of thing best not put to paper.

speaker: Braddock
en: Haytham.

speaker: Haytham
en: General Braddock.

speaker: Braddock
en: I suppose I shouldn't be surprised. Wolves often travel in packs.

speaker: Haytham
en: Master Pitcairn won't be here for but a few weeks. I shall return him to his proper post once our work is finished.

speaker: Braddock
en: The Devil's work no doubt. It's bad enough my superiors insisted I grant you use of Charles. But they've said nothing about this traitor. You'll not have him.

speaker: Haytham
en: Edward, listen to reason.

speaker: Braddock
en: We're done here. See these gentlemen out.

speaker: Charles
en: Well that didn't go as I expected.

speaker: Haytham
en: And to think, I used to call him brother...

speaker: Charles
en: What now? They'll chase us off if we try and return.

speaker: Haytham
en: We're done with the camp. And as luck would have it, so are they. Come along.

speaker: Charles
en: What are you planning?

speaker: Haytham
en: To steal Master Pitcairn.

speaker: Charles
en: What?

speaker: Haytham
en: You'll see. Now, when I give the signal, you're to distract Braddock's patrol and lure them into a dead end.

speaker: Braddock
en: Hmmm. Where shall we head next?

speaker: Redcoat
en: Perhaps down Marlborough?

speaker: Braddock
en: No... its residents are too content. Their homes are nice—their days untroubled.

speaker: Redcoat
en: What of Lyn or Ship Street?

speaker: Braddock
en: Yes. Those fresh arrived are often soon in dire straits. They're more likely to seize upon an opportunity to fatten their purses and feed their young.

speaker: Haytham
en: Now!

speaker: Charles
en: Oi! You're thieves and scoundrels one and all! Fie on you and your false war!

speaker: Braddock
en: After him!

speaker: Haytham
en: Unhand him, Edward!

speaker: Braddock
en: You again.

speaker: Haytham
en: Let us go—and John Pitcairn with us.

speaker: Braddock
en: I will not have my authority challenged.

speaker: Haytham
en: Nor I.

speaker: Braddock
en: Put them all in chains.

speaker: Haytham
en: I stay my hand today because you were once my brother—and a better man than this. But should our paths ever cross again, all debts will be forgotten. You're free now, John.

speaker: Braddock
en: Traitor! Go on then! Join them on their fool's errand! And when you find yourself lying broken and dying at the bottom of

speaker: John
en: I assume you've good reason for causing all this madness? What is it you require of me?

speaker: Haytham
en: I'll explain everything on the way...

speaker: Haytham
en: Evening, gentlemen.

speaker: Charles
en: Charming.

speaker: Haytham
en: Oh, peace, Charles! He'll grow on you.

speaker: Thomas
en: Oi, Catherine ya fussock! Git back here! Daddy needs a drink!

speaker: Haytham
en: How fares the search?

speaker: William
en: Maths and maps are not cutting it.

speaker: Haytham
en: What of your local contacts?

speaker: William
en: We'll need to earn their trust before they'll share what they know.

speaker: Thomas
en: I've an idea on how we might be effectin' that. There's a man who's taken to enslavin' natives. Rescue 'em and they'll owe us.

speaker: Haytham
en: Do you know where they're being held?

speaker: Thomas
en: Fraid not.

speaker: Charles
en: Benjamin Church will. He's a finder and a fixer. He's also on your list.

speaker: Haytham
en: And there I was, wondering whom I might solicit next. Well done.

speaker: Haytham
en: Wonderful.

speaker: Haytham
en: Charles!

speaker: Charles
en: Sir?

speaker: Haytham
en: Seems like we're not the only ones looking for Mister Church.

speaker: Charles
en: Dammit! He could be anywhere. What do we do?

speaker: Haytham
en: We find him. Come, I'll show you how.

speaker: Woman
en: Should we write his family, do you think?

speaker: Man
en: Not our business to meddle—even if we've the best of intentions.

speaker: Woman
en: But if you could have seen it! They were surely drunk, carrying on like that. And during the day, no less!

speaker: Man
en: Such scandalous behavior from one who aims to be a surgeon? Not likely if he keeps up such carousing...

speaker: Woman
en: A truly shameful display. Benjamin's parents would be mortified.

speaker: Man
en: Perhaps I should send someone to retrieve him before he damages his reputation beyond repair...

speaker: Woman
en: They stumbled off to the northeast—no doubt in search of a tavern or some other place of ill repute.

speaker: Haytham
en: Start questioning those on the street. I'm headed for higher ground...

speaker: Charles
en: I'm looking for Mr. Church. Mr. Benjamin Church. Excuse me, do you recognize this likeness? Pardon. Do you know this man? I'm terribly sorry, but it's important I find this man. A moment, please. I'm looking for the man that fits this likeness. If I may? I wonder if you recognize the man in this portrait? It's of the utmost importance that I find this man. I beg your pardon—have you seen this fellow?

speaker: Haytham
en: Time to take a listen. With luck, one of those people knows what became of Benjamin.

speaker: Redcoat 1
en: I've asked the criers, but they all plead ignorance.

speaker: Redcoat 2
en: Bugger that! They're lying.

speaker: Redcoat 1
en: Aye. What can I do? Threats slide off them and I'll not deign to grovel.

speaker: Redcoat 2
en: Actions speak louder than words, my friend. Arrest one and put him in stocks. See if he's so glib then.

speaker: Redcoat 1
en: To do so without cause will set them singing songs about us. Last thing the city needs is town criers complaining about our abuse of authority.

speaker: Redcoat 2
en: Then forget it. The crime is done, the killers gone, and those who know won't share their secrets. If the city wishes to harbor scoundrels—let them pay the price for it.

speaker: Redcoat 1
en: ...and so he says to Church, that one way or another the debt would be settled. I don't envy the man. He's grim times ahead.

speaker: Redcoat 2
en: What do you think they're planning?

speaker: Redcoat 1
en: All I know is it can't be good. Cutter was with 'em.

speaker: Redcoat 2
en: Probably looking for a nice quiet place to do the deed. From what I hear tell, his work usually involves quite a bit of screamin'.

speaker: Redcoat 1
en: Which reminds me, we'd best not buy any meat tomorrow.

speaker: Redcoat 2
en: Good call, that.

speaker: Man 1
en: ...I asked if I could help and they waved me away. Insisted it was all under control.

speaker: Man 2
en: How odd. Did they say what had happened?

speaker: Man 1
en: No. Only that it was a trifling matter and he'd be returned home soon. There was some blood, though... So I wonder if it wasn't more serious than they let on.

speaker: Man 2
en: Where were they taking him?

speaker: Man 1
en: Towards the hilltop. Perhaps there's a doctor at the fort.

speaker: Redcoat 3
en: I need you to focus.

speaker: Man 3
en: Easy for you to say! You didn't just watch your friend die!

speaker: Redcoat 3
en: Recall what happened as best you can.

speaker: Man 3
en: There were... three, no, four of them. All of clearly ill repute. They carried a fifth. He was bruised and unconscious. Thomas, the fool, tried to offer aid. So they cut his throat. And then they moved on, as if it were nothing. As if it were normal.

speaker: Redcoat 3
en: Which way did they go?

speaker: Man 3
en: I... I don't know. I was focused on trying to stop the bleeding.

speaker: Redcoat 3
en: Come on now, try and remember.

speaker: Man 3
en: That way... I think.

speaker: Haytham
en: See, Charles? We'll have Church in no time, just as I said we would.

speaker: Charles
en: If I might ask, sir, where did you learn to do all this?

speaker: Haytham
en: It is a requirement when you are raised in the manner that I was. Perception is fundamental to the Order. It guides the feet when running and climbing. Informs the hands when striking and fighting. But most important, it transforms the senses. And we begin to know the world in a different way. Careful. The place is well guarded. We need to slip past them...

speaker: Haytham
en: Locked! Hmmm. I'll have to find the key. Wait here...

speaker: Haytham
en: Here we are, then.

speaker: Silas
en: Why must you always make these things so difficult, Benjamin? Merely provide me with recompense and all shall be forgiven.

speaker: Benjamin
en: I'll not pay for protection I don't need!

speaker: Silas
en: Clearly, you DO require protection, else we wouldn't be here!

speaker: Silas
en: How very gauche. Now, what shall we do about our guest?

speaker: Cutter
en: Maybe I take 'is hands. Put an end to 'is surgerin'. Maybe I take 'is tongue. Put an end to 'is wagglin'. Or maybe I take 'is cock. Put an end to 'is fuckin' us!

speaker: Silas
en: So many options. I can't possibly decide. Take all three.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Now hold a moment. Perhaps I was hasty in refusing you earlier...

speaker: Silas
en: I'm so very sorry, Benjamin, but that door has closed.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Be reasonable, Silas.

speaker: Silas
en: I rather think I was. But you took advantage of my generosity. I won't be made a fool a second time. I fear I lack the constitution to beat witness to such barbarism. Come find me when you're finished, Cutter.

speaker: Benjamin
en: You'll regret this, Silas! Do you hear me? I'll have your head!

speaker: Silas
en: No, I rather think you won't.

speaker: Cutter
en: Just a quick little swipe and no more ears! How's that sound, Mister Church?

speaker: Benjamin
en: At least I'll be spared more of your inane prattle.

speaker: Cutter
en: Maybe you'll get lucky and pass out, though I dare say I'll do me best to ensure that doesn't happen.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Your parents must be so very proud to have raised a specimen like yourself.

speaker: Cutter
en: Quiet now! I need to concentrate on me work. Hold still a minute. I gotta decide where to start. A little bit from here... a little bit from there... Make meself a nice keepsake, I will.

speaker: Benjamin
en: You're absolutely mad.

speaker: Cutter
en: Just like all good artists!

speaker: Benjamin
en: You're a ruffian common as dirt, Cutter.

speaker: Cutter
en: And proud of it!

speaker: Benjamin
en: Who... Who are you?

speaker: Haytham
en: Haytham Kenway, at your service.

speaker: Benjamin
en: I... I don't understand... Why are you here?

speaker: Haytham
en: Walk with me, Mister Church, and all will be explained.

speaker: Haytham
en: It's been several weeks now since we freed the Mohawk prisoners from captivity. I had hoped their leader might make contact, but there's been only silence. My men grow restless. They want to know what comes next, and I do not have an answer. Lee, alone, remains active - pursuing leads, however slight. He stalks the city streets and scouts the bordering woods - hopeful that he might make contact with one of those we saved. There was a woman there, that night. It was she who helped the others to safety. If we could find her, I believe I'll have my answers. So I watch and wait, hopeful that my true mission might finally begin.

speaker: Haytham
en: Hello, Charles. Any luck finding our mystery woman?

speaker: Charles
en: Word is she's been stirring up trouble just outside the city in a town called Lexington.

speaker: Haytham
en: Well then that's where we'll begin our search! I'll meet you there.

speaker: Haytham
en: Have you found her?

speaker: Charles
en: She's made camp not too far from here.

speaker: Haytham
en: Excellent. Well the sooner we're done, the sooner we can get out of this cold.

speaker: Charles
en: We'll move faster on horseback.

speaker: Charles
en: I'm afraid I have some bad news, sir.

speaker: Haytham
en: Oh?

speaker: Charles
en: Braddock is insisting I return to service under him. I've tried to beg off, to no avail.

speaker: Haytham
en: No doubt he's still angry about losing Pitcairn - to say nothing of the shaming we gave him. Do as he asks. In the meantime, I'll work on having you released.

speaker: Charles
en: I am sorry for the trouble.

speaker: Haytham
en: Not your fault.

speaker: Charles
en: We're too late...

speaker: Haytham
en: The fire's only just been snuffed. The snow recently disturbed. She's close.

speaker: Charles
en: Bollocks.

speaker: Haytham
en: These tracks are fresh, they must be hers. Hmmm. Seems she took to higher ground. Out of the snow and into the trees.

speaker: Haytham
en: Wait here.

speaker: Haytham
en: Ah, dammit! Wait! Come back! Best you return to Braddock, Charles, before he grows suspicious. I can handle things from here.

speaker: Charles
en: But, sir

speaker: Haytham
en: But nothing. Go!

speaker: Haytham
en: Stop running! I only wish to talk! I am not your enemy! Please, just hear me out! Gods, woman! Only let me speak! Enough with these games! It is imperative that we speak! A moment of your time is all I ask! You try my patience, woman!

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Are you touched in the head?

speaker: Haytham
en: Me. Haytham. I come in peace.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Why are you speaking so slow?

speaker: Haytham
en: Oh, sorry.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: What do you want?

speaker: Haytham
en: Well, your name for one.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: I am Kaniehtí:io.

speaker: Haytham
en: Pleased to meet you, godz-zio?

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Just call me Ziio.

speaker: Haytham
en: Diio?

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Ziio.

speaker: Haytham
en: Ziio.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Now tell me why it is you're here.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Where did you get this?

speaker: Haytham
en: From an old friend.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: I've only seen such markings in one other place.

speaker: Haytham
en: Where?

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Well, it is forbidden for me to speak of it.

speaker: Haytham
en: I saved your people. Does this mean nothing to you? Look. I am not the enemy.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Close to here is a hill. Meet me there, and we'll see if you speak the truth.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: That town hosts soldiers who seek to drive my people from these lands. They're led by a man known as the Bulldog.

speaker: Haytham
en: Edward Braddock...

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: You know him?

speaker: Haytham
en: He is no friend of mine.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Every day more of my people are lost to men like him.

speaker: Haytham
en: Then I suggest we put a stop to it. Together.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: What do you propose?

speaker: Haytham
en: That we kill Edward Braddock. But first we have to find him.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: I don't trust you.

speaker: Haytham
en: I know.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Yet you remain.

speaker: Haytham
en: That I might prove you wrong.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: It will not happen.

speaker: Haytham
en: So you say.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: So I know.

speaker: Haytham
en: Yet I remain. Wait here. A Mohawk woman is likely to raise suspicions - if not muskets.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: This is hardly the first time I've been amongst your people. I can handle myself.

speaker: Haytham
en: I hope so...

speaker: Redcoat
en: ... can't stand being quartered there. The endless crashing of the waves. The sting of the salt in my eyes. And the goddammed gulls shrieking and shitting everywhere.

speaker: Soldier
en: You're sure that's where we're goin'?

speaker: Redcoat
en: Aye. The Bulldog's putting together another "expedition".

speaker: Soldier
en: That what they're callin' 'em now? Expeditions?

speaker: Redcoat
en: Aye. Smart too. Slap a fancy name on something and all evil is excused.

speaker: Redcoat
en: I hear the French are readying to move on our positions. Wonder what Braddock intends to do about it.

speaker: Soldier
en: He's already left for the advance camp. I'd wager our little holiday here is just about ended. We'll be marching south before week's end.

speaker: Man
en: Oi, where you goin', cully?

speaker: Haytham
en: Me?

speaker: Man
en: No. The other cock robin.

speaker: Haytham
en: Well, I uh... I WAS leaving.

speaker: Man
en: Oh? And now?

speaker: Haytham
en: Well, now... I'm going to feed you your teeth.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: And you were worried I was going to be the problem.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: You are hurt.

speaker: Haytham
en: Uch, it's nothing.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: Here... This should stop the bleeding.

speaker: Haytham
en: That wasn't necessary. But thank you.

speaker: Kaniehtí:io
en: We should move on. Meet me at Braddock's camp when you're ready.

speaker: Charles
en: Master Kenway! Master Kenway!

speaker: Haytham
en: Yes? May I help you?

speaker: Charles
en: Charles Lee, sir. A pleasure to make your acquaintance. I've been asked to introduce you to the city. Help you settle in.

speaker: Charles
en: Oh no need sir. I've arranged for your bags to be delivered to the Inn.

speaker: Haytham
en: Are you by any chance John and Isabella's son?

speaker: Charles
en: One and the same.

speaker: Haytham
en: Your commission is with Edward Braddock, is it not?

speaker: Charles
en: Aye. But he's yet to reach America and I figured I might... Well... At least until he arrives... I thought...

speaker: Haytham
en: Yes. Out with it.

speaker: Charles
en: Forgive me, sir. I had... I had hoped that I might study under you. If I am to serve the Order I can imagine no better mentor than yourself.

speaker: Haytham
en: Kind of you to say, but I think you overestimate me.

speaker: Charles
en: Impossible, sir. This way.

speaker: Woman
en: Thief! Someone stop him!

speaker: Haytham
en: Boston's quite a lively city.

speaker: Charles
en: There's all manner of things to see and do. Once you've settled in, I suggest you take some time to walk the streets. Who knows what opportunities you might discover...

speaker: Haytham
en: Hold a moment. I need to fetch a few things before we get to work.

speaker: Charles
en: I'll arrange for horses while you do that.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Get back here with that, you rogue! Damned sprigs! This accursed city will be the death of me...

speaker: Haytham
en: You seem troubled, friend.

speaker: Benjamin
en: That's because I am. Greatly so, in fact.

speaker: Haytham
en: What's happened?

speaker: Benjamin
en: I was robbed. The old bulk and file... And though I've managed to restore what's mine, I fear it's ruined.

speaker: Haytham
en: You mean, the book?

speaker: Benjamin
en: This is no ordinary book! It's an Almanac. The first I ever wrote. Benjamin Franklin. Pleased to meet you.

speaker: Haytham
en: Haytham Kenway.

speaker: Benjamin
en: You must be new to Boston.

speaker: Haytham
en: Why do you say that?

speaker: Benjamin
en: You're still possessed of virtue. To stop and help an old lout like myself... I... I don't mean to impose, but... you seem a spry fellow. Should you happen to find my missing pages, I'll reward you.

speaker: Haytham
en: Look, I'm not sure if I...

speaker: Benjamin
en: It's alright, alright. If you have the time, hurrah. If not—no harm done. The thing is useless in its current state anyway. But should you somehow restore it, you'll find me inside that general store over there.

speaker: Haytham
en: Well that was interesting.

speaker: Charles
en: We ride for the Green Dragon Tavern. The proprietors are... eccentric, but the rooms are spacious and they do not pry.

speaker: Haytham
en: Have you been told why it is I've come to Boston?

speaker: Charles
en: No. Master Birch said I should know only as much as you saw fit to share. He sent me a list of names and bade me ensure you could find them.

speaker: Haytham
en: And have you had any luck with that?

speaker: Charles
en: Aye. William Johnson waits for us at the Green Dragon.

speaker: Haytham
en: How well do you know him?

speaker: Charles
